# jQuery plugins and Angular 2

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/jquery-plugins-and-angular.md

# jQuery plugins and Angular 2

> Using the jQuery UI DatePicker in an Angular 2 application.

Checkout [Radzen Demos](/demos) and [download latest Radzen](/download)!

> Updated on October 26, 2017 to fix the plunkr demos and update them to Angular 4.

In this blog post I will show you how to use a jQuery plugin in an Angular 4 app. The plugin is the popular jQuery UI DatePicker.

Native date inputs are not widely available even though it is 2016. The HTML5 standard includes `<input type="date">` and `<input type="datetime-local">` but FireFox, desktop Safari and
Internet Explorer do not support them at the time of this writing. jQuery UI DatePicker comes to the rescue!

## JavaScript and CSS files

Before using a jQuery plugin we must include its dependencies in our page.
We include jQuery, the JavaScript implementation and the CSS files that provide the visual theme.

```html
<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.1.1.slim.min.js"></script>
<script src="https://code.jquery.com/ui/1.12.1/jquery-ui.min.js"></script>
<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://code.jquery.com/ui/1.11.4/themes/ui-darkness/jquery-ui.css">

```

## DatePicker component

We are ready to implement the Angular component.

```ts
import { ViewChild, ElementRef, AfterViewInit, Component } from '@angular/core';

declare var jQuery: any;

@Component({
  selector: 'my-datepicker',
  template: `<input #input type="text">`
})
export class DatePickerComponent implements AfterViewInit {
  @ViewChild('input') input: ElementRef;

  ngAfterViewInit() {
    jQuery(this.input.nativeElement).datepicker();
  }
}

```

You can try it live in this [plunkr](https://plnkr.co/edit/zsDxjEA5ZB0LPuNjw1vj?p=preview) demo.

Let's explain the code so far.

* First we declare jQuery as an ambient variable because it doesn't come from a TypeScript file.
This is a simpler way to use jQuery from TypeScript. In production apps you should prefer TypeScript definition files.
* The template of our component contains an `input` element because this is what the jQuery UI DatePicker initializes from.
* We need a reference to the DOM node which represents that input. The `ViewChild` attribute maps an element from the template
to a property of the component.
* The `ElementRef` type is a DOM node wrapper. Angular wraps DOM nodes in order to support server-side
rendering or non-browser platforms such as NativeScript. On those platforms the DOM is not available.
* Finally we implement the `ngAfterViewInit` lifecycle method because at this point all ViewChild properties are ready to use.
Accessing the `input` property earlier will cause an error.

## Input and Output Properties

While the component itself works it is not very useful yet. There is no way to set its value or get notified
when the user picks a date. Let's fix that.

```ts
import { Input, Output, EventEmitter, ViewChild, ElementRef, AfterViewInit, Component } from '@angular/core';

declare var jQuery: any;

@Component({
  selector: 'my-datepicker',
  template: `<input #input type="text">`
})
export class DatePickerComponent implements AfterViewInit {
  @Input() value = '';
  @Output() dateChange = new EventEmitter();

  @ViewChild('input') input: ElementRef;

  ngAfterViewInit() {
    jQuery(this.input.nativeElement).datepicker({
      onSelect: (value) => {
        this.value = value;

        this.dateChange.next(value);
      }
    })
    .datepicker('setDate', this.value);
  }
}

```

Our component has a `value` property that allows us to set the current date from code. It also emits a `dateChange` event when the user
selects a date.

Here how to use the new property and event ([plunkr](https://plnkr.co/edit/vjHMpQwutZD2iE3ayvf8?p=preview)):

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'my-app',
  template: `
    <div>
     <my-datepicker [value]="date" (dateChange)="onDateChange($event)"></my-datepicker>
     <div>Date: {{ date }}</div>
    </div>
  `,
})
export class AppComponent {
  date = "11/13/2016";

  onDateChange(date) {
    this.date = date;
  }
}

```

## Form support

Still something is off. Our component does not support forms. We should implement the `ControlValueAccessor`
interface to fix that.

```ts
import { forwardRef, Input, Output, EventEmitter, ViewChild, ElementRef, AfterViewInit, Component } from '@angular/core';
import { ControlValueAccessor, NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR } from "@angular/forms";

const DATE_PICKER_VALUE_ACCESSOR = {
  provide: NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR,
  useExisting: forwardRef(() => DatePickerComponent),
  multi: true
};

declare var jQuery: any;

@Component({
  selector: 'my-datepicker',
  template: `<input #input type="text">`,
  providers: [DATE_PICKER_VALUE_ACCESSOR]
})
export class DatePickerComponent implements AfterViewInit, ControlValueAccessor {
  private onTouched = () => { };
  private onChange: (value: string) => void = () => { };

  @Input() value = '';

  writeValue(date: string) {
    this.value = date;

    jQuery(this.input.nativeElement).datepicker('setDate', date);
  }

  registerOnChange(fn: any) {
    this.onChange = fn;
  }

  registerOnTouched(fn: any) {
    this.onTouched = fn;
  }

  @Output() dateChange = new EventEmitter();

  @ViewChild('input') input: ElementRef;

  ngAfterViewInit() {
    jQuery(this.input.nativeElement).datepicker({
      onSelect: (value) => {
        this.value = value;

        this.onChange(value);

        this.onTouched();

        this.dateChange.next(value);
      }
    })
    .datepicker('setDate', this.value);
  }
}

```

We register a new provider to tell Angular that our DatePicker component implements the `ControlValueAccessor` methods.

The DatePicker implements a few new methods: writeValue, registerOnChange and registerOnTouched.
 * Angular calls `writeValue` to sync a component with its value. In our case we set the jQuery UI DatePicker date.
 * The `registerOnChange` method registers a callback which tells Angular that the component value changed.
 * The `registerOnTouched` method registers a callback which tells Angular that the user interacted with the component.

We invoke the `onChange` and `onTouched` callbacks whenever the user selects a new date.

Here is a sample form that uses the DatePicker component ([plunkr](https://plnkr.co/edit/wU1OZsvdnlx66AiOv954?p=preview)).

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'my-app',
  template: `
    <form>
     <my-datepicker name="date" [(ngModel)]="form.date"></my-datepicker>
     <div>form: {{ form | json }}</div>
    </form>
  `,
})
export class AppComponentComponent {
  form = {
    date: "11/13/2016"
  };
}

```

## Setting DatePicker options

The jQuery UI DatePicker has a lot of configuration options. Let's support all of them by implementing a new `Input` property.

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'my-datepicker',
  template: `<input #input type="text">`
})
export class DatePickerComponent implements AfterViewInit, ControlValueAccessor, OnDestroy {
  @Input() options: any = {};

  /* snip */

  ngAfterViewInit() {
    jQuery(this.input.nativeElement).datepicker(Object.assign({}, this.options, {
      onSelect: (value) => {
        this.value = value;

        this.onChange(value);

        this.onTouched();

        this.dateChange.next(value);
      }
    }))
    .datepicker('setDate', this.value);
  }
}

```

We created a new `options` property and pass it to the jQuery UI DatePicker plugin. This allows us to pass configuration options
like this ([plunkr](https://plnkr.co/edit/ClFD01jZUoHeDkDk6Rg6?p=preview)):

```html
<my-datepicker [options]="{numberOfMonths: 2}"></my-datepicker>

```

## Cleanup

There is one remaining thing. We should cleanup the resources claimed by the jQuery UI DatePicker to avoid memory leaks. The
`ngOnDestroy` method is the perfect place to do that.

```ts
@Component({
  selector: 'my-datepicker',
  template: `<input #input type="text">`
})
export class DatePickerComponent implements AfterViewInit, ControlValueAccessor, OnDestroy {
  /* snip */

  ngOnDestroy() {
    jQuery(this.input.nativeElement).datepicker('destroy');
  }
}

```

Our component is now ready to use. It supports validation, two-way data-binding, reactive forms and
benefits from all the features provided by the jQuery UI DatePicker.

Until next time!

---

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/looking-ahead-whats-coming-in-2026.md

# Looking Ahead: What’s Coming in 2026

> This year, we’re doubling down on three things. Developer experience. Productivity. Design. From AI-powered tooling and new premium themes to powerful new components and templates, 2026 is all about helping teams build better apps, faster.

As we step into 2026, we’re excited to share a preview of what we’ve been working on and what you can expect throughout the year. 
Our focus remains the same: helping you build beautiful, powerful, and productive business applications faster than ever.

All of the features outlined below are planned as part of our [Subscription offering](https://www.radzen.com/pricing), designed for teams and developers who want advanced capabilities, polished UI, and maximum productivity.

## AI Agent in Radzen Blazor Studio

<img src="images/blog/radzen-ai-agent.png" alt="AI Agent in Radzen Blazor Studio" style="border-radius: 12px; max-width: 70%;" loading="lazy" />

AI is becoming an essential productivity tool, and Radzen is embracing it fully. In 2026, we’re introducing an AI agent directly inside Radzen Blazor Studio, designed to:

- Assist with component selection and configuration
- Help generate and refine UI layouts
- Speed up common development workflows
- Provide contextual guidance while you build

Our goal is to make app creation more intuitive and dramatically faster, especially for complex scenarios.

## New Premium Themes

Design continues to be a major area of investment for us in 2026. This year, we’re expanding our Material-based theme lineup with two new premium options that serve distinct needs: Material 3 Expressive and Zen.

### Material 3 Expressive

Material 3 Expressive builds on the foundation of Material 3 with richer motion, bolder color, and stronger visual personality. It’s designed for applications that want to stand out - whether customer-facing products, branded experiences, or apps that benefit from a more dynamic and engaging interface.

<img src="images/blog/radzen-material3-expressive.png" alt="Material 3 Expressive premium theme" style="border-radius: 12px;" loading="lazy" />

With enhanced motion patterns, expanded color usage, and expressive visual hierarchy, this theme brings greater energy while staying aligned with accessibility and usability best practices.

### Zen theme

Zen takes a different approach.

Built on Material 3 foundations, Zen is a premium, minimalist theme focused on clarity and restraint. It limits color to functional meaning and introduces subtle translucent layers to create depth without distraction. The result is a calm, focused interface especially well suited for data-rich, enterprise, and long-running applications.

<img src="images/blog/radzen-zen-theme.jpg" alt="Zen premium theme" style="border-radius: 12px;" loading="lazy" />

Where Material 3 Expressive emphasizes personality, Zen emphasizes balance - giving teams a refined, modern aesthetic that prioritizes readability and sustained usability.

Together, these additions expand the Material family to support a broader range of product styles - from bold and expressive to calm and minimal - while maintaining a consistent, reliable foundation.

## New Components

<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-spider-chart.png" alt="Radzen Blazor Spider Chart" style="border-radius: 12px; max-width: 70%;" loading="lazy" />

We’re expanding the Radzen component library with powerful new additions:

- **[Spider (Radar) Chart](https://blazor.radzen.com/spider-chart)** - Ideal for multi-dimensional data comparisons
- **Gantt Chart** - Perfect for project planning, timelines, and resource tracking
- **Spreadsheet component** - A flexible, Excel-like experience for data-heavy applications

## App Templates Expanding Throughout 2026

<img src="images/blazor-template-healthcare.jpg" alt="Healthcare Blazor Template" style="border-radius: 12px;" loading="lazy" />

In 2026, we’ll continue to introduce new [app templates](https://blazor.radzen.com/templates-healthcare) to help you move from idea to working application even faster. These templates are designed around real-world use cases and provide strong starting points for public-facing and internal applications alike, while remaining fully customizable.

## UI Blocks for Faster Front-End Development

<div style="margin-block: 40px;">
    <YouTube Video="ZM3XGYdpUcA" />
</div>

We’ll continue to expand our collection of [UI Blocks](https://blazor.radzen.com/ui-blocks-cta) in 2026 - reusable, pre-designed sections that help you assemble polished interfaces in minutes. Planned UI blocks include Social Share, Hero Sections, Product Lists, Product Overviews, Shopping Cart, Content Cards, and more.

## Looking Forward

2026 is shaping up to be one of our most ambitious years yet. Cutting-edge themes and AI-powered tooling, powerful new components and templates, everything we’re building is focused on one thing: helping you deliver better applications, faster.

Thank you for being part of the Radzen community. We can’t wait to share more as these features roll out.

# Manage your OneDrive using Radzen, MSGraph and Azure AD - Part I

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/manage-one-drive-with-ms-graph-part1.md

# Manage your OneDrive using Radzen, MSGraph and Azure AD - Part I

> Access OneDrive using MSGraph API and Azure AD authentication

This blog post demonstrates how to build with Radzen an Angular app that will access [Microsoft OneDrive](https://onedrive.live.com) using [Microsoft Graph API](https://graph.microsoft.io) and [Azure Active Directory](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/active-directory-whatis) authentication!

## Creating the app and MSGraph data-source

Create a new Radzen application, add MSGraph data-source similar to [our](documentation/ms-graph) article and add `Files.Read` scopes/permissions.

![image](images/blog/ms-graph-datasource.png)

## Creating a page with Tree and DataGrid to browse OneDrive files and folders

1. Create new page named __OneDrive__, drag and drop a __Row__ and two __Column__ component from Radzen toolbox. Set 3 and 9 for the size of first and second column.
![image](images/blog/ms-graph-page1.png)
1. Call __MSGraph__ data-source `getDrives()` method on page __Load__ event and define two page properties `getDrivesResult` for the returned data and `drive` for the first drive in the collection.
![image](images/blog/ms-graph-page2.png)
1. After `getDrives()` call invoke __MSGraph__ data-source `getDrivesRoot()` method with `${drive.id}` as parameter and define page property `rootId` to `${result.id}`.
![image](images/blog/ms-graph-page3.png)
1. Drag and drop __Tree__ component from Radzen toolbox to the first column, bind it to `getDrivesResult` page property and define two levels using `microsoft.graph.drive` and `microsoft.graph.driveItem` schemas. Set `owner.user.displayName` for the first level __Text__ property and `name` for the second level __Text__ property.
![image](images/blog/ms-graph-page4.png)
1. Call __MSGraph__ data-source `getDrivesItemsChildren()` method on __Tree__ component __NodeExpand__ event with three parameters:
- id = `${drive.id}`.
- driveItemId = `${event.level == 0 ? this.rootId : event.data.id}`. Provide `rootId` or current node/item `id` depending on `level`.
- $filter = `file eq null`. Filter drive items to return only folders.
Execute `${event.children = result.value}` after `getDrivesItemsChildren()` method call.
![image](images/blog/ms-graph-page5.png)
1. Add new event handler to the __Tree__ component __NodeLoaded__ event and execute `${event.leaf = event.data.folder ? event.data.folder.childCount == 0 : false}`. The tree node will not be expandable if there are no children.
![image](images/blog/ms-graph-page6.png)
1. Add new event handler to the __Tree__ component __NodeSelect__ event, define `selectedFolderId` page property with value `${event.level == 0 ? this.rootId : event.data.id}`, invoke `getDrivesItemsChildren()` method with two parameters:
- id = `${drive.id}`.
- driveItemId = `${event.level == 0 ? this.rootId : event.data.id}`.
and set page property `selectedItemChildren` to `${result.value}`.
![image](images/blog/ms-graph-page7.png)
1. Drag and drop __DataGrid__ component from Radzen toolbox to the second column, bind it to `selectedItemChildren` and define desired columns. Check `AllowSorting` and `AllowFiltering`.
![image](images/blog/ms-graph-page8.png)
1. Run the application, login using your Microsoft credentials and browse your OneDrive files and folders.
![image](images/blog/ms-graph-page9.png)

Enjoy!

---

# Manage your OneDrive using Radzen, MSGraph and Azure AD - Part II

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/manage-one-drive-with-ms-graph-part2.md

# Manage your OneDrive using Radzen, MSGraph and Azure AD - Part II

> Create new, rename and delete OneDrive items using MSGraph API and Azure AD authentication

This blog post demonstrates how to build an Angular app that will create new, rename and delete [Microsoft OneDrive](https://onedrive.live.com) items using [Microsoft Graph API](https://graph.microsoft.io) and [Azure Active Directory](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/active-directory/active-directory-whatis) authentication! To know more about how to setup your Radzen application please check [Manage your OneDrive using Radzen, MSGraph and Azure AD - Part I](/blog/manage-one-drive-with-ms-graph-part1).

## Creating pages for add new, edit/update and delete OneDrive files and folders

1. Create new page named __EditDriveItem__, call __MSGraph__ data-source `getDrivesItemsById()` method on page __Load__ event with two parameters:
- id = `${parameters.driveId}`.
- driveItemId = `${parameters.itemId}`.
and set page property `driveItem` to `${result}`.
![image](images/blog/ms-graph-edit-drive-item.png)
1. Drag and drop __Form__ component from Radzen toolbox, bind it to `driveItem` and define single field bound to `Name` property.
![image](images/blog/ms-graph-edit-drive-item-form.png)
1. Call __MSGraph__ data-source `updateDrivesItems()` method on __Form__ component __Submit__ event with three parameters:
- id = `${parameters.driveId}`.
- driveItemId = `${parameters.itemId}`.
- driveItem = `${event}`.
![image](images/blog/ms-graph-edit-drive-item-form-update.png)
Call __Navigate Back__ on __Form__ component __Cancel__ event.
1. Select page __OneDrive__, add new event handler to the __DataGrid__ component __RowSelect__ event and execute __Navigate to page__ __EditDriveItem__ with two parameters:
- driveId = `${drive.id}`.
- itemId = `${parameters.itemId}`.
![image](images/blog/ms-graph-edit-drive-item-select.png)
1. Create new page named __AddDriveItem__, drag and drop __Form__ component from Radzen toolbox, and define single field bound to `Name` property. Set __SubmitText__ to `Add new folder`.
![image](images/blog/ms-graph-add-drive-item.png)
1. Add __Form__ component __Submit__ event handler, execute code `${event.folder = {}}` and invoke __MSGraph__ data-source method `createDrivesItemsChildren()` method with three parameters:
- id = `${parameters.driveId}`.
- driveItemId = `${parameters.itemId}`.
- driveItem = `${event}`.
![image](images/blog/ms-graph-add-drive-item-submit.png)
Call __Navigate Back__ on __Form__ component __Cancel__ event.
1. Select page __OneDrive__, set __AllowAdd__ to __True__ for the __DataGrid__ component and execute __Navigate to page__ __AddDriveItem__ with two parameters:
- driveId = `${drive.id}`.
- folderId = `${selectedFolderId}`.
![image](images/blog/ms-graph-add-drive-item-grid.png)
1. Set __AllowDelete__ to __True__ for the __DataGrid__ component and invoke __MSGraph__ data-source method `deleteDrivesItems()` with two parameters:
- driveId = `${drive.id}`.
- driveItemId = `${event.id}`.
![image](images/blog/ms-graph-add-drive-item-delete.png)
1. Run the application, login using your Microsoft credentials, browse your OneDrive, delete and rename items and add new folders.
![image](images/blog/ms-graph-one-drive-crud.png)

Enjoy!

# Master/Detail with two grids, Angular and Radzen

> Display Order details for selected Order

Using Radzen you can create master/detail with two grids in three easy steps:

1. Drop DataGrid component to Radzen design surface, bind it to your first table (in my case [Orders](http://services.odata.org/V4/Northwind/Northwind.svc/Orders) from [Northwind OData service](http://services.odata.org/V4/Northwind/Northwind.svc/Orders)) and auto-generate columns
![image](images/blog/master-detail-two-grids1.png)
*Bind first DataGrid to Orders*

2. Define select event for the DataGrid component to invoke [Order Details](http://services.odata.org/V4/Northwind/Northwind.svc/Order_Details) with filter **OrderID eq ${event.OrderID}** and set a property **orderDetails** to the result value
![image](images/blog/master-detail-two-grids2.png)
*Invoke Order Details and set property value*

3. Drop second DataGrid component to Radzen design surface, bind it to **orderDetails** property and auto-generate columns
![image](images/blog/master-detail-two-grids3.png)
*Bind second DataGrid to Order Details*

4. Run the application to check Order details for the selected Order
![image](images/blog/master-detail-two-grids4.png)
*Order Details for selected Order*

Enjoy!

# Migrate Microsoft LightSwitch application

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/migrate-microsoft-lightswitch-application.md

# Migrate Microsoft LightSwitch application

> Migrate Microsoft LightSwitch application

In this blog post I will show you how to migrate a Microsoft LightSwitch application with Radzen.

1\. Create а new Microsoft LightSwitch application that displays the Products table from the Northwind database:

![Ls Northwind Db Clean](images/blog/ls-northwind-db-clean.png)
![Ls Northwind Db App Products](images/blog/ls-northwind-db-app-products.png)

2\. Enable Forms authentication for application access control:

![Ls Northwind Db App](images/blog/ls-northwind-db-app.png)

3\. Publish the app to IIS using an `admin` user as the application administrator:

![Ls Northwind Db App Publish](images/blog/ls-northwind-db-app-publish.png)
![Ls Northwind Db App Publish Login](images/blog/ls-northwind-db-app-publish-login.png)
![Ls Northwind Db App Publish Products](images/blog/ls-northwind-db-app-publish-products.png)

This will create the ASP.NET membership tables. LightSwitch uses those to store users, passwords, roles, etc:

![Ls Northwind Db Membership](images/blog/ls-northwind-db-membership.png)

4\. Create a new database as a copy of the existing one used in the LightSwitch application:

![Ls Northwind New Db Restore](images/blog/ls-northwind-new-db-restore.png)
![Ls Northwind New Db Clean](images/blog/ls-northwind-new-db-clean.png)

5\. Create a new Radzen application that displays the Products table:

![Ls Northwind New Radzen](images/blog/ls-northwind-new-radzen.png)
![Ls Northwind New Radzen Datasource](images/blog/ls-northwind-new-radzen-datasource.png)
![Ls Northwind New Radzen Products](images/blog/ls-northwind-new-radzen-products.png)

6\. Enable security with email confirmation:

![Ls Northwind New Radzen Security](images/blog/ls-northwind-new-radzen-security.png)

7\. Deploy the application to IIS from Radzen:

![Ls Northwind New Radzen Deploy](images/blog/ls-northwind-new-radzen-deploy.png)

We now have the ASP.NET Core 2.0 Identity tables in our new database:

![Ls Northwind Db Membership New](images/blog/ls-northwind-db-membership-new.png)

and we can use [the following SQL script](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/migration/proper-to-2x/membership-to-core-identity?view=aspnetcore-2.2#migrate-the-schema) to migrate our users, passwords, roles, etc. to the new database:

```
-- THIS SCRIPT NEEDS TO RUN FROM THE CONTEXT OF THE MEMBERSHIP DB
BEGIN TRANSACTION MigrateUsersAndRoles
USE Northwind

-- INSERT USERS
INSERT INTO NorthwindNew.dbo.AspNetUsers
          (Id,
           UserName,
           NormalizedUserName,
           PasswordHash,
           SecurityStamp,
           EmailConfirmed,
           PhoneNumber,
           PhoneNumberConfirmed,
           TwoFactorEnabled,
           LockoutEnd,
           LockoutEnabled,
           AccessFailedCount,
           Email,
           NormalizedEmail)
SELECT aspnet_Users.UserId,
     aspnet_Users.UserName,
     -- The NormalizedUserName value is upper case in ASP.NET Core Identity
     UPPER(aspnet_Users.UserName),
     -- Creates an empty password since passwords don't map between the 2 schemas
     '',
     /*
      The SecurityStamp token is used to verify the state of an account and
      is subject to change at any time. It should be initialized as a new ID.
     */
     NewID(),
     /*
      EmailConfirmed is set when a new user is created and confirmed via email.
      Users must have this set during migration to reset passwords.
     */
     1,
     aspnet_Users.MobileAlias,
     CASE
       WHEN aspnet_Users.MobileAlias IS NULL THEN 0
       ELSE 1
     END,
     -- 2FA likely wasn't setup in Membership for users, so setting as false.
     0,
     CASE
       -- Setting lockout date to time in the future (1,000 years)
       WHEN aspnet_Membership.IsLockedOut = 1 THEN Dateadd(year, 1000,
                                                   Sysutcdatetime())
       ELSE NULL
     END,
     aspnet_Membership.IsLockedOut,
     /*
      AccessFailedAccount is used to track failed logins. This is stored in
      Membership in multiple columns. Setting to 0 arbitrarily.
     */
     0,
     aspnet_Membership.Email,
     -- The NormalizedEmail value is upper case in ASP.NET Core Identity
     UPPER(aspnet_Membership.Email)
FROM   aspnet_Users
     LEFT OUTER JOIN aspnet_Membership
                  ON aspnet_Membership.ApplicationId =
                     aspnet_Users.ApplicationId
                     AND aspnet_Users.UserId = aspnet_Membership.UserId
     LEFT OUTER JOIN NorthwindNew.dbo.AspNetUsers
                  ON aspnet_Membership.UserId = AspNetUsers.Id
WHERE  AspNetUsers.Id IS NULL

-- INSERT ROLES
INSERT INTO NorthwindNew.dbo.AspNetRoles(Id, Name)
SELECT RoleId, RoleName
FROM aspnet_Roles;

-- INSERT USER ROLES
INSERT INTO NorthwindNew.dbo.AspNetUserRoles(UserId, RoleId)
SELECT UserId, RoleId
FROM aspnet_UsersInRoles;

IF @@ERROR <> 0
BEGIN
  ROLLBACK TRANSACTION MigrateUsersAndRoles
  RETURN
END

COMMIT TRANSACTION MigrateUsersAndRoles

```
![Ls Northwind Db Membership New Migrate1](images/blog/ls-northwind-db-membership-new-migrate1.png)
![Ls Northwind Db Membership New Migrate2](images/blog/ls-northwind-db-membership-new-migrate2.png)

We are done!

Now we only need to reset the password from the deployed Radzen application. Microsoft LightSwitch apps needed either a desktop app or custom pages for user management. For the purpose of this blog post I'll take the shortcut and I will enter my admin user email directly in the database:

![Ls Northwind Db Membership Email](images/blog/ls-northwind-db-membership-email.png)

Now we can reset the password from the deployed Radzen application:

![Ls Northwind New Radzen Password Reset](images/blog/ls-northwind-new-radzen-password-reset.png)

You will receive email with a link to generate new password and you can use it to login:

![Ls Northwind New Radzen New Password Login](images/blog/ls-northwind-new-radzen-new-password-login.png)
![Ls Northwind New Radzen New Password Success](images/blog/ls-northwind-new-radzen-new-password-success.png)

If you don't want your users to reset their passwords you can use a custom password hasher which makes ASP.NET Membership (LightSwitch) passwords work with ASP.NET Core Identity (Radzen):

We need first to copy both `Password` and `PasswordSalt` from old `aspnet_Membership` table:

```
-- THIS SCRIPT NEEDS TO RUN FROM THE CONTEXT OF THE MEMBERSHIP DB
BEGIN TRANSACTION MigrateUsersAndRoles
USE Northwind

-- INSERT USERS
INSERT INTO NorthwindNew.dbo.AspNetUsers
          (Id,
           UserName,
           NormalizedUserName,
           PasswordHash,
           SecurityStamp,
           EmailConfirmed,
           PhoneNumber,
           PhoneNumberConfirmed,
           TwoFactorEnabled,
           LockoutEnd,
           LockoutEnabled,
           AccessFailedCount,
           Email,
           NormalizedEmail)
SELECT aspnet_Users.UserId,
     aspnet_Users.UserName,
     -- The NormalizedUserName value is upper case in ASP.NET Core Identity
     UPPER(aspnet_Users.UserName),
     -- Copy both Password and PasswordSalt
     aspnet_Membership.Password + ':' + aspnet_Membership.PasswordSalt,
     /*
      The SecurityStamp token is used to verify the state of an account and
      is subject to change at any time. It should be initialized as a new ID.
     */
     NewID(),
     /*
      EmailConfirmed is set when a new user is created and confirmed via email.
      Users must have this set during migration to reset passwords.
     */
     1,
     aspnet_Users.MobileAlias,
     CASE
       WHEN aspnet_Users.MobileAlias IS NULL THEN 0
       ELSE 1
     END,
     -- 2FA likely wasn't setup in Membership for users, so setting as false.
     0,
     CASE
       -- Setting lockout date to time in the future (1,000 years)
       WHEN aspnet_Membership.IsLockedOut = 1 THEN Dateadd(year, 1000,
                                                   Sysutcdatetime())
       ELSE NULL
     END,
     aspnet_Membership.IsLockedOut,
     /*
      AccessFailedAccount is used to track failed logins. This is stored in
      Membership in multiple columns. Setting to 0 arbitrarily.
     */
     0,
     aspnet_Membership.Email,
     -- The NormalizedEmail value is upper case in ASP.NET Core Identity
     UPPER(aspnet_Membership.Email)
FROM   aspnet_Users
     LEFT OUTER JOIN aspnet_Membership
                  ON aspnet_Membership.ApplicationId =
                     aspnet_Users.ApplicationId
                     AND aspnet_Users.UserId = aspnet_Membership.UserId
     LEFT OUTER JOIN NorthwindNew.dbo.AspNetUsers
                  ON aspnet_Membership.UserId = AspNetUsers.Id
WHERE  AspNetUsers.Id IS NULL

-- INSERT ROLES
INSERT INTO NorthwindNew.dbo.AspNetRoles(Id, Name)
SELECT RoleId, RoleName
FROM aspnet_Roles;

-- INSERT USER ROLES
INSERT INTO NorthwindNew.dbo.AspNetUserRoles(UserId, RoleId)
SELECT UserId, RoleId
FROM aspnet_UsersInRoles;

IF @@ERROR <> 0
BEGIN
  ROLLBACK TRANSACTION MigrateUsersAndRoles
  RETURN
END

COMMIT TRANSACTION MigrateUsersAndRoles

```

Just create a `server\Startup.Custom.cs` file in the Radzen application with the following content:

```
namespace NorthwindNew
{
    public partial class Startup
    {
        partial void OnConfigureServices(IServiceCollection services)
        {
            services.AddScoped<IPasswordHasher<ApplicationUser>, CustomPasswordHasher>();
        }
    }

    public class CustomPasswordHasher : PasswordHasher<ApplicationUser>
    {
        public static string GenerateHash(string providedPassword, byte[] saltAsByteArray)
        {
            var sha = new System.Security.Cryptography.SHA1CryptoServiceProvider();

            byte[] p1 = saltAsByteArray;
            byte[] p2 = System.Text.Encoding.Unicode.GetBytes(providedPassword);

            byte[] data = new byte[p1.Length + p2.Length];

            p1.CopyTo(data, 0);
            p2.CopyTo(data, p1.Length);

            return Convert.ToBase64String(sha.ComputeHash(data));
        }

        public override PasswordVerificationResult VerifyHashedPassword(ApplicationUser user, string hashedPasswordAndSalt,
           string providedPassword)
        {
            if (hashedPasswordAndSalt.IndexOf(":" != -1)
            {
                var hashedPassword = hashedPasswordAndSalt.Split(':')[0];
                var salt = hashedPasswordAndSalt.Split(':')[1];

                var hashedProvidedPassword = GenerateHash(providedPassword, Convert.FromBase64String(salt));

                return hashedPassword == hashedProvidedPassword
                    ? PasswordVerificationResult.SuccessRehashNeeded
                    : base.VerifyHashedPassword(user, hashedPassword, providedPassword);
            }
            else
            {
                return base.VerifyHashedPassword(user, hashedPasswordAndSalt, providedPassword);
            }
        }
    }
}")

```

Enjoy!

# The evolution of ASP.NET Web Forms with ASP.NET Core, Angular and Radzen.

> The evolution of ASP.NET Web Forms with ASP.NET Core, Angular and Radzen.

Still having a bunch of applications using the good old [ASP.NET Web Forms](https://www.asp.net/web-forms)? Tired of the application performance, ViewState and all the hacks you've made to make it look good and actually work? Do you want something lightweight, super fast and pretty? You don't have time to learn yet another framework, do you? And you want to leverage your expertise in C# or VB.NET? Well, it's time for action. [ASP.NET Core 2.0](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/getting-started) is here and it's time to get advantage of it with Radzen!

## ASP.NET Core 2.0 is fast
Check out the recent performance tests made by [Ben Adams](https://twitter.com/ben_a_adams/status/1016386841644331010). It's fast, right?
![image](images/blog/aspnetcore-perf.png)

## You can deploy your applications on Linux too
Yep, you can deploy your applications on [Linux](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/host-and-deploy/linux-nginx), on [Apache](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/host-and-deploy/linux-apache), [Docker](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/host-and-deploy/docker), on [Azure](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/host-and-deploy/azure-apps) and of course on [your trustworthy Windows IIS](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/host-and-deploy/iis/?view=aspnetcore-2.1&tabs=aspnetcore2x).
![image](images/blog/aspnetcore-deploy.png)

## You can use both C# and VB.NET
VB.NET was widely popular in ASP.NET Web Forms and [we at Radzen are proud to be the first solution to use it with ASP.NET Core](/blog/visual-basic-support)!
![image](images/blog/vb-startup.png)

## OData for ASP.NET Core 2.0 is official
[Microsoft just released officially OData for ASP.NET Core 2.0](https://blogs.msdn.microsoft.com/odatateam/2018/07/03/asp-net-core-odata-now-available) and together with [Entity Framework Core](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/ef/core/what-is-new/ef-core-2.1) you have the best way to expose your data!
![image](images/blog/aspnetcore-odata.png)

So how do you kickstart with all these great technologies? How to drag & drop and data-bind components visually like you used to do with ASP.NET Web Forms and Visual Studio? It's easy - we have it all in Radzen!

## Visual WYSIWYG design-time experience
With the [Radzen designer](/documentation/design-time) you can easily create layouts and pages, drag & drop components and bind them to your data, configure them in the way you want with minimal effort and code.
![image](images/blog/radzen-designer.png)

## Rich service and database connectivity
You have data in a [Microsoft SQL Server](/documentation/ms-sql), [MySQL](/documentation/mysql) or [PostgreSQL](/documentation/postgresql) database? Radzen can connect to them! You have an [OData](/documentation/odata), [REST](/documentation/rest) or [Swagger](/documentation/swagger) service? Radzen can consume them!
![image](images/blog/radzen-datasources.png)

## Code-generation and templates to kickstart your development
Because your productivity is important for us we have created [the best code generation service](/blog/master-detail-crud) to expose your data as C# or VB.NET models and controllers.
![image](images/blog/vs-code.png)

## Angular toolbox with 55 powerful components
Radzen applications are powered by [Angular](https://angular.io) - the most popular and widely adopted JavaScript framework from Google used by millions of developers with lots of resources and learning materials, and [Bootstrap](https://getbootstrap.com), the most popular responsive CSS framework.
![image](images/blog/radzen-toolbox.png)

## Extensible. No vendor lock-in. No running costs. Mobile ready.
With Radzen you will cut the development time to minimum. Without using proprietary frameworks and code. The [applications can be fully customized and extend](/documentation/customizing-generated-application) per your needs and all stays at your premises. [Find more about Radzen here.](/why)

# MSGraph with Blazor

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/msgraph-with-blazor.md

# MSGraph with Blazor

> How to connect MSGraph using OData and AzureAD in Blazor applications

We are happy to share that Blazor applications in Radzen recently got a very important update: OData data source with AzureAD authentication!

In this post I'm going to show you how to connect __MSGraph__ using __OData__ and __AzureAD__ in __Blazor__ applications in few steps. [Microsoft Graph](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/overview) is the gateway to data in Microsoft 365 and exposes REST APIs to access Excel, OneDrive, Outlook/Exchange, SharePoint, etc.

1\. Create new application in [Azure portal](https://aka.ms/AppRegistrationsPreview).

![Blazor Msgraph1](images/blog/blazor-msgraph1.png)

2\. Add `http://localhost:5000/ms-graph-callback` in __Authentication -> Redirect URIs__. Add permissions to sign-in and read the user. Check also [Microsoft Graph REST API reference](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/users?view=graph-rest-1.0) for more info how to access and manage users.

![Blazor Msgraph2](images/blog/blazor-msgraph2.png)

3\. Create new __Blazor__ application in Radzen, add new __OData__ data-source connected to `https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/` endpoint with __AzureAD__ authentication. Set `https://login.microsoftonline.com/common/v2.0/` for __Authorization Endpoint__ and enter __ClientID__, and __Client Secret__ obtained from your application in Azure portal. Add `user.read` to __Scopes__ and check all entities.

![Blazor Msgraph3](images/blog/blazor-msgraph3.png)

![Blazor Msgraph4](images/blog/blazor-msgraph4.png)

4\. Create new page, invoke `MSGraph.getMe` data source method using __Load__ event and assign `${result.displayName}` to `name` property. Add new __Label__ component to the page and set __Text__ property to `${name}`.

![Blazor Msgraph5](images/blog/blazor-msgraph5.png)

![Blazor Msgraph6](images/blog/blazor-msgraph6.png)

5\. Run the application, sign-in and check the result.

![Blazor Msgraph7](images/blog/blazor-msgraph7.png)

![Blazor Msgraph8](images/blog/blazor-msgraph8.png)

Let's now list [Microsoft OneDrive](https://onedrive.live.com) files and folders!

1. Create new page named __OneDrive__, drag and drop a __Row__ and two __Column__ component from Radzen toolbox. Set 3 and 9 for the size of first and second column and add __Tree__ component to the first column and __DataGrid__ component to the second column.
1. Define page property `rootItems` of type `List<DriveItem>` with `null` as value.
1. Invoke __MSGraph__ data-source `getDrives()` method on page __Load__ event and set page property `driveId` to `result.Value.ToList()[0].id`.
1. In `getDrives()` __Then__ invoke __MSGraph__ data-source `getDrivesRoot()` method with `${driveId}` as parameter. Set `rootItems` to `new List<DriveItem>(){ result }` and define property `itemId` with value `${result.id}`. Execute `${grid0.Reload()}`.
1. Bind the __Tree__ component to `rootItems` page property and define one level using `microsoft.graph.driveItem` schema. Set `name` for the level __TextProperty__ property and `children` for the level __ChildrenProperty__ property.
1. Invoke __MSGraph__ data-source `getDrivesItemsChildren()` method on __Tree__ component __Expand__ event with three parameters:
- id = `${driveId}`.
- driveItemId = `{((DriveItem)args.Value).id}`.
- $filter = `file eq null`. Filter drive items to return only folders.
Execute `event.Children.TextProperty = "name"` and `event.Children.Data = result.Value` in invoke __Then__.
1. Set page property `itemId` to `((DriveItem)event.Value).id` on __Tree__ component __Change__ event and execute `${grid0.Reload()}`.
1. Bind the __DataGrid__ component to `getDrivesItemsChildren()` using new data wizard, remove unwanted columns and paging parameters from __LoadData__ event `getDrivesItemsChildren()` invoke and add two parameters to:
- id = `${driveId}`.
- driveItemId = `${itemId}`.
Turn off __DataGrid__ paging, sorting and filtering and set `Visible` property to `${itemId != null}`.

![image](images/blog/blazor-onedrive-design.png)

.. and that's all!

![image](images/blog/blazor-onedrive.gif)

Combining Radzen powerful native Blazor WYSIWYG designer, CRUD pages scaffolding and connectivity to MSGraph you can develop complex user interfaces visually consuming data from Microsoft Office 365.

If you still haven’t tried Radzen you can get the latest bits from [here](/download). Check also [our FREE native Blazor components](https://blazor.radzen.com). Don’t forget to share your feedback with us! Send an email to [info at radzen.com](mailto:info@@radzen.com) or post in our [forum](http://forum.radzen.com).

Enjoy!

# Multitenant Blazor applications

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/multitenant-blazor-applications.md

# Multitenant Blazor applications

> Multitenant Blazor applications

In this post I'm going to show you how to enable multitenancy with data isolation for Blazor application in few steps. The end result will be an application that uses a separate database for every tenant. The current tenant will be determined from the application URL.

1\. Create new Blazor application, add new MSSQL data-source connected to our Sample database and auto-generate pages.

![Blazor Multi Tenant1](images/blog/blazor-multi-tenant1.png)

2\. Run the application from Radzen to generate everything needed and add the following file to application ignore list to tell Radzen to ignore it during subsequent code generation.

```
server\Program.cs
```

![Blazor Multi Tenant2](images/blog/blazor-multi-tenant2.png)

3\. Add the following __Multitenancy__ section in `server\appsettings.json` with information about tenants, their hostnames and connection strings. We specify two hostnames per tenant - one for debug mode (so you can test while developing the application) and one for production (which your users will browse).

**server\appsettings.json**
```json
{
  ...
  "ConnectionStrings": {
    "SampleConnection": "Server=.;Initial Catalog=Sample-Tenant1;Persist Security Info=False;User ID=sa;Password=passw0rdMSSQL;MultipleActiveResultSets=False;Encrypt=false;TrustServerCertificate=true;Connection Timeout=30"
  },
  "Multitenancy": {
    "Tenants": [
      {
        "Name": "Tenant1",
        "Hostnames": [
          "localhost:5001",
          "tenant1.radzen-rocks.com"
        ],
        "ConnectionString": "Server=.;Initial Catalog=Sample-Tenant1;Persist Security Info=False;User ID=sa;Password=yourpassword;MultipleActiveResultSets=False;Encrypt=false;TrustServerCertificate=true;Connection Timeout=30"
      },
      {
        "Name": "Tenant2",
        "Hostnames": [
          "localhost:5002",
          "tenant2.radzen-rocks.com"
        ],
        "ConnectionString": "Server=.;Initial Catalog=Sample-Tenant2;Persist Security Info=False;User ID=sa;Password=yourpassword;MultipleActiveResultSets=False;Encrypt=false;TrustServerCertificate=true;Connection Timeout=30"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

4\. Add partial method `Startup.OnConfigureServices` to read multitenancy from `server\appsettings.json` and register it for dependency injection together with HttpContextAccessor.

```cs
using BlazorMultiTenant.Data;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Builder;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Hosting;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Infrastructure;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Storage;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration;
using Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection;
using System.Collections.ObjectModel;

namespace BlazorMultiTenant
{
    public partial class Startup
    {
        partial void OnConfigureServices(IServiceCollection services)
        {
            services.AddSingleton<IHttpContextAccessor, HttpContextAccessor>();
            services.AddSingleton(Configuration.GetSection("Multitenancy".Get<Multitenancy>());
        }

        partial void OnConfigure(IApplicationBuilder app, IWebHostEnvironment env)
        {
            using (var scope = app.ApplicationServices.GetRequiredService<IServiceScopeFactory>().CreateScope())
            {
                using (var context = scope.ServiceProvider.GetService<SampleContext>())
                {
                    var created = context.Database.EnsureCreated();
                    if (created)
                    {
                        var databaseCreator = (RelationalDatabaseCreator)context.Database.GetService<IDatabaseCreator>();
                        databaseCreator.CreateTables();
                    }
                }

                using (var context = scope.ServiceProvider.GetService<ApplicationIdentityDbContext>())
                {
                    context.Database.Migrate();
                }
            }
        }
    }

    public class Tenant
    {
        public string Name { get; set; }
        public string[] Hostnames { get; set; }
        public string ConnectionString { get; set; }
    }

    public class Multitenancy
    {
        public Collection<Tenant> Tenants { get; set; }
    }
}")

```

![Blazor Multi Tenant3](images/blog/blazor-multi-tenant3.png)

5\. Enable default security for the application and auto-generate pages for user and role management.

![Blazor Multi Tenant4](images/blog/blazor-multi-tenant4.png)

6\. Add `server\Data\SampleContext.Custom.cs` and `server\Data\ApplicationIdentityDbContext.Custom.cs` with the following code to read the tenants.

**SampleContext.Custom.cs**
```cs
public partial class SampleContext
{
    private readonly HttpContext context;
    private readonly Multitenancy multitenancy;

    public SampleContext(DbContextOptions<SampleContext> options, ApplicationIdentityDbContext identityDbContext, IHttpContextAccessor httpContextAccessor, Multitenancy mt) : base(options)
    {
        context = httpContextAccessor.HttpContext;
        multitenancy = mt;
    }

    public SampleContext(IHttpContextAccessor httpContextAccessor, Multitenancy mt, ApplicationIdentityDbContext identityDbContext)
    {
        context = httpContextAccessor.HttpContext;
        multitenancy = mt;
    }

    protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder optionsBuilder)
    {
        if (multitenancy != null && context != null)
        {
            var tenant = multitenancy.Tenants
                    .Where(t => t.Hostnames.Contains(context.Request.Host.Value)).FirstOrDefault();

            if (tenant != null)
            {
                optionsBuilder.UseSqlServer(tenant.ConnectionString);
            }
        }
    }
}

```

**ApplicationIdentityDbContext.Custom.cs**
```cs
public partial class ApplicationIdentityDbContext
{
    private readonly HttpContext context;
    private readonly Multitenancy multitenancy;

    public ApplicationIdentityDbContext(DbContextOptions<ApplicationIdentityDbContext> options, IHttpContextAccessor httpContextAccessor, Multitenancy mt) : base(options)
    {
        context = httpContextAccessor.HttpContext;
        multitenancy = mt;
    }

    public ApplicationIdentityDbContext(IHttpContextAccessor httpContextAccessor, Multitenancy mt)
    {
        context = httpContextAccessor.HttpContext;
        multitenancy = mt;
    }

    protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder optionsBuilder)
    {
        if (multitenancy != null && context != null)
        {
            var tenant = multitenancy.Tenants
                    .Where(t => t.Hostnames.Contains(context.Request.Host.Value)).FirstOrDefault();

            if (tenant != null)
            {
                optionsBuilder.UseSqlServer(tenant.ConnectionString);
            }
        }
    }
}

```

7\. Add `UseUrls()` to `server\Program.cs` to specify the urls the web host will listen on for each tenant in debug mode. Modify the connection string in `.env` and `appsettings.json` and set default tenant to __Tenant1__.

```cs
public class Program
{
    public static void Main(string[] args)
    {
        CreateHostBuilder(args).Build().Run();
    }

    public static IHostBuilder CreateHostBuilder(string[] args) =>
        Host.CreateDefaultBuilder(args)
            .ConfigureWebHostDefaults(webBuilder =>
            {
                webBuilder.UseKestrel();
                webBuilder.UseUrls("https://localhost:5001", "https://localhost:5002";
                webBuilder.UseStartup<Startup>();
            });
}")

```
**.env**
```
ConnectionStrings__SampleConnection="Server=.;Initial Catalog=Sample-Tenant1;Persist Security Info=False;User ID=sa;Password=passw0rdMSSQL;MultipleActiveResultSets=False;Encrypt=false;TrustServerCertificate=true;Connection Timeout=30"

```

8\. Run the application, go to `http://localhost:5001` and login using `admin/admin` to access __Tenant1__ database. You can now create roles and users for __Tenant1__.

![Blazor Multi Tenant5](images/blog/blazor-multi-tenant5.png)
![Blazor Multi Tenant6](images/blog/blazor-multi-tenant6.png)

9\. Modify the connection string in `.env` and `appsettings.json` and set default tenant to __Tenant2__.

**.env**
```
ConnectionStrings__SampleConnection="Server=.;Initial Catalog=Sample-Tenant2;Persist Security Info=False;User ID=sa;Password=passw0rdMSSQL;MultipleActiveResultSets=False;Encrypt=false;TrustServerCertificate=true;Connection Timeout=30"

```

**server\appsettings.json**
```json
{
  ...
  "ConnectionStrings": {
    "SampleConnection": "Server=.;Initial Catalog=Sample-Tenant2;Persist Security Info=False;User ID=sa;Password=passw0rdMSSQL;MultipleActiveResultSets=False;Encrypt=false;TrustServerCertificate=true;Connection Timeout=30"
  },
  "Multitenancy": {
    "Tenants": [
      {
        "Name": "Tenant1",
        "Hostnames": [
          "localhost:5001",
          "tenant1.radzen-rocks.com"
        ],
        "ConnectionString": "Server=.;Initial Catalog=Sample-Tenant1;Persist Security Info=False;User ID=sa;Password=yourpassword;MultipleActiveResultSets=False;Encrypt=false;TrustServerCertificate=true;Connection Timeout=30"
      },
      {
        "Name": "Tenant2",
        "Hostnames": [
          "localhost:5002",
          "tenant2.radzen-rocks.com"
        ],
        "ConnectionString": "Server=.;Initial Catalog=Sample-Tenant2;Persist Security Info=False;User ID=sa;Password=yourpassword;MultipleActiveResultSets=False;Encrypt=false;TrustServerCertificate=true;Connection Timeout=30"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

10\. Run the application, go to `http://localhost:5002` and login using `admin/admin` to access __Tenant2__ database and add roles and users for __Tenant2__.

![Blazor Multi Tenant7](images/blog/blazor-multi-tenant7.png)

You have now separate security for each tenant!

![Blazor Multi Tenant8](images/blog/blazor-multi-tenant8.png)

Both __ApplicationIdentityDbContext__ and __SampleDataContext__ will retrieve runtime the tenant connection string depending on the application host:

![Blazor Multi Tenant9](images/blog/blazor-multi-tenant9.png)

Enjoy!

[Source Code](https://github.com/radzenhq/radzen-examples/tree/master/BlazorMultiTenant)

# What's New in Radzen Blazor Studio: Smarter Toolbox, Streamlined Properties, and Easier Theming

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/new-in-radzen-blazor-studio-smarter-toolbox-streamlined-properties-and-easier-theming.md

# What's New in Radzen Blazor Studio: Smarter Toolbox, Streamlined Properties, and Easier Theming

> We’re excited to share some of the latest updates in Radzen Blazor Studio - all designed to improve your productivity and streamline your UI development experience.

We’re excited to share some of the latest updates in Radzen Blazor Studio-all designed to improve your productivity and streamline your UI development experience.

## Toolbox Enhancements: Simple vs. Advanced Modes
Our updated Toolbox now features a **Simple mode** that organizes Radzen Blazor Components by functionality. This new layout is ideal for developers who prefer a cleaner, more task-oriented view of available components. A **toggle button** at the top of the Toolbox panel lets you easily switch between **Simple** and **Advanced** modes, giving you full control over how you browse and add components to your app.

<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-studio-toolbox.gif" alt="A preview of Radzen Blazor Studio Toolbox" style="border-radius: 12px;" loading="lazy">

But we’re not stopping there! We’re currently working on integrating code snippets into the Toolbox. These will be preconfigured component setups for common scenarios, helping you scaffold UI elements even faster.

## Grouped Component Properties for Easier Configuration

Setting up and customizing components just got easier. The **Properties grid** now groups related settings together, making it faster to understand and adjust component behavior. Whether you're configuring a data grid or fine-tuning a chart, this update helps reduce friction and keeps your focus where it matters-on building great apps.

<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-studio-property-grid.png" alt="Properties Grid in Radzen Blazor Studio" style="border-radius: 12px;" loading="lazy">

## Smarter Theming: One Color to Rule Them All
Changing your app’s look is now as simple as picking a single primary color.

Different design systems use and calculate colors in various ways. We’ve taken this into account and updated the theme editor to automatically generate colors from a single primary color selection, based on the chosen theme (design system).

And if you need precise control, you can always override individual colors to fine-tune your palette.

<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-studio-smart-theming.gif" alt="Smart Theming in Radzen Blazor Studio" style="border-radius: 12px;" loading="lazy">

# New powerful Blazor DataGrid component from Radzen

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/new-powerful-blazor-datagrid-component-from-radzen.md

# New powerful Blazor DataGrid component from Radzen

> Introducing our new powerful Blazor DataGrid component. Virtualization support, frozen columns, multiple columns sorting and more!

We are happy to share that we've just released our brand new powerful Blazor DataGrid component with virtualization support, frozen columns,
multiple columns sorting, improved filtering API and many more!

## Virtualization

Virtualization allows you to render large amounts of data on demand. The RadzenDataGrid component uses [Entity Framework to query the visible data](https://blazor.radzen.com/datagrid-virtualization). Just set the AllowVirtualization property to true. Requires .NET Core 5.0+.
RadzenDataGrid supports [virtualization with custom data-binding](https://blazor.radzen.com/datagrid-virtualization-loaddata) scenarios as well - handle the LoadData event as usual.

![image](images/blog/datagrid-virtualization.gif)

## Frozen columns

Lock columns to prevent them from scrolling out of view via the [Frozen property](https://blazor.radzen.com/datagrid-frozen-columns).

![image](images/blog/datagrid-frozen-columns.gif)

## Multiple columns sorting and column sort API

You can allow now [multiple column sorting](https://blazor.radzen.com/datagrid-multi-sort) if you set AllowMultiColumnSorting to true. You can set also the initial column sort order using [SortOrder column property](https://blazor.radzen.com/datagrid-sort-api).

![image](images/blog/datagrid-multiple-columns-sorting.gif)

## Filtering API

Set the [initial filter of your RadzenDataGrid](https://blazor.radzen.com/datagrid-filter-api) via the FilterValue and FilterOperator column properties.

![image](images/blog/datagrid-filtering-api.gif)

## Radzen support

The new DataGrid component will be added to Radzen after a month. Only newly created pages will use it though - existing ones will not be updated automatically.

We would love to hear your feedback in the meantime!

Cheers!

---

# New: RadzenSkeleton Blazor Component

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/new-radzen-skeleton-blazor-component.md

# New: RadzenSkeleton Blazor Component

> RadzenSkeleton is a UI component that displays a placeholder while your application fetches data.

Loading states are part of every modern web application. Instead of leaving users staring at empty screens or spinners, developers now use skeleton loaders - lightweight placeholders that resemble the content being loaded.

With the latest release of Radzen.Blazor, you now have a dedicated component for this: **[RadzenSkeleton](https://blazor.radzen.com/skeleton)**.

## What is RadzenSkeleton?

RadzenSkeleton is a UI component that displays a placeholder while your application fetches data. It helps you:

- **Maintain layout** - reserve space so the UI doesn’t shift when content arrives.
- **Improve perceived performance** - users see immediate structure instead of a blank screen.
- **Match content shapes** - text, images, avatars, cards, or custom layouts.

<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-skeleton-component.png" alt="Radzen Blazor Skeleton Component" class="rz-w-50 rz-mx-auto rz-my-8" style="border-radius: 12px;" loading="lazy">

## Basic Usage

With RadzenSkeleton, you can make loading states in your Blazor apps look professional, smooth, and consistent with minimal effort. Here’s how you can get started:

```html
<RadzenSkeleton />
```

This renders a simple text skeleton with a height value inherited by the parent's font size.

You can also create circular or rectangular skeletons, ideal for profile pictures, icons, or images.

The component is flexible enough for complex placeholders:

- **Animations** - choose between Pulse or Wave to indicate activity.
- **Custom dimensions** - control width and height to mimic your actual UI.
- **Multiple placeholders** - in combination with [RadzenStack](https://blazor.radzen.com/stack) and [RadzenTable](https://blazor.radzen.com/table) you can simulate entire cards, forms, or grids.

```html
<!-- Circular skeleton -->
<RadzenSkeleton Variant="SkeletonVariant.Circular" Style="width: 1rem; height: 1rem" />

<!-- Rectangular skeleton with Wave animation -->
<RadzenSkeleton Variant="SkeletonVariant.Rectangular" Animation="SkeletonAnimation.Wave" Style="width: 4rem; height: 4rem" />
```

## When to Use It

- **Data-heavy dashboards** - show the layout of charts and tables before data loads.

- **Lists and feeds** - simulate rows, images, or text blocks.

- **Profile pages** - placeholders for avatars and user details.

Explore all demos and usage examples here: [Radzen Skeleton Component Demos](https://blazor.radzen.com/skeleton).

---

# Radzen applications on a mobile device

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/radzen-application-on-mobile-devices.md

# Radzen applications on a mobile device

> Use Apache Cordova to create a mobile Radzen application

Radzen applications are responsive by default which means that they work on a variety of devices - desktops, laptops, tablets or phones.

In this blog post I will show how to use [Apache Cordova](https://cordova.apache.org) to create native iOS or Android wrapper of a Radzen application.

## Install Cordova

Cordove is shipped as a NodeJS package. To install it run the following command from a terminal or command prompt.

`npm install -g cordova`

## Create a Cordova application

The next step is to create a cordova application which will serve as the wrapper of the Radzen application.

Cordova can do that via the `cordova create` command. For demo purposes I will wrap the RadzenCRM demo so I will run the following command.

`cordova create RadzenCRM com.radzen.crm "Radzen CRM"`

## Build the Radzen application

Cordova applications run on a mobile device and cannot host the [server-side layer](documentation/architecture#dotnet) of a Radzen application.
We will use the [manual build procedure](documentation/manual-deploy#production).

1. Go in the `client` directory of your Radzen application.
1. Edit the `client\src\environments\environment.prod.ts` file and change all data source URLs to your production server:
   ```js
   export const environment = {
     serverMethodsUrl: 'http://yourserver/',
     crm: 'https://yourserver/CRM',
     securityUrl: 'http://yourserver/auth',
     production: true
   };
   ```

   For the RadzenCRM demo those are:

   ```js
   export const environment = {
    serverMethodsUrl: 'https://crm.radzen.com/',
    crm: 'https://crm.radzen.com/odata/CRM',
    securityUrl: 'https://crm.radzen.com/auth',
    production: true
   };
   ```
1. Run `npm install`.
1. Create a production build within the `wwwroot` directory of your Cordova application:
 - Windows: `.\node_modules\.bin\ng build --prod --base-href . --output-path <some-directory>\RadzenCRM\www`
 - MacOS: `./node_modules/.bin/ng build --prod --base-href . --output-path <some-directory>/RadzenCRM/www`

## Run in emulators

We can now test the application in the Android or iOS emulators.

### Android

First make sure that you have all Android prerequisites installed. Refer to the [Cordova documentation](https://cordova.apache.org/docs/en/latest/guide/platforms/android/index.html) for more instructions.

1. Open command prompt (Windows) or terminal (macOS) and go to the directory of your Cordova application.
1. Run `cordova platform add android`.
1. Then run `cordova emulate android`. After building the application Cordova will run it in the configured Android Virtual Device.

<img src="images/blog/cordova-android.png" width="320" loading="lazy" alt="Radzen application running on Android emulator">

### iOS

The iOS emulator works only on macOS and will need a working XCode installation.

1. Open terminal (macOS) and go to the directory of your Cordova application.
1. Run `cordova platform add ios`.
1. Then run `cordova emulate ios`. Cordova will build the application and run it in iOS Simulator.

<img src="images/blog/cordova-ios.png" width="320" loading="lazy" alt="Radzen application running on iOS simulator">

Cheers!

---

# Accessibility-compliant UI Components

> Our latest updates bring a host of new accessibility features to our UI components. With these new features, we aim to help you make digital experiences more inclusive and equitable for everyone.

Our latest updates bring a host of new accessibility features to our UI components. With these new features, we aim to help you make digital experiences more inclusive and equitable for everyone.

## WAI-ARIA attributes

ARIA attributes provide additional information to assistive technologies, making complex widgets and interactions more understandable and navigable for users with disabilities.

## Keyboard navigation

Clear and consistent focus styles are applied to interactive elements to enhance usability and accessibility.

## WCAG 2.2 AA compliant color palettes

# Radzen Blazor Components v10.0 - Chip, Gantt, LinearGauge, and More

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/radzen-blazor-components-v10-new-chip-gantt-linear-gauge-and-more.md

# Radzen Blazor Components v10.0 - Chip, Gantt, LinearGauge, and More

> Radzen Blazor v10 ships four new components - Chip, ChipList, Gantt, and LinearGauge - plus Scatter and Bubble chart series, reorderable Tabs, dozens of DataGrid fixes, and accessibility improvements across the board.

**Radzen Blazor v10.0** is here - a major release packed with brand-new components, powerful feature additions, and quality-of-life improvements across the library. Whether you're building project management tools, data dashboards, or polished form experiences, this release has something for you.

Let's walk through everything that's new.

## Gantt

<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-gantt.png" alt="Radzen Blazor Gantt Component" style="border-radius: 12px; width: 80%; margin: 3rem auto;" loading="lazy" />

Plan, schedule, and visualize. The new **[RadzenGantt](https://blazor.radzen.com/gantt)** component renders interactive project timelines with tasks, durations, and dependencies - all inside the browser.

If you're building project management, manufacturing, or resource planning applications, Gantt gives your users an intuitive, visual way to understand timelines and track progress without leaving your Blazor app.

## Chip and ChipList

<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-chip.png" alt="Radzen Blazor Chip Component" style="border-radius: 12px; width: 80%; margin: 3rem auto;" loading="lazy" />

Tags, categories, filters, selected items - chips are one of the most versatile UI patterns in modern applications. The new **[RadzenChip](https://blazor.radzen.com/chip)** and **[RadzenChipList](https://blazor.radzen.com/chiplist)** components bring this pattern to your Blazor apps with full theme support.

Use chips to display compact pieces of information, let users select from a set of options, or build token-based input fields. ChipList handles collections with built-in selection, removal, and templating - so you can get a polished chip experience with minimal code.

## LinearGauge

<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-linear-gauge.png" alt="Radzen Blazor Linear Gauge Component" style="border-radius: 12px; width: 80%; margin: 3rem auto;" loading="lazy" />

The new **[RadzenLinearGauge](https://blazor.radzen.com/linear-gauge)** component displays values along a horizontal or vertical scale - perfect for KPI dashboards, progress indicators, and metric comparisons.

Combine it with the existing RadialGauge and ArcGauge to build comprehensive dashboard experiences.

## Scatter and Bubble Chart Series

<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-bubble-chart.png" alt="Radzen Blazor Bubble Chart" style="border-radius: 12px; width: 80%; margin: 3rem auto;" loading="lazy" />

The Radzen Chart component now supports **[Scatter](https://blazor.radzen.com/scatter-chart)** and **[Bubble](https://blazor.radzen.com/bubble-chart)** series. Scatter plots help you identify correlations between two variables, while Bubble series add a third dimension by varying the size of each data point.

These new series types are ideal for scientific visualization, financial analytics, and any scenario where you need to plot multidimensional data.

## Feature Highlights

### Reorderable Tabs

**RadzenTabs** now supports the `AllowReorder` property. Users can drag tabs to rearrange them - great for customizable dashboards, multi-document interfaces, and any layout where users want control over their workspace.

### Accordion Expand/Collapse All

The **RadzenAccordion** component gains `ExpandAll()` and `CollapseAll()` methods, along with enhanced ARIA attributes. This is a simple but frequently requested addition that makes accordion-heavy UIs more user-friendly.

### PickList Enhancements

**RadzenPickList** received several upgrades in this release:

- **Virtualization support** via `AllowVirtualization` - handle large lists without performance penalties
- **New events**: `SelectedSourceChanged` and `SelectedTargetChanged` for fine-grained state tracking
- **Validation support** through `SourceExpression` and `TargetExpression` - integrate seamlessly with Blazor's `EditForm`
- **EmptyTemplate and EmptyText** properties for better empty-state UX

### Carousel Animation Control

The **RadzenCarousel** now exposes an `AnimationDuration` property, letting you fine-tune how quickly slides transition. Small detail, big impact on the feel of your application.

### Chat - New Messages Button

**RadzenChat** now includes a new-messages button that appears when the user scrolls away from the latest messages - making it easy to jump back to the newest content in long conversations.

### HTML Editor and TextBox - Extensibility

`RadzenTextBox`, `RadzenTextArea`, and `RadzenHtmlEditor` now expose virtual `OnChange` and `SetValue` methods, making it easier to build derived components with custom behavior.

### DropDownDataGrid - Search Clear Button

**RadzenDropDownDataGrid** now shows a clear button in the search field, helping users quickly reset their search and start fresh.

### Drag-and-Drop Events

**RadzenDropZoneContainer** gains `Start` and `End` drag events, giving you precise control over drag-and-drop workflows - useful for tracking state, showing visual feedback, or triggering side effects.

### PanelMenu - Stacked Icon Display

The **RadzenPanelMenu** now supports `MenuItemDisplayStyle.IconAndTextStacked`, placing the icon above the text for a more compact navigation style - common in sidebar menus and mobile-first layouts.

## Accessibility and Keyboard Navigation

This release includes broad accessibility improvements:

- Improved ARIA attributes across **Accordion**, **Tooltip**, and **TOC** components
- Full keyboard navigation compliance for **Tabs** (arrow keys, Home/End, Space/Enter)
- Keyboard selection fixes for **DropDown**, **DropDownDataGrid**, and virtualized lists
- Better focus management across multiple components

## DataGrid Fixes and Improvements

The **RadzenDataGrid** received extensive attention in this release with numerous bug fixes:

- Fixed column resizing on mobile and tablet devices
- Resolved visual spacing issues with fixed/frozen columns
- Improved `Reload()` performance - no more lag
- Fixed `colspan`/`rowspan` rendering
- Corrected keyboard selection behavior with virtualization enabled
- Fixed new row addition when using `LoadData`
- Resolved frozen column header and footer rendering issues

## Performance

CSS rules and SCSS mixins have been optimized across the entire component library, reducing the overall CSS footprint and improving rendering performance.

## Breaking Changes

Before upgrading, note these breaking changes:

1. **RadzenTocItem** now renders an **anchor** element instead of a **button**. Update any CSS selectors that target `.rz-toc-link`.
2. **RadzenToc** selection attribute changed from `aria-current="location"` to `aria-selected`.
3. **RadzenToc** scrolling no longer modifies the browser address bar. URL fragments update only when users click TOC links.

See the full [changelog](https://blazor.radzen.com/changelog) for the complete list of changes.

## Get More with the Radzen Blazor Subscription

Looking for premium themes, the visual Radzen Blazor Studio designer, application templates, priority support, and access to tools like the Radzen MCP Server?

The **[Radzen Blazor Subscription](/pricing)** gives you everything you need to build Blazor applications faster - from AI-assisted development to production-ready templates.

**[See plans and pricing →](/pricing)**

## Thank You

A huge thank you to our community and contributors for your feedback, bug reports, and pull requests. Every release is better because of you.

[Explore Radzen Blazor Components](https://blazor.radzen.com)

[Try Radzen Blazor Studio](/blazor-studio)

[View plans and pricing](/pricing)

# Radzen Blazor Components v11.0: Spreadsheet, 30+ New Charts, and More

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/radzen-blazor-components-v11.md

# Radzen Blazor Components v11.0: Spreadsheet, 30+ New Charts, and More

> Radzen Blazor v11 is our biggest release yet: a full Excel-class Spreadsheet, 30+ new MIT-licensed chart types, SignaturePad and Tile Layout components, HTML Editor tables, a Scheduler Agenda view, the Material 3 Expressive theme, and built-in localization.

What if your Blazor app could drop in a full spreadsheet, formulas, tables, charts and all, in just a few lines of markup? That's just one of the things that's new in **Radzen Blazor Components v11**. Let's get into it.

<div style="margin-block: 40px;">
    <YouTube Video="LgGJgg51N6U" />
</div>

If you're new here: Radzen Blazor is a free, open-source library of over 145 native Blazor components (as of June 2026). And v11 is our biggest release ever, so let's walk through the headline features.

## Spreadsheet

Let's start with the big one: a brand-new **[RadzenSpreadsheet](https://blazor.radzen.com/spreadsheet)** component, and it's genuinely Excel-class.

It ships with over a hundred Excel-compatible formulas, like `VLOOKUP`, `XLOOKUP`, and `SUMIFS`, with live recalculation as your data changes. You get real tables: sort, filter (including Top 10 and color filters), and a totals row. You can insert charts and images right inside the sheet. There's full undo and redo on everything, CSV and high-fidelity XLSX import and export, and a ribbon you can completely customize and lock down with permissions.

Multiple worksheets, freeze panes, merged cells, data validation, and conditional formatting are all built in too.

**[Try the Spreadsheet demo →](https://blazor.radzen.com/spreadsheet)**

## 30+ New Chart Types

Charts got a major upgrade, with more than **[30 new chart types](https://blazor.radzen.com/charts)**, all free and MIT-licensed.

There's a full lineup for finance, like **[candlestick](https://blazor.radzen.com/candlestick-chart)**, **[OHLC](https://blazor.radzen.com/ohlc-chart)**, and [high-low](https://blazor.radzen.com/highlow-chart). Statistical charts like **[box plot](https://blazor.radzen.com/box-plot-chart)**, **[histogram](https://blazor.radzen.com/histogram-chart)**, **[heatmap](https://blazor.radzen.com/heatmap-chart)**, and **[contour](https://blazor.radzen.com/contour-chart)**. Business charts like **[waterfall](https://blazor.radzen.com/waterfall-chart)**, **[funnel](https://blazor.radzen.com/funnel-chart)**, and **[pyramid](https://blazor.radzen.com/pyramid-chart)**, plus **[treemap](https://blazor.radzen.com/treemap-chart)**, **[radar](https://blazor.radzen.com/radar-column-chart)**, **[pareto](https://blazor.radzen.com/pareto-chart)**, and more.

And across all of them you get render animations, gradient fills, zoom and pan, a crosshair, synchronized charts, a **[range navigator](https://blazor.radzen.com/range-navigator)**, and logarithmic and multiple axes. We also redesigned the data labels to stay readable over any fill, and added rounded and exploded pie slices and semi-circle charts.

**[Explore all chart demos →](https://blazor.radzen.com/charts)**

## New Components: SignaturePad and Tile Layout

There are new components, too.

**[RadzenSignaturePad](https://blazor.radzen.com/signature-pad)** captures handwritten signatures right in your app, perfect for approvals, agreements, and delivery confirmations.

**[RadzenTileLayout](https://blazor.radzen.com/tile-layout)** lets you build dashboards with draggable, resizable tiles, so your users can arrange their workspace exactly the way they like it.

## Upgrades to Components You Already Use

Two components your users rely on every day got significant updates.

The **[HTML Editor](https://blazor.radzen.com/html-editor)** now supports full table creation and editing, so authors can build and adjust tables directly in the rich text editor.

The **[Scheduler](https://blazor.radzen.com/scheduler)** adds a new **Agenda** view, a clean list-style layout that complements the existing day, week, and month views.

## New Theme: Material 3 Expressive

On theming, there's a new premium theme, **Material 3 Expressive**, available in light, dark, and accessible WCAG variants. See it alongside the rest of our themes on the **[themes page](https://blazor.radzen.com/themes)**.

## Built-in Internationalization

Internationalization is now built in. Localization is resource-based across every component, with more languages shipping out of the box, including German, French, Spanish, Italian, and Japanese, so your app can speak your users' language with zero extra setup.

## Polish Across the Library

On top of all that, there's a ton of polish across the whole library, from unified input sizing for the entire input family (via the new `InputSize` option) to refinements in components like ColorPicker and SelectBar, a `ToggleVariant` for RadzenToggleButton, and added support for Content Security Policy.

## Breaking Changes

Before you upgrade, note these breaking changes:

1. **.NET 7 support has been removed.** The library now targets net8.0, net9.0, and net10.0.
2. The legacy **RadzenHtml** component was removed. RadzenHtmlEditor is unaffected.
3. Markdown types moved to the `Radzen.Documents.Markdown` namespace.
4. RadzenPopup's internal `Popup` is now public.

See the full [changelog](https://blazor.radzen.com/changelog) for the complete list of changes.

## Get Started with v11

That's Radzen Blazor Components v11: free, open source, and MIT-licensed.

Ready to try it? Update your [`Radzen.Blazor` NuGet package](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Radzen.Blazor) and explore every new component in the [live demos](https://blazor.radzen.com).

If this helps with your Blazor projects, drop us a star on [GitHub](https://github.com/radzenhq/radzen-blazor), and tell us in the [forums](https://forum.radzen.com/) what you'd like us to build next.

[Explore Radzen Blazor Components](https://blazor.radzen.com)

[Try Radzen Blazor Studio](/blazor-studio)

[View plans and pricing](/pricing)
