# Radzen Blazor Components v5 - RTL Support, New Themes and More

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/radzen-blazor-components-v5-rtl-support-new-themes-and-more.md

# Radzen Blazor Components v5 - RTL Support, New Themes and More

> Radzen Blazor Components v5 brings a suite of new features and improvements

We are excited to announce a suite of new features and improvements to our free Radzen Blazor Components library! This update brings enhanced support for internationalization, new components, new dark themes, and significant improvements to typography and iconography. Let's dive into the details!

## Right-to-Left (RTL) support
One of the most significant updates in this major version is the introduction of the highly anticipated Right-to-Left (RTL) support. All Radzen Blazor Components now fully support RTL direction, making it easier to create applications in languages that are written from right to left, such as Arabic, Hebrew, and Persian.

To enable it, just add **dir="rtl"** attribute to the html tag in your layout.

Here is a preview of the DataGrid component in Hebrew RTL mode using the in-browser auto translation from English.
<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-rtl-datagrid.png" alt="A preview of Radzen Blazor DataGrid component in Hebrew RTL mode using auto in-browser translation from English." style="border-radius: 12px;" loading="lazy">

You can run the [online demos](https://blazor.radzen.com/datagrid) in RTL mode - simply toggle the **Enable RTL directionality** option in the demos config.

## New Components

### RadzenAppearanceToggle
The new RadzenAppearanceToggle component allows end users to quickly switch between light and dark modes, enhancing user experience by providing an easy way to adapt the interface to their preference or environment.

<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-appearance-toggle.png" alt="RadzenAppearanceToggle component" style="display: block; border-radius: 40px; margin: 40px auto; max-width: 500px;" loading="lazy">

Try it now in the [online demos](https://blazor.radzen.com/appearance-toggle).

### RadzenTheme
Use RadzenTheme component to load themes into your app. With the RadzenTheme component, applying and switching themes is more straightforward than ever.

To set a theme in .NET8 open the **App.razor** file of your application. Add this code within the **head** element:

```html
<RadzenTheme Theme="material3" @rendermode="InteractiveServer" />

```

See how to use in other .NET versions in the [Get Started](https://blazor.radzen.com/get-started) article.

## New Dark Themes
Our theme library expands with several new free themes, including the open-sourced Material Dark theme. All new themes are shipped with a WCAG compliant counterparts.

Here’s a rundown of the new additions:

- **Material Dark Theme**: This popular theme is now open-sourced and **available for free**! Enjoy the sleek, modern look of Material Dark in your applications.
<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-material-dark-theme.png" alt="Radzen Blazor Material Dark theme" style="border-radius: 12px;" loading="lazy">
- **Standard Dark Theme**: A dark theme counterpart to the clean and professional Standard theme.
<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-standard-dark-theme.png" alt="Radzen Blazor Standard Dark theme" style="border-radius: 12px;" loading="lazy">
- **Humanistic Dark Theme**: A dark variant of the Humanistic theme.
<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-humanistic-dark-theme.png" alt="Radzen Blazor Humanistic Dark theme" style="border-radius: 12px;" loading="lazy">
- **Software Dark Theme**: A dark variant of the Software theme.
<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-software-dark-theme.png" alt="Radzen Blazor Software Dark theme" style="border-radius: 12px;" loading="lazy">

## New Variable Fonts
All our themes now utilize **variable fonts**, providing greater typographic flexibility. Variable fonts eliminate the traditional distinctions between different weights and styles that have been present as separate font files.

<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-variable-fonts.gif" alt="Variable fonts in Radzen Blazor Components" style="display: block; border-radius: 12px; margin: 40px auto; max-width: 600px; border: 1px solid #ccc;" loading="lazy">

- Source Sans Pro to **Source Sans 3**: We have replaced all Source Sans Pro fonts with the more versatile [Source Sans 3](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Source+Sans+3/tester) variable fonts.
- Roboto to **Roboto Flex**: All Roboto fonts have been updated to the [Roboto Flex](https://fonts.google.com/specimen/Roboto+Flex/tester) variable font, offering a broader range of languages, styles and improved rendering.

## New Material Symbols Icon Set

To complement the new typography, we have also updated our default icon set. We have replaced the Material Icons font with the new [Material Symbols](https://blazor.radzen.com/icon) variable font containing more than 2,500 glyphs. This change brings a more cohesive and flexible icon set to your apps for a modern and consistent visual language.

<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-material-symbols-icons.png" alt="Material Symbols in Radzen Blazor Components" style="display: block; border-radius: 12px; margin: 40px auto; max-width: 600px; border: 1px solid #ccc;" loading="lazy">

## And More
As a major version, v5 brings updates across the board - from dependencies and markup fixes to properties and naming conventions. Below is a preview of the updated Advanced Filtering buttons in Radzen DataGrid - one of many improvements introduced in v5 of Radzen Blazor Components. See all in the [Changelog](https://blazor.radzen.com/changelog).
<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-datagrid-filtering-update.png" alt="Radzen Blazor DataGrid Filtering" style="display: block; border-radius: 12px; margin: 40px auto; border: 1px solid #ccc;" loading="lazy">

## Radzen.Blazor 5.0 in Radzen Blazor Studio

When migrating to Radzen.Blazor 5.0 you are likely to experience appearance issues. Those happen because the browser loads a cached (thus old) version of the theme CSS files. If you are using a [free theme](/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/themes-and-swatches#free-themes) just clear your browser cache to force loading the latest CSS file. If you are using a [premium theme](/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/themes-and-swatches#premium-themes) you have to reapply the theme in [Radzen Blazor Studio](/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/themes-and-swatches#change-application-theme) in order to update it: simply change to any other theme and then back to the one you were using.

# Radzen Blazor Components v7.0 released!

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/radzen-blazor-components-v7-released.md

# Radzen Blazor Components v7.0 released!

> We’re thrilled to announce a major milestone: Radzen Blazor Components v7.0 is here!

We’re thrilled to announce a major milestone: **[Radzen Blazor Components v7.0](https://blazor.radzen.com)** is here! 🚀
This release brings **performance boosts**, **enhanced UI animations**, a **powerful new expression parser**, and key component upgrades - all designed to make your Blazor apps smoother, faster, and more flexible than ever.

## What’s New in Radzen Blazor Components v7.0.0

### Lean and Mean

- Removed the `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis` dependency - now powered by our own **C# expression parser** for better performance and reliability.
- Introduced `ToFilterString()` to expose DataGrid filters as valid C# expression strings.

### Smooth Animations

- Added **polished animations** across core components like:
  - `Popup`
  - `Dialog`
  - `DropDown`
  - `Tooltip`
  - `Panel`
  - `Accordion`
  - ...and more

### Faster Rendering

- Significant rendering optimizations across multiple components.
- `RadioButtonList` and `CheckBoxList` now offer new rendering options with flexible item alignment.
- `Scheduler`’s Month View now intelligently handles overlapping appointments on a per-week basis.

### Improved Accessibility

- `SelectBar`, `RadioButtonList`, and `CheckBoxList` now share a single tab stop for improved keyboard navigation and accessibility.

# Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio Plugin

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/radzen-blazor-for-visual-studio-plugin.md

# Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio Plugin

> Announcing the Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio plugin

Hi all! We have some exciting news to share.

You may have noticed one [particular](/blazor-studio/documentation/roadmap#visual-studio-plugin) item buried in the Radzen Blazor Studio roadmap - the Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio plugin.
This blog post would finally reveal the curtain.

## What is the Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio plugin
Lots of developers use [Radzen Blazor Studio](/blazor-studio) side by side with Visual Studio. They just feel so cozy in the beloved Microsoft IDE and
don't want to use a third party tool for coding and debugging. Still Radzen Blazor Studio adds tons of features to help with Blazor development so one has no other choice but to switch between the two.

The Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio plugin (the name is TBD) aims to solve that. We plan to make all Radzen Blazor Studio features available right inside Visual Studio 2022!

Here is an animated gif showing the current state of our work:
<img src="images/blog/radzen-visual-studio.gif" alt="Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio - preview of available functionality" loading="lazy">

## Is this a new product
Although it is a new development we don't plan to make it a new product (as in a new SKU). It will be available as a download for all Radzen Blazor Studio subscribers ([Professional](/pricing), [Enterprise](/pricing) and
grandfathered Radzen Studio). It will even use the same license key.

## What will the plugin support
The plan is to support the following features that are available today in [Radzen Blazor Studio](/blazor-studio):

- WYSIWYG design time support for existing and new Blazor applications - component toolbox, drag and drop, property grid.
- Support for creating new applications that use the Radzen.Blazor component library.
- Various data source support - databases, REST, OData.
- Page scaffolding - CRUD, security etc.
- Radzen.Blazor visual theme customization.

## Which versions of Visual Studio will be supported
The plugin supports Visual Studio 2022.

## ETA
We intend to release the plugin in phases. The first phase will include the WYSIWYG design time support only. We expect to ship a preview version of it this fall!

## What does that mean for Radzen Blazor Studio
Our commitment with Radzen Blazor Studio remains as strong as always! We consider the Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio plugin as a complementary feature of Radzen Blazor Studio so it isn't going anywhere.
Both tools share a significant amount of features and implementation so they will evolve together.

Are you excited? Feel free to share feedback and questions in the [new category](https://forum.radzen.com/c/vs-plugin/14) of our community forum.

---

# New PickList Component

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/radzen-blazor-picklist-component.md

# New PickList Component

> The PickList component simplifies selection processes by easily transferring items between two collections.

The PickList component simplifies selection processes by easily transferring items between two collections.

You can configure PickList’s orientation, buttons’ layout and appearance. The component also supports source and destination list headers, filtering, and multiple selection.

<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-picklist-component.png" alt="Radzen Blazor Components - PickList Component" loading="lazy">

[See PickList demo](https://blazor.radzen.com/picklist)

# Radzen Blazor Studio is now providing support for OData services

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/radzen-blazor-studio-is-now-providing-support-for-odata-services.md

# Radzen Blazor Studio is now providing support for OData services

> OData - the best way to REST.

The Open Data Protocol (OData) is a popular method of exposing a database as a REST API.

<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-studio-odata-data-source.png" alt="Radzen Blazor Studio - OData data source" style="margin-top: 80px;" loading="lazy">

Radzen Blazor Studio now offers exceptional support for OData services. It scaffolds service classes that can make HTTP requests to the OData service and, if necessary, authenticate them. Additionally, it generates model classes for all entities and various pages that facilitate the creation of a full CRUD application from the OData service.

[Learn more about OData](/blazor-studio/documentation/odata)

# Radzen Blazor Studio makes REST API integration a breeze

> Radzen Blazor Studio now supports REST API

We are excited to share that REST API support is now available!

With the new data source enhancements, you can seamlessly access your APIs, fetch data, and dive right into creating efficient applications.

<img src="images/blog/radzen-blazor-studio-data-sources.png" alt="Radzen Blazor Studio - Data sources" style="margin-top: 80px;" loading="lazy">

## REST API Integration Made Effortless

- Radzen Blazor Studio now allows you to connect to REST APIs in no time.
- It automates the process by scaffolding service classes, enabling HTTP requests to the REST API, and even handling optional authentication.
- Model classes for all entities returned by the REST API are generated automatically, saving you valuable time and effort.

## Why Choose Radzen Blazor Studio?

- **Speed up development:** The REST API support streamlines the integration process, making it faster and more efficient.
- **Code generation:** Radzen Blazor Studio automatically generates the necessary code, reducing errors and improving code quality.
- **Flexibility:** Customize your API calls and data handling as needed to create tailored solutions.

# Raising the standard with a new Standard theme for Radzen Blazor Components

Major distinctive features are:

- Improved visual hierarchy

- Optimized spacing

# Read image as base64 string using file input, JavaScript, Blazor (server-side) and SignalR

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/read-image-base64-blazor-signalr.md

# Read image as base64 string using file input, JavaScript, Blazor (server-side) and SignalR

> Read image as base64 string using file input, JavaScript, Blazor (server-side) and SignalR

While working on [Blazor prototype](/documentation/roadmap) for [Radzen](https://twitter.com/radzenhq/status/1051898691559325696) I've found a little trick how to enable quck image read as base64 string using `<input type="file" />`, JavaScript and SignalR.

1\. Create new Blazor (server-side) project.

![image](images/blog/UploadImageBlazor1.png)

2\. Define `readFileAsBase64` JavaScript function in your `index.html` to read the file input selected file as data url (base64 string):

![image](images/blog/UploadImageBlazor2.png)

```javascript
window.readFileAsBase64 = (fileInput) => {
	const readAsDataURL = (fileInput) => {
		return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
			const reader = new FileReader();
			reader.onerror = () => {
				reader.abort();
				reject(new Error("Error reading file.");
			};
			reader.addEventListener(""load"", () => {
				resolve(reader.result);
			}, false);
			reader.readAsDataURL(fileInput.files[0]);
		});
	};

	return readAsDataURL(fileInput);
};")

```
3\. Define file input and img HTML components to select and display the image and execute using JSRuntime `readFileAsBase64` function to read the image data:

![image](images/blog/UploadImageBlazor3.png)

```html
![@Picture](images/blog/@Picture)

<input ref="fileUpload" class="form-control" type="file"
       onchange="@(async (e) => Picture = await JSRuntime.Current.InvokeAsync<string>("readFileAsBase64", fileUpload))" />

@functions{
    ElementRef fileUpload;
    string Picture;
}

```

4\. By default SignalR buffer size is set to 13 kb and to enable read of bigger images go to server project `Startup.cs` and set ApplicationMaxBufferSize:

![image](images/blog/UploadImageBlazor4.png)

```cs
// This method gets called by the runtime. Use this method to configure the HTTP request pipeline.
public void Configure(IApplicationBuilder app, IHostingEnvironment env)
{
	...
	//app.UseServerSideBlazor<App.Startup>();

	// Set ApplicationMaxBufferSize to enable read of bigger images using JSRuntime. Default is 13 kb.
	app.UseSignalR(route => route.MapHub<BlazorHub>(BlazorHub.DefaultPath, options =>
	{
		options.ApplicationMaxBufferSize = 10 * 1024 * 1024;
	})).UseBlazor<App.Startup>();
}

```

5\. Run the application and select image:

![image](images/blog/UploadImageBlazor5.png)

![image](images/blog/UploadImageBlazor6.png)

[Source Code](https://github.com/radzenhq/radzen-examples/tree/master/UploadImagesBlazor)

Enjoy!

---

# Security for multitenant web applications with ASP.NET Core

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/security-for-multitenant-web-applications-with-aspnetcore.md

# Security for multitenant web applications with ASP.NET Core

> Security for multitenant web applications with ASP.NET Core

In this post I'm going to show you how to enable security per tenant for the multitenant web application created in [my previous blog post](/blog/creating-multitenant-web-applications-aspnetcore-angular).

1\. Create new application with .NET server-side project, add new MSSQL data-source connected to our Sample database and auto-generate pages.

![Multi Tenant1](images/blog/multi-tenant1.png)

2\. Run the application from Radzen to generate everything needed and add the following files to application ignore list to tell Radzen to ignore them during subsequent code generation.

```
client\src\environments\environment.ts
server\Program.cs
```

![Multi Tenant Security1](images/blog/multi-tenant-security1.png)

3\. Add the following __Multitenancy__ section in `server\appsettings.json` with information about tenants, their hostnames and connection strings. We specify two hostnames per tenant - one for debug mode (so you can test while developing the application) and one for production (which your users will browse).

```json
{
  ...
  "Multitenancy": {
    "Tenants": [
      {
        "Name": "Tenant1",
        "Hostnames": [
          "localhost:5001",
          "tenant1.radzen-rocks.com"
        ],
        "ConnectionString": "Server=.;Initial Catalog=Sample-Tenant1;Persist Security Info=False;User ID=sa;Password=yourpassword;MultipleActiveResultSets=False;Encrypt=false;TrustServerCertificate=true;Connection Timeout=30"
      },
      {
        "Name": "Tenant2",
        "Hostnames": [
          "localhost:5002",
          "tenant2.radzen-rocks.com"
        ],
        "ConnectionString": "Server=.;Initial Catalog=Sample-Tenant2;Persist Security Info=False;User ID=sa;Password=yourpassword;MultipleActiveResultSets=False;Encrypt=false;TrustServerCertificate=true;Connection Timeout=30"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

4\. Enable default security for the application and auto-generate pages for user and role management.

![Multi Tenant Security1.1](images/blog/multi-tenant-security1.1.png)

5\. Add `server\Data\SampleContext.Custom.cs` and `server\Data\ApplicationIdentityDbContext.Custom.cs` with the following code to read the tenants.

**SampleContext.Custom.cs**
```cs
public partial class SampleContext
{
    private readonly HttpContext context;
    private readonly Multitenancy multitenancy;

    public SampleContext(DbContextOptions<SampleContext> options, ApplicationIdentityDbContext identityDbContext, IHttpContextAccessor httpContextAccessor, Multitenancy mt) : base(options)
    {
        context = httpContextAccessor.HttpContext;
        multitenancy = mt;
        Database.EnsureCreated();
        identityDbContext.Database.Migrate();
    }

    public SampleContext(IHttpContextAccessor httpContextAccessor, Multitenancy mt, ApplicationIdentityDbContext identityDbContext)
    {
        context = httpContextAccessor.HttpContext;
        multitenancy = mt;
        Database.EnsureCreated();
        identityDbContext.Database.Migrate();
    }

    protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder optionsBuilder)
    {
        if (multitenancy != null && context != null)
        {
            var tenant = multitenancy.Tenants
                    .Where(t => t.Hostnames.Contains(context.Request.Host.Value)).FirstOrDefault();

            if (tenant != null)
            {
                optionsBuilder.UseSqlServer(tenant.ConnectionString);
            }
        }
    }
}

```

**ApplicationIdentityDbContext.Custom.cs**
```cs
public partial class ApplicationIdentityDbContext
{
    private readonly HttpContext context;
    private readonly Multitenancy multitenancy;

    public ApplicationIdentityDbContext(DbContextOptions<ApplicationIdentityDbContext> options, IHttpContextAccessor httpContextAccessor, Multitenancy mt) : base(options)
    {
        context = httpContextAccessor.HttpContext;
        multitenancy = mt;
    }

    public ApplicationIdentityDbContext(IHttpContextAccessor httpContextAccessor, Multitenancy mt)
    {
        context = httpContextAccessor.HttpContext;
        multitenancy = mt;
    }

    protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder optionsBuilder)
    {
        if (multitenancy != null && context != null)
        {
            var tenant = multitenancy.Tenants
                    .Where(t => t.Hostnames.Contains(context.Request.Host.Value)).FirstOrDefault();

            if (tenant != null)
            {
                optionsBuilder.UseSqlServer(tenant.ConnectionString);
            }
        }
    }
}

```

6\. Add `UseUrls()` to `server\Program.cs` to specify the urls the web host will listen on for each tenant in debug mode.

```cs
public class Program
{
    public static void Main(string[] args)
    {
        var host = BuildWebHost(args);

        host.Run();
    }

    public static IWebHost BuildWebHost(string[] args) =>
        WebHost.CreateDefaultBuilder(args)
            .UseKestrel()
            .UseUrls("http://localhost:5001", "http://localhost:5002"
            .UseStartup<Startup>()
            .Build();
}")

```

7\. Specify Angular application data services url for default tenant for debug (`client\src\environments\environment.ts`).

**client\src\environments\environment.ts** - for debug
```js
export function dataSourceRoot(): string {
  return 'http://localhost:5001';
}

export const environment = {
  sample: `${dataSourceRoot()}/odata/Sample`,
  securityUrl: `${dataSourceRoot()}/auth`,
  production: false,
};
```

8\. Run the application from Radzen and login using `admin/admin` to access __Tenant1__ database. You can now create roles and users for __Tenant1__.

![Multi Tenant Security2](images/blog/multi-tenant-security2.png)
![Multi Tenant Security3](images/blog/multi-tenant-security3.png)

9\. Modify `.env` and `client\src\environments\environment.ts` to set default tenant to __Tenant2__.

**.env**
```
ConnectionStrings__SampleConnection="Server=.;Initial Catalog=Sample-Tenant2;Persist Security Info=False;User ID=sa;Password=pwd;MultipleActiveResultSets=False;Encrypt=false;TrustServerCertificate=true;Connection Timeout=30"

```

**client\src\environments\environment.ts**
```js
export function dataSourceRoot(): string {
  return 'http://localhost:5002';
}
...
```

10\. Run the application and login using `admin/admin` to access __Tenant2__ database and add roles and users for __Tenant2__.

![Multi Tenant Security4](images/blog/multi-tenant-security4.png)

You have now separate security for each tenant!

![Multi Tenant Security5](images/blog/multi-tenant-security5.png)

Both __ApplicationIdentityDbContext__ and __SampleDataContext__ will retrieve runtime the tenant connection string depending on the application host:

![Multi Tenant Security6](images/blog/multi-tenant-security6.png)

To deploy the application please follow the instructions in [my previous blog post](/blog/creating-multitenant-web-applications-aspnetcore-angular).

[Source Code](https://github.com/radzenhq/radzen-examples/tree/master/SampleMultiTenant)

Enjoy!

# Send an email with Angular, .NET Core and Radzen

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/send-email-with-angular-and-dotnetcore.md

# Send an email with Angular, .NET Core and Radzen

> Send an email with Angular, .NET Core and Radzen

This blog post demonstrates how to invoke POST request from an Angular 5 application to .NET Core 2.x Web API controller and send an email using System.Net.Mail.SmtpClient.

1.Create new Radzen application with .NET Core 2.x server-side project, add new empty page and set new `mailMessage` property on __Page__ __Load__ event to empty object:
![image](images/blog/send-email1.png)
![image](images/blog/send-email2.png)
![image](images/blog/send-email3.png)

2.Design your email form using [Rows and Columns](/documentation/design-time) and set `mailMessage` respective property on every input component change:
![image](images/blog/send-email4.png)

3.Add new Button component at the end of the email form and execute `(<any>this).sendEmail(this.mailMessage)` on __Button__ __Click__ event
![image](images/blog/send-email5.png)

4.Run the application to generate Angular and .NET Core apps and add the following code to `client/send-email.component.ts` and `server/SendMailController.cs` similar to [Invoke custom server-side method article](/documentation/custom-controller):

## client/send-email.component.ts

```ts
import { Component, Injector } from '@angular/core';
import { SendEmailGenerated } from './send-email-generated.component';

// Import HttpClient and HttpParams which are needed to make HTTP calls.
import { HttpClient, HttpHeaders } from '@angular/common/http';
// Import the environment to get the server URL
import { environment } from '../../environments/environment';

@Component({
  selector: 'send-email',
  templateUrl: './send-email.component.html'
})
export class SendEmailComponent extends SendEmailGenerated {
  constructor(injector: Injector, private http: HttpClient) {
    super(injector);
  }

  sendEmail(mailMessage: any) {
    let headers = new HttpHeaders();

    headers = headers.set('Accept', 'application/json');

    if (mailMessage) {
      headers = headers.set('Content-Type', 'application/json');
    }

    this.http.post(`http://localhost:5000/api/mail/sendmail`, mailMessage, {
      headers
    }).subscribe(result => {
      console.log("Email sent!";
    });

  }
}")

```

## server/SendMailController.cs

```cs
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;

namespace Sample.Controllers
{
    public class Email
    {
        public string To { get; set; }
        public string Cc { get; set; }
        public string Subject { get; set; }
        public string Text { get; set; }
    }

    [Route("api/[controller]/[action]"]
    public class MailController : Controller
    {
        [HttpPost]
        public async Task<IActionResult> SendMail([FromBody]Email email)
        {
            var client = new System.Net.Mail.SmtpClient(""smtp.example.com"", 111);
            client.UseDefaultCredentials = false;
            client.EnableSsl = true;

            client.Credentials = new System.Net.NetworkCredential(""yourusername"", ""yourpassword"");

            var mailMessage = new System.Net.Mail.MailMessage();
            mailMessage.From = new System.Net.Mail.MailAddress(""youremail@example.com"");

            mailMessage.To.Add(email.To);

            if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(email.Cc))
            {
                mailMessage.CC.Add(email.Cc);
            }

            mailMessage.Body = email.Text;

            mailMessage.Subject = email.Subject;

            mailMessage.BodyEncoding = System.Text.Encoding.UTF8;
            mailMessage.SubjectEncoding = System.Text.Encoding.UTF8;

            await client.SendMailAsync(mailMessage);

            return Ok();
        }
    }
}")

```

5.Run the application, compose your email and send it:
![image](images/blog/send-email6.png)

Enjoy!

# Smarter Code Editing in Radzen Blazor Studio

# Smarter Code Editing in Radzen Blazor Studio

> Radzen Blazor Studio gets Go to Definition, Rename Symbol, Find All References, smarter Razor editing, and a richer CSS workflow - built for how Blazor developers actually work.

A big upgrade is coming to [Radzen Blazor Studio](/blazor-studio).

The next release brings a wave of code editor features built around how Blazor developers actually work - so you can write code faster, navigate projects more easily, and stay focused from first component to final build.

If you haven't tried Radzen Blazor Studio yet, this is the right time to take a look. It's becoming an even more powerful Blazor IDE for developers who want speed, clarity, and productivity in one place.

<img src="images/blog/editor-context-menu.png" alt="Peek Definition in the Radzen Blazor Studio code editor" style="border-radius: 12px; width: 80%; margin: 3rem auto;" loading="lazy" />

## New in C# and Razor Files

The Radzen Blazor Studio editor is getting a major productivity boost with powerful navigation, refactoring, and editing improvements.

### Navigate your code instantly

- **Go to Definition** (F12): Jump straight to any symbol, including symbols from referenced NuGet packages.
- **Peek Definition**: View a definition inline without leaving your current file.
- **Find All References**: See every usage of a symbol across your project, displayed in an inline peek window.
- **Go to Implementation**: Move from an interface directly to the classes that implement it.

### Refactor with confidence

- **Rename Symbol**: Safely rename a type, method, or property everywhere it appears - across your entire project.
- **Reference counts**: See how many references each method has, right above the signature. Click once to expand the full list inline.

### Find anything, fast

- **Outline view** (Ctrl+Shift+O): See every type and member in the current file at a glance.
- **Project-wide symbol search** (Ctrl+T): Find any class, method, or property by name - instantly.

<img src="images/blog/editor-outline-view.png" alt="Outline view in Radzen Blazor Studio showing types and members" style="border-radius: 12px; width: 80%; margin: 3rem auto;" loading="lazy" />

### Write Razor more naturally

- Edit a Razor tag and its matching tag updates automatically.
- Tags close themselves as you type.
- Every occurrence of a symbol highlights when your cursor lands on it.
- **Format Document** and **Format on Type** keep your code clean without manual effort.
- Compiler-accurate syntax highlighting with refreshed dark and light themes.

## New in CSS and HTML Files

- **Live validation** with errors and quick fixes.
- **Hover documentation** for every property and selector.
- **Color pickers** in the gutter - pick colors visually without leaving the editor.
- **Outline, folding, rename, Go to Definition, Find References**, and **document formatting**.
- **Clickable links** for @@import, href, and src - jump to the target with a single click.

All of this works inside `<style>` blocks in your .razor files too.

<img src="images/blog/css-documentation.png" alt="CSS hover documentation in Radzen Blazor Studio" style="border-radius: 12px; width: 80%; margin: 3rem auto;" loading="lazy" />

These improvements make [Radzen Blazor Studio](/blazor-studio) an even stronger choice for Blazor development - with smarter code navigation, safer refactoring, better Razor editing, and a richer CSS workflow built right in.

# Testing Angular 2 apps with Webpack and mocha

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/testing-angular-webpack-mocha.md

# Testing Angular 2 apps with Webpack and mocha

> Testing Angular 2 applications with Webpack and the Mocha test runner. Comparison with karma.

Checkout [Radzen Demos](/demos) and [download latest Radzen](/download)!

Unit tests are a first class citizen in Angular 2. The officially recommended test runner is Karma and
the testing library is Jasmine. Karma executes unit tests in a browser (sometimes a headless one such as PhantomJS).
Thus unit tests run in a close to real-world environment.

In this blog post I will show you a different approach to running tests - with Mocha, Chai and Sinon.
Mocha has a test runner which works with Node and does not need a browser. We need Chai and sinon because Mocha does not include
assertion and mocking libraries. We will use Webpack for bundling and module loading.

## Setup

We need a simple Angular 2 Webpack application. Let's use the one from the [official Webpack introduction](https://angular.io/docs/ts/latest/guide/webpack.html).

Then we need to install some npm packages:

- mocha (test runner)
- mocha-webpack (build the tests with Webpack before running them)
- chai (assertion library)
- @@types/chai (TypeScript definitions for chai)
- sinon (mocking library)
- @@types/sinon (TypeScript definitions for sinon)
- webpack-node-externals (exclude server-side node modules from the build)
- jsdom (provides stubs for DOM API required by Angular - HTMLElement, XMLHttpRequest)

```
npm install --save-dev mocha mocha-webpack chai @@types/chai sinon @@types/sinon webpack-node-externals jsdom
```

## Add some tests

Modify the AppComponent from the Webpack introduction tutorial to implement a few simple tasks.

### src/app/app.component.ts
```ts
import { Component } from '@@angular/core';

@@Component({
  selector: 'my-app',
  template: require('./app.component.html')
})
export class AppComponent {
  value = 0;

  onIncrementClick() {
    this.value = Math.min(100, ++this.value);
  }

  onDecrementClick() {
    this.value = Math.max(-100, --this.value);
  }
}
```

### src/app/app.component.html

```html
<main>
  <h2>Value: {{ value }}</h2>
  <button class="increment" (click)="onIncrementClick()">+</button>
  <button class="decrement" (click)="onDecrementClick()">-</button>
</main>

```

Add tests for those tasks.

### src/app/app.component.spec.ts

```ts
import { getTestBed, TestBed } from '@angular/core/testing';
import { AppComponent } from './app.component';
import { By } from '@angular/platform-browser';
import { expect } from 'chai';
import { spy } from 'sinon';

describe(`AppComponent ${i}`, () => {
  beforeEach(() => {
    TestBed.configureTestingModule({
      declarations: [AppComponent]
    });
  });

  afterEach(() => {
    getTestBed().resetTestingModule();
  });

  it('should display 0 as initial value', () => {
    const fixture = TestBed.createComponent(AppComponent);

    fixture.detectChanges();

    const h2 = fixture.debugElement.query(By.css('h2'));

    expect(h2.nativeElement.textContent).to.equal('Value: 0');
  });

  it('should increment the value', () => {
    const fixture = TestBed.createComponent(AppComponent);

    fixture.componentInstance.onIncrementClick();

    fixture.detectChanges();

    const h2 = fixture.debugElement.query(By.css('h2'));

    expect(h2.nativeElement.textContent).to.equal('Value: 1');
  });

  it('should invoke onIncrementClick when the user clicks the increment button', () => {
    const fixture = TestBed.createComponent(AppComponent);

    const onIncrementClick = spy(fixture.componentInstance, 'onIncrementClick');

    const button = fixture.debugElement.query(By.css('.increment'));

    button.triggerEventHandler('click', {});

    expect(onIncrementClick.called).to.equal(true);
  });

  /* snip */
});

```

There are a few differences with the Karma/Jasmine approach.

- We reset the testing module after each test because Zone.js does not support Mocha yet.
- Assertions are done with Chai: `expect(value).to.equal(true)` instead of `expect(value).toEqual(true)`.
- Mocking is done with Sinon.

## Run the tests

First we need to create e Webpack config file that will ignore Node server-side modules during packaging.

### config/webpack.mocha.js

```js
var webpackMerge = require('webpack-merge');
var nodeExternals = require('webpack-node-externals');

var commonConfig = require('./webpack.test');

module.exports = webpackMerge(commonConfig, {
  externals: [
    nodeExternals()
  ]
});
```

Then we need to create a shim file which will load all dependencies and configure Angular for testing. This
file is very similar to `karma-test-shim.js` from the official Webpack introduction tutorial.

### config/mocha-test-shim.js

```js
var jsdom = require('jsdom')

var document = jsdom.jsdom('<!doctype html><html><body></body></html>');

var window = document.defaultView;

global.document = document;
global.HTMLElement = window.HTMLElement;
global.XMLHttpRequest = window.XMLHttpRequest;

require('core-js/es6');
require('core-js/es7/reflect');

require('zone.js/dist/zone');
require('zone.js/dist/long-stack-trace-zone');
require('zone.js/dist/proxy');
require('zone.js/dist/sync-test');
require('zone.js/dist/async-test');
require('zone.js/dist/fake-async-test');

var testing = require('@angular/core/testing');
var browser = require('@angular/platform-browser-dynamic/testing');

testing.TestBed.initTestEnvironment(browser.BrowserDynamicTestingModule, browser.platformBrowserDynamicTesting());

```

The biggest difference is that we are using `jsdom` to provide stubs for a few DOM APIs that Angular 2 needs.

We also need a configuration file for `mocha-webpack` in order to avoid passing all options through command line.

### mocha-webpack.opts

```
--webpack-config config/webpack.mocha.js
--require config/mocha-test-shim.js
src/**/*.spec.ts
```

The first line specifies the Webpack config file, the second line includes the shim and the last line specifies where the test files are.

Finally we can update the npm test scripts in `package.json` to run our tests with `mocha-webpack`.

```json
"scripts": {
  "test": "mocha-webpack",
  "test:watch": "mocha-webpack --watch"
}
```

Running the tests is as simple as `npm test`. To run them in watch mode use `npm run test:watch`.

## Compared to Karma

Let's compare the test running time of Karma and Mocha. The [angular2-webpack-mocha](https://github.com/akorchev/angular2-webpack-mocha) github repo is a sample application configured
for both Karma and Mocha. Here are the results of running the tests 10 times:

![image](images/blog/karma-mocha.png)

Mocha is more than one second faster than Karma. Running the tests 100 times show 15-20% improvement over Karma.

Testing in watch mode also feels snappier with Mocha.

### Mocha
![image](images/blog/mocha-watch.gif)

### Karma
![image](images/blog/karma-watch.gif)

# Using GitHub Copilot with Radzen Blazor Studio

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/using-github-copilot-with-radzen-blazor-studio.md

# Using GitHub Copilot with Radzen Blazor Studio

> Radzen Blazor Studio is the only Blazor IDE with built-in GitHub Copilot support. Here's how AI-assisted autocomplete works inside the visual designer's code editor - and why it matters for your Blazor workflow.

AI coding agents have changed how developers write code. GitHub Copilot alone is used by millions of developers worldwide, suggesting entire blocks of code as you type. But until now, using Copilot with Blazor meant working exclusively in Visual Studio or VS Code - outside of any visual design environment.

**Radzen Blazor Studio** changes that. It's the first and only Blazor development environment with native GitHub Copilot integration, combining AI-assisted coding with a visual designer, 110+ UI components (as of March 2026), and full project management - all in one tool.

## What Copilot Does Inside Radzen Blazor Studio

When you enable GitHub Copilot in Radzen Blazor Studio, you get real-time, context-aware code suggestions directly in the code editor. Copilot understands your project structure and adapts to your coding patterns across C#, Razor, and JavaScript files.

<img src="images/blog/copilot-autocomplete-in-radzen-blazor-studio.gif" alt="GitHub Copilot autocomplete working in Radzen Blazor Studio" style="border-radius: 12px;" loading="lazy" />

This means you can:

- Get AI-powered completions while writing event handlers, data binding expressions, and component configuration
- Generate boilerplate code for common Blazor patterns - form validation, data grid columns, dialog workflows
- Receive suggestions that are aware of the Radzen Blazor component API, so completions reference actual component properties and events
- Switch seamlessly between the visual designer and the code editor without losing AI assistance

The key difference from using Copilot in a general-purpose editor is context. Radzen Blazor Studio knows your application's data sources, pages, components, and layout. Copilot benefits from that context when generating suggestions.

## How to Enable It

Setting up Copilot takes less than a minute:

1. Open **Settings** (bottom-left corner) and navigate to **Development → Copilot**
2. Toggle **Enable Copilot**
3. Follow the on-screen instructions to authenticate with your GitHub account
4. Restart Radzen Blazor Studio

<img src="images/blazor-studio/documentation/enable-copilot-in-radzen-blazor-studio.png" alt="Enable GitHub Copilot in Radzen Blazor Studio settings" style="border-radius: 12px; max-width: 70%;" loading="lazy" />

After authentication, Copilot suggestions appear inline as you type. Press **Tab** to accept a suggestion, or keep typing to dismiss it. You stay in full control of every line.

> This functionality requires a GitHub account with an active [Copilot subscription](https://github.com/features/copilot).

<img src="images/blazor-studio/documentation/copilot-enabled-in-radzen-blazor-studio.png" alt="GitHub Copilot enabled in Radzen Blazor Studio" style="border-radius: 12px; max-width: 70%;" loading="lazy" />

## Why It Matters: Visual Design Meets AI Coding

Blazor developers have traditionally had to choose between two workflows: a visual, drag-and-drop approach for UI layout, or a code-first approach with AI assistance. Radzen Blazor Studio eliminates that tradeoff.

You can design a page visually using the WYSIWYG designer, configure components through the property panel, and then switch to the code editor where Copilot helps you write the business logic - all within the same environment. No context switching between tools, no copy-pasting between windows.

This is particularly powerful for common Blazor development tasks:

**DataGrid configuration** - Drag a RadzenDataGrid onto your page, bind it to a data source visually, then let Copilot help you write custom column templates, filter logic, or export handlers.

**Form building** - Use the designer to lay out form fields with RadzenFormField, then switch to code where Copilot suggests validation rules, submit handlers, and error messaging.

**Event handling** - Wire up component events through the property panel, then let Copilot generate the implementation based on your project context.

## What's Next: The Radzen AI Story

GitHub Copilot integration is one part of a broader AI strategy at Radzen. Here's what's available today and what's coming:

- **GitHub Copilot in Radzen Blazor Studio** - available now, as described in this post
- **[RadzenAIChat](https://blazor.radzen.com/aichat)** - a Blazor component for embedding conversational AI in your applications, with built-in memory and OpenAI compatibility
- **AI Agent in Radzen Blazor Studio** - coming in 2026, a built-in agent that assists with component selection, UI layout generation, and development workflows
- **[Radzen Blazor MCP Server](/blazor-mcp)** - gives AI coding agents like Cursor, Claude Code, and GitHub Copilot live access to the Radzen Blazor component library

Radzen is building toward a development experience where visual design, hand-written code, and AI assistance work together - not as separate tools, but as integrated parts of the same workflow.

## Get Started

If you're already using GitHub Copilot, enabling it in Radzen Blazor Studio takes less than a minute. If you're not yet using Radzen, [download Radzen Blazor Studio](/blazor-studio/download) and try the free trial - Copilot support is included.

[Try Radzen Blazor Studio](/blazor-studio)

[Read the Copilot documentation](/blazor-studio/documentation/github-copilot)

[Explore Radzen Blazor Components](https://blazor.radzen.com)

# Visually design Blazor application

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/visually-design-blazor-application.md

# Visually design Blazor application

> Visually design Blazor application.

In this blog post I'm going to show you how to use the powerful Radzen designer to visually design your Blazor application.

1\. Create new Blazor project, add our __Sample__ data source and add new empty page.

![Visually Design Blazor1](images/blog/visually-design-blazor1.png)
![Visually Design Blazor2](images/blog/visually-design-blazor2.png)
![Visually Design Blazor3](images/blog/visually-design-blazor3.png)
![Visually Design Blazor4](images/blog/visually-design-blazor4.png)

2\. Drop __DataGrid__ component from the toolbox and bind it to __Sample__ `Products`.

![Visually Design Blazor5](images/blog/visually-design-blazor5.png)
![Visually Design Blazor6](images/blog/visually-design-blazor6.png)
![Visually Design Blazor7](images/blog/visually-design-blazor7.png)
![Visually Design Blazor8](images/blog/visually-design-blazor8.png)

3\. Edit `Product Picture` __DataGrid__ column using the template designer and add new __Image__ component bound to `${data.ProductPicture}`. Set `Width` property to `100px`.

![Visually Design Blazor9](images/blog/visually-design-blazor9.png)
![Visually Design Blazor10](images/blog/visually-design-blazor10.png)
![Visually Design Blazor11](images/blog/visually-design-blazor11.png)
![Visually Design Blazor12](images/blog/visually-design-blazor12.png)

4\. Add new column to the __DataGrid__, drop a __Button__ component with `delete` icon in column template and invoke `deleteProduct` data source method. Execute the grid `Reload()` method after delete.

![Visually Design Blazor13](images/blog/visually-design-blazor13.png)
![Visually Design Blazor14](images/blog/visually-design-blazor14.png)
![Visually Design Blazor15](images/blog/visually-design-blazor15.png)
![Visually Design Blazor16](images/blog/visually-design-blazor16.png)

5\. Add new `Add Product` page, drop a __Button__ component on `Products` page, set `Text` to `Add Product` and navigate to `Add Product` on `Click`.

![Visually Design Blazor17](images/blog/visually-design-blazor17.png)
![Visually Design Blazor18](images/blog/visually-design-blazor18.png)
![Visually Design Blazor19](images/blog/visually-design-blazor19.png)

Let's design now `Add Product` page.

6\. Open `Add Product` page, add new Page __Load__ event and set new `product` property of type `Product` to `new Product()`.

![Visually Design Blazor20](images/blog/visually-design-blazor20.png)

7\. Drop __TemplateForm__ to `Add Product` page and bind it to `product` Page property.

![Visually Design Blazor21](images/blog/visually-design-blazor21.png)

8\. Drop __Row__ with two __Columns__ in the __TemplateForm__. Add __Label__ in the first column and __TextBox__ in the second with __Name__ property set to `ProductName`.

![Visually Design Blazor22](images/blog/visually-design-blazor22.png)

9\. Duplicate the first row, change the __Label__ Text, remove the __TextBox__ and add __Numeric__ with __Name__ set to `ProductPrice`.

![Visually Design Blazor23](images/blog/visually-design-blazor23.png)
![Visually Design Blazor24](images/blog/visually-design-blazor24.png)

10\. Duplicate the second row, change the __Label__ Text, remove the __Numeric__ and add __FileInput__ with __Name__ set to `ProductPicture`.

![Visually Design Blazor25](images/blog/visually-design-blazor25.png)

11\. Invoke `createProduct` with `product` property as parameter on __TemplateForm__ `Submit` event.

![Visually Design Blazor26](images/blog/visually-design-blazor26.png)

12\. Run the application and you will see the Radzen DataGrid component data-bound to the Products table of the Sample database. Click Add Product button to add new product and click delete button to delete existing products.

![Visually Design Blazor27](images/blog/visually-design-blazor27.png)
![Visually Design Blazor28](images/blog/visually-design-blazor28.png)
![Visually Design Blazor29](images/blog/visually-design-blazor29.png)

Congratulations! You've just visually designed a fully functional Blazor application without writing any code.

![Visually Design Blazor30](images/blog/visually-design-blazor30.png)

Enjoy!

# We Rebuilt Our Website with Blazor - Here's Why (and How)

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blog/we-rebuilt-our-website-with-blazor-heres-why-and-how.md

# We Rebuilt Our Website with Blazor - Here's Why (and How)

> We decided it was time to practice what we preach. We rebuilt our entire website with Blazor. And yes, it now runs entirely on the same tech we develop and support every day.

Over the past, we’ve had a recurring question from our community:
**“Why isn’t your website built with Blazor?”**

A fair question - especially since everything we offer is built around Blazor:

- **[Free Radzen Blazor Components](https://blazor.radzen.com)**
- **[Radzen Blazor Studio](/blazor-studio)**, our visual development environment for building Blazor apps
- **[Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio](/blazor-visual-studio)**, the extension that streamlines Blazor development within the Visual Studio environment.

So, we decided it was time to practice what we preach. We rebuilt our entire website with **Blazor**. And yes, it now runs entirely on the same tech we develop and support every day.

Here is a preview of the site on different screen sizes with the premium [Fluent Dark theme](/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/themes-and-swatches). You can use the theme picker in the site navigation to preview all themes.

<img src="images/blog/responsive-razden-blazor-website-fluent-dark-theme.png" alt="Responsive Radzen Blazor website featuring Fluent Dark theme" style="border-radius: 12px;" loading="lazy" />

## Why We Made the Switch

Blazor has matured into a capable, production-ready framework. While our legacy site worked well enough, it wasn’t showing what Blazor can really do - especially when paired with our components and tools.

We wanted:
- A better reflection of our product and ecosystem
- A real-world use case to improve our components
- To answer the “why not Blazor?” question with a working example

## What We Used

We rebuilt the site using Blazor WebAssembly with server prerendering.

This gives us the best of both worlds:
- Performant client-side experience thanks to Blazor WASM
- Initial HTML rendered on the server, which improves SEO and perceived load speed
- Seamless transition to full interactivity once the WASM app loads

Naturally, we used [Radzen Blazor Components](https://blazor.radzen.com) across the board - for UI, layout, forms and navigation.

## What We Learned

Rebuilding our website wasn’t just a branding decision - it was an opportunity to put our tools under real pressure.

Some things we discovered along the way:

#### Polish matters
A public-facing site demands attention to design and performance - great motivation for tightening up component behavior like the animations that we introduced in [Radzen Blazor Components v7.0](/blog/radzen-blazor-components-v7-released).

#### Blazor is ready
From routing to layout, Blazor handled everything with stability and flexibility.

#### Found bugs and fixed them
A great side benefit! We discovered edge cases in our own components and addressed them immediately.

#### Shipped two new components
- **[RadzenToc](https://blazor.radzen.com/toc)** for in-page navigation
- **[RadzenMarkdown](https://blazor.radzen.com/markdown)** for rendering Markdown content in Blazor apps.

## The Result

What you see now is the result of building in Blazor with the same tools we offer you:

- Improved site responsiveness
- Cleaner, more maintainable codebase
- Real-world testing ground for Radzen products

## Going Forward

We’re proud to say the site is finally aligned with our mission: Building Blazor apps should be a zen experience - empowering developers to create first-class web apps that look beautiful and work on every screen size.

If you’ve been on the fence about going all-in on Blazor, consider this our challenge to you. It’s ready. And if you’re using [Radzen Blazor Studio](/blazor-studio), you’re already halfway there.

Radzen remains one of the most active, developer-driven ecosystems in the Blazor world, powered by passionate developers who love building production-grade applications.

## Radzen Blazor Components

This year’s component updates focused on visual polish, performance, and interactivity - delivering more flexibility and speed for Blazor developers.

A release focused on refinement and smoother user experiences.

- **Animations Everywhere** - Popup, Dialog, DropDown, Tooltip, Panel, and Accordion now feature modern transitions.
- **Custom Expression Parser** - replaced the Roslyn dependency for faster, leaner, and more reliable evaluation.

The Skeleton component introduces modern loading placeholders that improve perceived performance and user experience. It’s available in text, rectangular, and circular variants with Pulse and Wave animations.

Try it on the [RadzenSkeleton demo](https://blazor.radzen.com/skeleton).

Two lightweight content components that simplify layout and documentation:

- PivotDataGrid - Dynamic pivot tables for in-app data aggregation.

- Performance enhancements throughout.

A flexible, real-time communication component designed for internal tools, support dashboards, and collaboration interfaces.

# Radzen Blazor Studio - Visual Blazor App Builder with AI Agent Support

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-studio.md

> Build Blazor apps visually, with code, or with AI agents. Radzen Blazor Studio works with Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, Gemini, and more - and its built-in MCP server lets your agent scaffold pages, edit components, and manage themes in your project.

# Radzen Blazor Studio: Build Visually, with Code, or with AI

Radzen Blazor Studio is a development environment where visual design, code, and AI agents work together. Use a WYSIWYG designer, CRUD scaffolding, 145+ UI components, and AI coding agents like Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, and Gemini - all in one place.

**Connect Data -**

## Unlock the Full Potential of Your Data

### Experience the power of data integration.

Want to work with REST services? Radzen Blazor Studio integrates with REST APIs, giving you the flexibility to incorporate external data sources effortlessly into your applications.

[Consuming REST API ↗](/blazor-studio/documentation/rest)

Quickly connect to your database - MSSQL, MySQL, SQLite, Oracle or PostgreSQL.

Radzen Blazor Studio simplifies common procedures related to database data. Whether it's querying, updating, or managing data, Radzen Blazor Studio provides a straightforward approach that doesn't require you to dive deep into C# intricacies.

See how to [build an internal app from your database](/build-internal-app-from-database).

[See Database Docs ↗](/blazor-studio/documentation/databases)

# &ldquo;

### Radzen allows users to visualize data from many sources easily without hard-core programming.

#### - Ken Draper, Software Specialist at NIAD Systems Inc.

**Design -**

## Unleash Your Creativity

### Deliver visually stunning and consistent user interfaces.

Visually edit pages and layouts by setting properties and adding new items or deleting existing ones. You have full control over application screens.

Intuitive drag and drop

Rich UI toolbox

Components’ inspector

[Design Time Docs ↗](/blazor-studio/documentation/design-time/introduction)

A set of 145+ components - open source and free for commercial use. The components are implemented in C# and take full advantage of the Blazor framework.

[See Demos ↗](https://blazor.radzen.com)

With Radzen Blazor Studio you can either customize components’ look & feel globally or simply tweak individual component instances where necessary.

Global styles are applied across the entire application, and are typically defined in a theme.

Radzen Blazor Studio features sets of free and premium themes including **Material 3** and **Fluent UI**.

Swatches are a premium feature of Radzen Blazor Studio. Each theme contains a collection of predefined color swatches to pick from, including **WCAG 2.2 AA** compliant and **High Contrast** ones.

[Learn more about Appearance ↗](/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/style-components)

Build amazing applications for any device by taking advantage of the fully-responsive layout capabilities.

Progressive Web App (PWA) support comes out of the box.

[Responsive Page Layout ↗](/blazor-studio/documentation/pages/responsive-page-layout)

**AI Coding Agents -**

## Build with AI, Your Way

### Use your preferred AI coding agent inside Radzen Blazor Studio - or connect it to the built-in MCP server.

However you prefer to build - visually, with code, or with AI - Radzen Blazor Studio supports your workflow. Use AI coding agents alongside the visual designer and code editor for a development experience no other Blazor IDE offers.

Claude Code

GitHub Copilot

Codex

Gemini

And more

AI agents also get built-in access to [Radzen Blazor MCP ↗](/blazor-mcp) for deep knowledge of every Radzen Blazor component.

Radzen Blazor Studio ships with a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server. Point an AI coding agent at the project you have open and ask, in plain language, for the changes you want. The agent works through the same design-time engine as the visual designer - so every edit is valid and type-checked, and you watch it land on the canvas right away.

Edit components with type-checked, structural edits

Switch themes and tune your brand colors

Connect data - infer a model from a database, import OpenAPI / OData, add REST services

Scaffold pages, layouts, authentication, and localization

Already chatting with an agent inside Radzen Blazor Studio? It's configured automatically - these steps are for connecting an agent you run outside the IDE, like a terminal CLI or another editor. See the [MCP server setup guide](/blazor-studio/documentation/mcp-server). Some capabilities, such as premium UI blocks and theme customization, require a license.

Try it in your own agent: ask it to "add a search box above the grid and switch to the dark theme" - and watch the change appear on the canvas.

**Develop -**

## Developers Love Radzen

### Radzen Blazor Studio provides tons of productivity gains for Blazor developers.

Radzen Blazor Studio is powered by popular open source technologies - ASP.NET Core, Blazor, Bootstrap, TypeScript.

The generated source code is human readable and you can build it with free tools.

Run your Radzen apps directly from Visual Studio Professional or Visual Studio Code.

The toolbox lists all Blazor components in the opened application - both third party and built-in ones. It also includes commonly used HTML elements such as div, p, button et al.

[Learn more ↗](/blazor-studio/documentation/design-time/components)

Use the built-in wizards and templates to facilitate common tasks such as data scaffolding and page creation.

Create Blazor Server and Blazor WebAssembly applications, supporting .NET 8, .NET 9, and .NET 10.

[See How ↗](/blazor-studio/documentation/applications)

Scaffold a complete CRUD application in a few steps and generate CRUD pages from a set of templates.

[See How ↗](/blazor-studio/documentation/databases)

Allow your users to create accounts, roles, sign in with passwords or Active Directory. Make parts of your applications accessible only to certain users.

ASP.NET Core Identity, Azure AD, Windows credentials

Provide localized version of your application by visually editing resource files (.resx). Radzen shows translated content when the language changes.

[See Localization Docs ↗](/blazor-studio/documentation/localization)

Allow your users to export the data in the generated list pages.

Export to XLS

Export to CSV

Debugging allows you to see how your application behaves at runtime. You can step through your code and inspect the values of properties, fields and variables. You can also examine the execution path by stepping in and out of methods.

[See Debugging Docs ↗](/blazor-studio/documentation/debugging)

You can manage methods and their statements of your Blazor components or C# classes via Radzen Blazor Studio’s Methods design mode.

### What is Radzen Blazor Studio?

Radzen Blazor Studio is a development environment for building Blazor web applications. Build visually, with code, or with AI agents like Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex, and Gemini. It features a WYSIWYG designer, CRUD scaffolding from databases, 145+ UI components, premium themes, and one-click deployment to Azure and IIS.

### What platforms does Radzen Blazor Studio support?

Radzen Blazor Studio runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

Radzen Blazor Studio runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

### Can Radzen Blazor Studio connect to REST APIs?

Yes. Radzen Blazor Studio integrates with REST APIs, OData services, and OpenAPI specifications, as well as databases including MSSQL, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, and SQLite.

Yes. Radzen Blazor Studio integrates with REST APIs, OData services, and OpenAPI specifications, as well as databases including MSSQL, MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, and SQLite.

### Does Radzen Blazor Studio work with .NET 10?

Yes. Radzen Blazor Studio supports .NET 10 and the latest version of Blazor, including both Blazor Server and Blazor WebAssembly hosting models.

Yes. Radzen Blazor Studio supports .NET 10 and the latest version of Blazor, including both Blazor Server and Blazor WebAssembly hosting models.

Add authentication and authorization to your Blazor apps with a few clicks.

You can easily localize your Blazor application - add different cultures and change the UI messages by visually editing resource files (.resx).

Internet Information Services (IIS) is a popular hosting option for Blazor applications. Radzen Blazor Studio makes deployment to IIS a breeze. You can also deploy to Azure, FTP server, ZIP file, or a folder.

Radzen Blazor Studio generates service classes for database access. Your data is exposed as a set of methods that retrieve or manipulate data.

### 8. Add new pages and components

Radzen Blazor Studio provides a powerful design time UI for creating pages and adding Blazor components.

# Radzen Blazor Studio Documentation
Radzen Blazor Studio is a visual development environment for building modern Blazor web apps - with a designer, code editor, database integration, and AI-powered tooling.

Design pages with a drag-and-drop WYSIWYG interface, connect to data sources, and generate clean, production-ready code.

# AI Agents

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-studio/documentation/ai-agents.md

> Radzen Blazor Studio supports AI coding agents through the Agent Client Protocol (ACP). Learn which agents are supported and how to get started.

# AI Agents in Radzen Blazor Studio

Radzen Blazor Studio supports AI coding agents through the [Agent Client Protocol (ACP)](https://agentclientprotocol.org/) - an open protocol that standardizes communication between development tools and AI agents. With ACP, you can chat with an AI agent directly inside Radzen Blazor Studio. The agent can read and edit your files, run terminal commands, and help you build your application faster.

Radzen Blazor Studio does **not** ship any AI agent. You need to install the agent of your choice before using it.

<img src="images/blazor-studio/documentation/ai-agent-panel-in-radzen-blazor-studio.png" class="image-center rz-border-radius-2" loading="lazy">

## Supported agents

- [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart)
- [Codex](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) - additionally requires you to run `npm install -g @@zed-industries/codex-acp` (which needs NodeJS).
- [Cursor](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/installation)
- [Gemini CLI](https://geminicli.com/docs/get-started/installation/)
- [GitHub Copilot](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/set-up-copilot-cli/install-copilot-cli)
- [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai)

Once installed restart Radzen Blazor Studio then select the agent from the dropdown in the AI panel and start chatting.

> **Note**
> Starting June 15, 2026, Claude Code usage through the [Agent SDK](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/agent-sdk/overview) (including `claude -p`) on Claude subscription plans draws from a new monthly Agent SDK credit, separate from your interactive usage limits.

## Radzen Blazor MCP

When you use an AI agent through Radzen Blazor Studio, [Radzen Blazor MCP](/blazor-mcp) is automatically configured - no manual setup needed. The agent gets access to Radzen Blazor component documentation, API details, and ready-made templates out of the box.

## MCP Server

Radzen Blazor Studio also includes its own built-in MCP server that lets the agent scaffold pages, edit components, and manage themes and data sources directly in your open project. Agents you use through the AI panel get this configured automatically - no setup needed. To connect an agent you run **outside** Radzen Blazor Studio (a terminal CLI or another editor), see the [MCP server](/blazor-studio/documentation/mcp-server) guide.

## Troubleshooting

If you don't see an installed agent in the agent dropdown make sure it is available in `PATH`. You should be able to run the agent CLI executable from terminal or command prompt.

# Edit a Radzen Blazor Theme

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/edit-theme.md

> Learn how to customize the look and feel of your Radzen Blazor App and quickly perform advanced component customizations

# Edit a Radzen Blazor Theme

The **Appearance** panel in Radzen Blazor Studio lets you easily customize the global look and feel of your application - live, as you work.

## How-to Video

<YouTube Video="u59RQ_AHiAs" />

## Basic Color Customization

> **Note:**
> Color customization is a [premium feature](/blazor-studio/documentation/editions) and is available only for apps that use the [Radzen Blazor Components](/blazor-components) library.

![Theme color customization](images/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/radzen-blazor-studio-edit-theme-colors.gif)

Follow these steps to customize your app’s theme colors:

1. Open a **.razor** file from your Radzen Blazor project in Radzen Blazor Studio.
2. In the left-hand **Navigation bar**, click **Appearance** to open the panel.
3. *(Optional)* Choose the theme you want to edit from the dropdown at the top.
4. *(Optional)* Pick a **swatch** from the list of available [Swatches](/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/themes-and-swatches#swatches).
5. In the **Colors** section, you’ll see color pickers for each theme color.
6. Click a color picker and select new colors for your app. Repeat as needed.

All color changes are saved automatically to your app’s **`site.css`** file (wwwroot/css/site.css). You can open and edit this file directly if you want to fine-tune styles manually.

> **Note:**
> Changing theme colors affects all components in your application. Choose colors that work well together for a consistent look.

> **Tip:**
> Some lighter shades have built-in opacity. This helps maintain good contrast between backgrounds and text.

## Advanced Theme Customization

> **Note:**
> Advanced theme customization is a [premium feature](/blazor-studio/documentation/editions) available for apps using the [Radzen Blazor Components](/blazor-components) library.

![Advanced theme customization](images/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/radzen-blazor-studio-advanced-edit-theme.gif)

Advanced customization lets you control more aspects of your app’s design - such as typography, borders, shadows, spacing, and component sizing.
You can also override default global styles for individual components. Some changes may require basic CSS knowledge.

### Steps

1. Open a **.razor** file that includes the elements or components you want to style, so you can preview your changes live.
2. In the left-hand **Navigation bar**, click **Appearance** to open the panel.
3. Find the section or component you want to customize.
4. Adjust the available properties as needed. Repeat for each setting you want to change.

> **Note:**
> Global theme customizations affect components unless they have styles edited locally in the **Styles** tab.
> Local edits override global styles.

> **Important:**
> Any adjustments made through the **Appearance** panel are stored in your project’s **`site.css`** file (wwwroot/css/site.css).
> This means you can reuse or modify those styles directly if you need to adjust them outside Radzen Blazor Studio.

You can customize:

- Typography (base font size, font family)
- Background colors for components or the app
- Base icon size
- Theme-defined borders, shadows, and transitions
- All theme properties and interaction states for Radzen Blazor components

## Export and Import Styles

Exporting and importing themes in **JSON** format makes it easy to reuse the same styles across multiple apps, ensuring a consistent design.

> **Note:**
> Exporting and importing custom themes is a [premium feature](/blazor-studio/documentation/editions).

### Export Styles

To export your theme:

1. Click **Export styles** in the Appearance panel.
2. Radzen Blazor Studio will create a file named **{theme}-custom.json**.
   You can use it as a backup or import it into another Radzen Blazor project.

### Import Styles

To import a custom theme:

1. Click **Import styles** in the Appearance panel.
2. Select a JSON theme file created by Radzen Blazor Studio.
   The imported styles will be applied automatically.

## Reset a Customized Theme

To restore a theme to its original design, click **Reset** in the Appearance panel.
This removes all customizations and reloads the default theme styles.

## Tip for Teams

Since all theme changes are saved to **`site.css`**, you can easily version-control them with Git or any other source control system.

This makes it simple for teams to review, share, and roll back design updates as part of your regular development workflow.

---

# Style Components

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/style-components.md

> Learn how to customize the look and feel of Radzen Blazor components in your application

# Style Components

In Radzen Blazor Studio, you can style your app in two ways - **globally** across the whole app, or **locally** for a single component.

Use app-wide styling for consistency; use local (component instance) styling for one-off tweaks.

## App-wide Styles via Themes

These styles live in your app’s theme and are edited from the **Appearance** panel.

In the appearance panel you adjust **theme properties** that define the overall look and feel of your application. These properties exist at three levels:

- **Global** level properties, e.g. **primary color**
- **Context** level properties, e.g. **focused state border**
- **Component** level properties. These are the component-specific details you'd like to edit, such as the **input border radius** or **DataGrid background color**.

<img src="images/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/customize-component-theme-properties.png" class="image-center rz-border-radius-2" style="margin: 40px auto; max-width: 50%; max-height: 600px;" loading="lazy">

> **Remember:**
> Edits made via the Appearance panel are applied across the whole application.

Theme edits are written to your app’s **`site.css`** file. You can open and adjust this file directly if you want to fine-tune styles or review them in version control.

You can also **export** and **import** styles to reuse them across multiple Radzen Blazor apps.

Learn more about [Themes and Swatches](/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/themes-and-swatches) or see how to [Customize a theme](/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/edit-theme).

## Local Styles via the Styles Tab

Local styles apply only to the selected component or HTML element.
They are edited from the **Styles** tab in the **Properties** panel.

The **Styles** tab contains:

### Theme Variables

Modify theme-driven properties for that specific component (for example, background color or border style).

These settings override the theme’s defaults for that instance only.

  <img src="images/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/radzen-blazor-edit-component-theme-properties.png" class="image-center" style="margin: 40px auto;" loading="lazy">

### Generic Styles

Apply generic CSS rules such as margins, padding, font size, or alignment.

<img src="images/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/radzen-blazor-edit-component-generic-styles.png" class="image-center" style="margin: 40px auto;" loading="lazy">

> **Remember:**
> Local style changes are added **inline** to the component’s `style` attribute and **do not** update the `site.css` file.
> Local styles always **override** global theme styles for that component.

---

# Themes and Swatches

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/themes-and-swatches.md

> Learn how to change app theme and find out more about the powerful theming options available in Radzen Blazor Studio

# Themes and Swatches
Radzen Blazor Studio features sets of [free](#free-themes) and [premium](#premium-themes) themes and predefined color [swatches](#swatches) for [Radzen Blazor Components](/blazor-components).

## Change application theme

To change the theme of your Radzen Blazor application:

1. In the **Navigation bar**, click on the <img src="images/blazor-studio/documentation/design-time/appearance-icon.png" style="width: 32px; margin: 0; vertical-align: middle;" loading="lazy"> **Appearance** option. This opens the Appearance panel.
2. Select your preferred theme from the **dropdown** at the top of the Appearance panel.

They are **not** available during trial mode. Check the [online demos](https://blazor.radzen.com) of the Radzen Blazor components to get a preview.

A sleek and elegant dark version of Material 3 theme for enhanced readability and visual appeal.

<img src="images/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/material3-dark-chart-radzen-blazor.png" alt="Radzen Blazor Material3 Dark Charts" width="70%" class="image-center" style="margin: 40px auto;" loading="lazy">

### Fluent UI theme
The Fluent Design System is a design language developed by Microsoft. It is used by many of Microsoft's own products, as well as by third-party developers who want to create user experiences that are consistent with the Microsoft ecosystem.

<img src="images/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/fluent-ui-chart-radzen-blazor.png" alt="Radzen Blazor FluentUI Light Charts" width="70%" class="image-center" style="margin: 40px auto;" loading="lazy">

### Fluent UI Dark theme
The Fluent UI Dark theme aligns your applications with Microsoft's Fluent Design System, delivering a polished user experience with a dark twist.

<img src="images/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/fluent-ui-dark-chart-radzen-blazor.png" alt="Radzen Blazor FluentUI Dark Charts" width="70%" class="image-center" style="margin: 40px auto;" loading="lazy">
<img src="images/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/fluent-ui-dark-data-grid-radzen-blazor.png" alt="Radzen Blazor FluentUI Dark DataGrid" width="70%" class="image-center" style="margin: 40px auto;" loading="lazy">

### Using a premium theme in a Visual Studio application
The premium theme assets are not included in the Radzen.Blazor Nuget package. To use a premium theme in your Visual Studio application you need to:

1. Create a new **Blazor Server** application in Radzen Blazor Studio and pick the desired premium theme.
1. Copy the theme CSS file from the newly created application to your Visual Studio application's `wwwroot` directory. The theme CSS file is located in `wwwroot\css`.
1. Copy the `wwwroot\fonts` directory to your Visual Studio application's `wwwroot` directory.

## Swatches

> **Note:** Swatches are a [premium](/blazor-studio/documentation/editions) feature.

Each theme contains a collection of predefined color swatches.

<img src="images/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/radzen-blazor-theme-swatches.png" width="50%" class="image-center" style="margin: 40px auto;" loading="lazy">

A swatch is a color palette containing carefully picked color tints and shades of:

- Base background and text colors
- Primary color
- Secondary color
- Info color
- Success color
- Warning color
- Danger color

Swatches are a great starting point to quickly customize the global styling of your application via a single click.

<div style="width: 70%; margin: 40px auto;">
    ![image](images/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/radzen-blazor-material3-theme.gif)
</div>

### WCAG Swatches

WCAG stands for Web Content Accessibility Guidelines - an internationally recognized set of recommendations for making web content more accessible. The WCAG color swatches cover the minimum contrast requirements for AA level of conformance in WCAG 2.2 - The visual presentation of text and images of text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1.

<img src="images/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/blazor-wcag-aa-colors.png" alt="Radzen Blazor Standard theme with and without WCAG 2.2 AA compliant colors" width="70%" class="image-center" style="margin: 40px auto;" loading="lazy">

### High Contrast Swatches

The High Contrast swatches cover the enhanced contrast requirements for AAA level of conformance in WCAG 2.2 - The visual presentation of text and images of text has a contrast ratio of at least 7:1.

<img src="images/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/blazor-fluent-light-high-contrast.png" alt="Radzen Blazor FluentUI Light High Contrast theme swatch" width="70%" class="image-center" style="margin: 40px auto;" loading="lazy">
<img src="images/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/blazor-fluent-dark-high-contrast.png" alt="Radzen Blazor FluentUI Dark High Contrast theme swatch" width="70%" class="image-center" style="margin: 40px auto;" loading="lazy">

> **Note:** Inappropriate component positioning or configurations might lead to low contrast between text and background colors. It is recommended to always test your layouts, content, and component configurations against the desired accessibility guidelines. See [testing and evaluating web accessibility](https://www.w3.org/WAI/test-evaluate/preliminary) on the W3C website.

### Apply a color swatch

To apply a swatch, simply select it from the list of available swatches for a chosen theme. Its colors are automatically populated in the pickers under Colors customization section and applied to your app in real time. Read more about [Basic color customization](/blazor-studio/documentation/appearance/edit-theme#basic-color-customization).

To reset a theme to its original colors, hit the Reset button in the Appearance panel.
