# Applications

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-studio/documentation/applications.md

> Create new Blazor Server and WebAssembly applications. Open existing ones.

# Applications

Radzen Blazor Studio helps you build Blazor applications quickly and visually.
Here’s how to create a new one or open an existing project.

## Create a new application

Radzen Blazor Studio can create **Blazor Web** applications that target **.NET 9** or **.NET 10**.
If you plan to build apps for .NET 9, make sure the **.NET 9 SDK** is also installed.

All generated applications use the **Radzen.Blazor** component library.

### Steps

1. Click the **“+”** button in the bottom-left corner of Radzen Blazor Studio.
   This opens the **New Application** wizard.
2. Enter a name for your application.
   The name sets both the solution filename and the root namespace.
3. Choose a **rendering mode**.
   Supported modes include **Server**, **WebAssembly**, and **Auto**.
   Interactivity is enabled globally.
4. Pick a directory where the application will be created.
5. Click **Finish**.
6. Once created, run the application to open it in your browser.

![New Application](images/blazor-studio/documentation/new-application.gif)

> **Note**
> If you prefer to create a clean Blazor app without third-party components, you can use the .NET CLI instead:
> `dotnet new blazor`

## Open an existing application

To open an existing Blazor project:

1. Click the **Open** button in the bottom-left corner.
2. Select the `.sln` or `.csproj` file for your application.

Radzen Blazor Studio will load the project so you can start editing right away.

![Existing Application](images/blazor-studio/documentation/existing-application.gif)

## v1.64.0
### Improvements
- Smarter code editing with Go to Definition (F12), Find All References, project-wide symbol search, rename refactoring and reference counts above methods. Razor editing now auto-closes tags, highlights matching symbols and keeps formatting clean as you type. CSS and HTML editors include live error checking, color pickers in the gutter, hover documentation and clickable links between files - also available inside `<style>` blocks in Razor files. Read more in the [announcement](https://www.radzen.com/blog/smarter-code-editing-in-radzen-blazor-studio).
- Oracle support enabled for .NET 10 applications.
- Updated premium themes.

### Fixes
- Completion documentation is missing when switching between files quickly.
- False "BuildRenderTree already defined" error appears for Razor files with code-behind.
- Razor file completions include irrelevant C# snippets.
- Data grid export to CSV/Excel fails for stored procedures with no input parameters.

### Download v1.64.0
- [windows](@(Settings.CdnUrl)/Radzen%20Blazor%20Studio%20Setup%201.64.0.exe)

# Code Editor

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-studio/documentation/code-editor.md

> Code Editor in Radzen Blazor Studio. Full IntelliSense, GitHub Copilot integration, syntax highlighting, and real-time diagnostics for C# and Razor development.

# Code Editor

Radzen Blazor Studio includes the same powerful code editor used by Visual Studio Code.

It provides a familiar, fast, and reliable editing experience for developers who write C# and Razor.

## Autocomplete

Radzen Blazor Studio offers full **autocomplete** support in both C# and Razor files.

You can see available members, parameter info, and API references as you type.

<img src="images/blazor-studio/documentation/code-editor-autocomplete.gif" alt="Radzen Blazor Studio autocomplete" loading="lazy">

## GitHub Copilot Autocomplete

Radzen Blazor Studio integrates **GitHub Copilot** directly into the Code Editor.

Copilot helps you write code faster by suggesting whole lines or blocks of code as you type - right inside Radzen Blazor Studio.

### How it works
When you start typing in the code editor, Copilot automatically analyzes your context and offers intelligent suggestions.
Press **Tab** to accept a suggestion, or keep typing to dismiss it. Suggestions appear faded until you confirm them.

<img src="images/blog/copilot-autocomplete-in-radzen-blazor-studio.gif" alt="GitHub Copilot in Radzen Blazor Studio" loading="lazy" style="width: 60%;">

### Benefits
- **Faster coding** - Get real-time code completions as you type.
- **Smarter suggestions** - Copilot learns from billions of open-source examples.
- **Seamless experience** - Works just like the built-in autocomplete, no setup required.

### Requirements
You need an **active GitHub Copilot subscription** and must be signed in with your GitHub account in Radzen Blazor Studio.
If you don’t have Copilot enabled, the editor will fall back to the standard autocomplete experience.

> **Tip:**
> Copilot suggestions are meant to assist, not replace your code. Always review what you accept to ensure it fits your application logic and security standards.

### Learn more
For details on connecting your GitHub account, managing Copilot settings, and advanced usage examples, see [GitHub Copilot in Radzen Blazor Studio](/blazor-studio/documentation/github-copilot).

## Diagnostics

As you write code, Radzen Blazor Studio analyzes it in real time.

If there’s a problem, you’ll see a squiggly underline showing where the issue is.

Hover over the line to read details about the error or warning.

<img src="images/blazor-studio/documentation/code-editor-diagnostics.gif" alt="Radzen Blazor Studio diagnostics" loading="lazy">

## Preview

Hover over code elements to instantly see details such as:

- Member types
- API documentation
- Current values (during [debugging](/blazor-studio/documentation/debugging))

<img src="images/blazor-studio/documentation/code-editor-preview.gif" alt="Radzen Blazor Studio preview" loading="lazy">

# CRM Tutorial: Customize CRUD Pages

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/customize-crud.md

> Extend the automatically generated pages via Radzen Blazor Studio WYSIWYG visual designer

# Customize CRUD Pages | Create a Blazor CRM application with Radzen Blazor Studio
In this step from the CRM Application tutorial we will customize the automatically scaffolded CRUD pages.

- Start by adding some contacts
- Customize the **Opportunities** page
  - Associate an opportunity with the current application user.
  - Display the user first and last name in the opportunity DataGrid.
- Add icons for the Task Status and Task Type columns in the **Tasks** page.
- Add search capabilities to the **Contacts** page.

## Add some contacts

The contact is a paramount entity in the RadzenCRM application as everything depends on it - opportunities, tasks etc.

Let's add some contacts. We will use some famous members from the tech industry.

1. Open the Contacts page in Radzen Blazor Studio.
1. Select the DataGrid component and remove the **ID** column as we don't need it.
1. Run the application from Radzen Blazor Studio.
1. Log in with `salesmanager@@demo.radzen.com` and `SalesManager1@@`. Those are the credentials of the Jane Smith application user who is a **Sales Manager** (we added that user in the [Customize security](blazor-studio/documentation/crm/security) article).
1. Navigate to the **Contacts** page.
1. Add two contacts:
  - FirstName: `Bill`, LastName: `Gates`, Email: `bill.gates@@microsoft.com` (probably not his real email), Company: `Microsoft`.
  - FirstName: `Elon`, LastName: `Musk`, Email: `elon.musk@@tesla.com` (maybe not real too), Company: `Tesla`.
  ![Crm Customize Crud Contacts](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-customize-crud-contacts.png)

## Customize the Opportunities page

### Associate opportunities with users

The first thing we will do is associate the opportunity with the current user and filter the opportunities so:
- Members of the **Sales Representative** role see only their opportunities.
- Members of the **Sales Manager** role see all opportunities.

#### Server-side Blazor

1. Stop the running application.
1. Add a new file `Services\RadzenCRMService.Custom.cs` with the following content.

```cs
using System;
using System.Data;
using System.Linq;
using System.Linq.Dynamic.Core;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using System.Threading.Tasks;
using System.Text.Encodings.Web;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components;
using Microsoft.Data.SqlClient;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Radzen;

using CRMBlazorServerRBS.Data;
using CRMBlazorServerRBS.Models.RadzenCRM;

namespace CRMBlazorServerRBS
{
    public partial class RadzenCRMService
    {
        private readonly SecurityService security;

        public RadzenCRMService(RadzenCRMContext context, NavigationManager navigationManager, SecurityService security)
          : this(context, navigationManager)
        {
            this.security = security;
        }

        partial void OnOpportunityCreated(Opportunity item)
        {
            var userId = security.User.Id;

            // Set the UserId property of the opportunity to the current user's id
            item.UserId = userId;
        }

        partial void OnOpportunitiesRead(ref IQueryable<Opportunity> items)
        {
            if (!security.IsInRole("Sales Manager")
            {
                var userId = security.User.Id;

                // Filter the opportunities by the current user's id
                items = items.Where(item => item.UserId == userId);
            }
        }
    }
}")

```

#### Client-side WebAssembly Blazor
1. Stop the running application.
1. Add a new file `Server\Controllers\RadzenCRM\OpportunitiesController.Custom.cs` with the following content.

```cs
using System;
using System.Net;
using System.Data;
using System.Linq;
using Microsoft.Data.SqlClient;
using System.Collections.Generic;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.OData.Query;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.OData.Routing.Controllers;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.OData.Results;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.OData.Deltas;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.OData.Formatter;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Metadata.Internal;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
using CRMBlazorWasmRBS.Server.Models;
using CRMBlazorWasmRBS.Server.Models.RadzenCRM;

namespace CRMBlazorWasmRBS.Server.Controllers.RadzenCRM
{
    [Authorize]
    public partial class OpportunitiesController
    {
        partial void OnOpportunitiesRead(ref IQueryable<Opportunity> items)
        {
            var userManager = (UserManager<ApplicationUser>)HttpContext.RequestServices.GetService(typeof(UserManager<ApplicationUser>));

            var user = userManager.GetUserAsync(HttpContext.User).Result;
            if (user != null)
            {
                var roles = userManager.GetRolesAsync(user).Result;

                if (!roles.Contains("Sales Manager")
                {
                    // Filter the opportunities by the current user's id
                    items = items.Where(item => item.UserId == user.Id);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}")

```
1. Set `UserId` before submitting the opportunity in AddOpportunity page.

```cs
protected async Task FormSubmit()
{
    try
    {
        opportunity.UserId = Security.User?.Id;

        await RadzenCRMService.CreateOpportunity(opportunity);
        DialogService.Close(opportunity);
    }
    catch (Exception ex)
    {
        errorVisible = true;
    }
}
```

Since we are manually setting the UserId of the opportunity we should remove the corresponding form field from the
**Add Opportunity** and **Edit Opportunity** pages.

1. Open the **Add Opportunity** page.
1. Select the **TemplateForm** component.
1. Delete the FormField that contains the **UserId** text box.
1. Repeat steps 1 to 3 for the **Edit Opportunity** page.

Let's try if it worked!

1. Run the application from Radzen.
1. Log in with `salesmanager@@demo.radzen.com` and `SalesManager1@@`.
1. Add a new opportunity with the following details:
  - **Amount**: `50000`
  - **Contact**: `bill.gates@@microsoft.com`
  - **Opportunity Status**: `Active`
  - **Close Date**: `02/01/2019`
  - **Name**: `Microsoft deal`

You should see this.

![Crm Customize Crud Opportunities](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-customize-crud-opportunities.png)

1. Add a new opportunity with the following details:
  - **Amount**: `100000`
  - **Contact**: `elon.musk@@tesla.com`
  - **Opportunity Status**: `Won`
  - **Close Date**: `02/02/2019`
  - **Name**: `Tesla deal`

### Display the first and last name in the Opportunities DataGrid

But what is that GUID in the User ID column? It is the Id of Jane Smith - the user we have logged in as. Let's display something more user-friendly than a GUID.

#### Server-side Blazor

1. Open the **Opportunities** page in Radzen.
1. First we have to get the current user as an entity so we can use its properties in the DataGrid.
1. Open `Services\RadzenCRMService.Custom.cs` with Visual Studio.
1. Append the following statement to the `OnOpportunitiesRead` method: `items = items.Include(item => item.User);`. Here is how it should look like:

```cs
partial void OnOpportunitiesRead(ref IQueryable<Opportunity> items)
{
    if (!security.IsInRole("Sales Manager")
    {
        var userId = security.User.Id;

        // Filter the opportunities by the current user's id
        items = items.Where(item => item.UserId == userId);

    }
    // Include the User
    items = items.Include(item => item.User);
}")

```

#### Client-side WebAssembly Blazor

1. Open the **Opportunities** page in Radzen.
1. First we have to get the current user as an entity so we can use its properties in the DataGrid.
1. Select the DataGrid component and edit its **LoadData** event handlers.
1. Append `,User` in the `expand` parameter value. The `expand` parameter is similar to a SQL JOIN (and in fact does exactly that behind the scenes).

Now let's customize the DataGrid!
1. Go to the **Properties** tab of the property grid and edit the **Template** of the User ID column.
1. Drag and drop a **Label** component. Set its **Text** property to `@@opportunity.User.FirstName`.
1. Drag and drop another **Label**. Set its **Text** property to `@@opportunity.User.LastName`.
1. Close the template editor by clicking the **End template editing** button.
1. Finally set the **FilterProperty** and **SortProperty** of the User ID column to `User.FirstName`. This tells the DataGrid what property to sort by when the user changes the order by clicking the column header.
![Crm Customize Crud Opportunity User](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-customize-crud-opportunity-user.png)

If you run the application now it should display the current user name instead of the GUID.

![Crm Customize Crud Opportunity User1](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-customize-crud-opportunity-user1.png)

## Add icons in the Tasks DataGrid

We will improve the look and feel of the **Tasks** page by using icons in the **Task Status** and **Task Type** DataGrid columns.

Run the application and add three tasks with the following properties

1. **Title**: `Introduction`, **Opportunity**: `Microsoft deal`, **Due Date**: `02/02/2019`, **Task Type**: `Email`, **Task Status**: `Complete`.
1. **Title**: `Demonstration`, **Opportunity**: `Microsoft deal`, **Due Date**: `03/06/2019`, **Task Type**: `Online Meeting`, **Task Status**: `In Progress`.
1. **Title**: `Negotiation`, **Opportunity**: `Microsoft deal`, **Due Date**: `03/26/2019`, **Task Type**: `Call`, **Task Status**: `Not Started`.

![Crm Customize Crud Tasks](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-customize-crud-tasks.png)

Now let's add the icons for the **Task Type** column.

1. Open the **Tasks** page in Radzen.
1. Select the **DataGrid** component.
1. Edit the **Template** property of the **Task Type** column.
1. Drag and drop a **Label** component and set its **Text** property to `@@task.TaskType.Name`.
1. Drag and drop an **Icon** component. Set the **Icon** property to `settings_phone` (click the **...** button
to open the **Icon Picker** dialog). Set the **Visible** property to `@@(task.TaskType.Name == "Call")`.
This icon will be visible only when the current task type is equal to `Call`.
Go to the **Style** tab of the property grid and set **VerticalAlign** to `middle`.
1. Duplicate the existing icon by right-clicking it and picking the **Duplicate** option.
Change the **Icon** property to `video_call` and set the **Visible** property to `@@(task.TaskType.Name == "Online Meeting")`.
1. Duplicate the last icon. Change its **Icon** property to `email` and set the **Visible**
property to `@@(task.TaskType.Name == "Email")`.
1. Click **End template editing**.

The **Tasks** page should now look like this. ![Crm Customize Crud Task Type Icons](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-customize-crud-task-type-icons.png)

Do the same for the **Task Status** column.
1. Edit the **Template** of the **Task Status** column.
1. Drag and drop a **Label** component and set its **Text** property to `@@task.TaskStatus.Name`.
1. Drag and drop an **Icon** component. Set the **Icon** property to `check_circle` (click the **...** button
to open the **Icon Picker** dialog). Set the **Visible** property to `@@(task.TaskStatus.Name == "Complete")`.
Go to the **Style** tab of the property grid and set **VerticalAlign** to `middle`.
1. Duplicate the existing icon by right-clicking it and picking the **Duplicate** option.
Change the **Icon** property to `cancel` and set the **Visible** property to `@@(task.TaskStatus.Name == "Not Started")`.
1. Duplicate the last icon. Change its **Icon** property to `autorenew` and set the **Visible**
property to `@@(task.TaskStatus.Name == "In Progress")`.
1. Click **End template editing**.

Here is how the end result should look like:
![Crm Customize Crud Task Status](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-customize-crud-task-status.png)

It is time to learn how to create a [dashboard](blazor-studio/documentation/crm/dashboard) page with Radzen Blazor Studio.

# CRM Tutorial: Create a Dashboard Page

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/dashboard.md

> Create a dashboard page with Radzen Blazor Studio to show various metrics

# Create a Dashboard Page | Create a Blazor CRM application with Radzen Blazor Studio
In this tutorial we will create a nice dashboard page for our CRM application that shows some performance metrics.

- Display the monthly stats - total revenue, new opportunities, average deal size and win rate percentage.
- Show some charts - contact life time value, revenue progress, revenue per employee.
- Summarize the active opportunities and tasks.

Before we start we would need more data in the CRM application. Run it from Radzen Blazor Studio and add more opportunities, contacts and tasks.
Or you can use [this SQL script](https://github.com/radzenhq/radzen-blazor-studio/blob/master/CRMBlazorServerRBS/crm-database-data.sql) which comes with sample data (but will delete all existing data).

## Create the dashboard page

First create a new empty page called "Home". Set it to be the start page of the application.

## Display monthly stats

### Calculate stats

#### Server-side Blazor

We will create a method which will calculate the monthly stats.

1. Open `Pages\Index.razor.cs` and inject the Entity Framework context as a property:
   ```cs
   ...
   [Inject]
   public Data.RadzenCRMContext Context { get; set; }
   ...
   ```
1. Add a new class `Stats` in the same file. It will contain the monthly stats we are interested in
   ```cs
   public class Stats
   {
       public DateTime Month { get; set; }
       public decimal Revenue { get; set; }

       public int Opportunities { get; set; }
       public decimal AverageDealSize { get; set; }
       public double Ratio { get; set; }
   }
   ```
1. Add a new method to the **Index** class to calculate the stats.
   ```cs
   public Stats MonthlyStats()
   {
       double wonOpportunities = Context.Opportunities
                           .Include(opportunity => opportunity.OpportunityStatus)
                           .Where(opportunity => opportunity.OpportunityStatus.Name == "Won"
                           .Count();

       var totalOpportunities = Context.Opportunities.Count();

       var ratio = wonOpportunities / totalOpportunities;

       return Context.Opportunities
                     .Include(opportunity => opportunity.OpportunityStatus)
                     .Where(opportunity => opportunity.OpportunityStatus.Name == ""Won"")
                     .ToList()
                     .GroupBy(opportunity => new DateTime(opportunity.CloseDate.Year, opportunity.CloseDate.Month, 1))
                     .Select(group => new Stats()
                     {
                         Month = group.Key,
                         Revenue = group.Sum(opportunity => opportunity.Amount),
                         Opportunities = group.Count(),
                         AverageDealSize = group.Average(opportunity => opportunity.Amount),
                         Ratio = ratio
                     })
                     .OrderBy(deals => deals.Month)
                     .LastOrDefault();
   }")

   ```

#### Client-side WebAssembly Blazor

We will create a method which will calculate the monthly stats.

1. Add `Server\Controllers\ServerMethodsController.cs` with the following code.
   ```cs
   using System;
   using System.Net;
   using System.Data;
   using System.Linq;
   using Microsoft.Data.SqlClient;
   using System.Collections.Generic;
   using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
   using Microsoft.AspNetCore.OData.Query;
   using Microsoft.AspNetCore.OData.Routing.Controllers;
   using Microsoft.AspNetCore.OData.Results;
   using Microsoft.AspNetCore.OData.Deltas;
   using Microsoft.AspNetCore.OData.Formatter;
   using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
   using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Metadata.Internal;
   using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity;
   using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
   using CRMBlazorWasmRBS.Server.Models;
   using CRMBlazorWasmRBS.Server.Models.RadzenCRM;

   namespace CRMBlazorWasmRBS.Server.Controllers
   {
       [Route("api/[controller]/[action]"]
       public class ServerMethodsController : Controller
       {
           private CRMBlazorWasmRBS.Server.Data.RadzenCRMContext context;

           public ServerMethodsController(CRMBlazorWasmRBS.Server.Data.RadzenCRMContext context)
           {
               this.context = context;
           }

           public IActionResult MonthlyStats()
           {
               double wonOpportunities = context.Opportunities
                                 .Include(opportunity => opportunity.OpportunityStatus)
                                 .Where(opportunity => opportunity.OpportunityStatus.Name == ""Won"")
                                 .Count();

               var totalOpportunities = context.Opportunities.Count();

               var ratio = wonOpportunities / totalOpportunities;

               var stats = context.Opportunities
                                 .Include(opportunity => opportunity.OpportunityStatus)
                                 .Where(opportunity => opportunity.OpportunityStatus.Name == ""Won"")
                                 .ToList()
                                 .GroupBy(opportunity => new DateTime(opportunity.CloseDate.Year, opportunity.CloseDate.Month, 1))
                                 .Select(group => new
                                 {
                                       Month = group.Key,
                                       Revenue = group.Sum(opportunity => opportunity.Amount),
                                       Opportunities = group.Count(),
                                       AverageDealSize = group.Average(opportunity => opportunity.Amount),
                                       Ratio = ratio
                                 })
                                 .OrderBy(deals => deals.Month)
                                 .LastOrDefault();

            return Ok(System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Serialize(stats, new System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions { PropertyNamingPolicy = null }));
        }
   }")

   ```
1. Open `Client\Pages\Index.razor.cs` and inject the HttpClient as a property:
   ```cs
   ...
   [Inject]
   HttpClient Http { get; set; }
   ...
   ```
1. Add a new class `Stats` in the same file. It will contain the monthly stats we are interested in
   ```cs
   public class Stats
   {
       public DateTime Month { get; set; }
       public decimal Revenue { get; set; }

       public int Opportunities { get; set; }
       public decimal AverageDealSize { get; set; }
       public double Ratio { get; set; }
   }
   ```
1. Add a new method to the `Index` class. It will calculate the stats.
   ```cs
   public async Task<Stats> MonthlyStats()
   {
      var response = await Http.SendAsync(new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, new Uri($"{NavigationManager.BaseUri}api/servermethods/monthlystats"));

      return await response.ReadAsync<Stats>();
   }")

   ```

### Display the monthly stats

Now that the custom method is done it is time to create the UI that will display the stats. We will use a **Row** component with four **Columns**.
Each column will contain a **Card** that displays a metric from the monthly stats.

We will describe the process to create one card and then copy paste it.

1. Open **Index** page and delete the top most **Column**. ![Crm Dashboard Column](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-column.png)
1. Drag and drop a new **Column** component inside the row. ![Crm Dashboard Column1](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-column1.png)
1. Set the **XL** size to 3 units and the **LG** size to 6 units. By default the available horizontal space is 12 units.
This means that on XL size devices (wide-screen desktops) this column will occupy 1/4<sup>th</sup> of the available width (because 3/12 = 1/4). On **LG** screens (laptop displays) it will occupy half the available space (6 / 12 = 1/2).
On smaller screen sizes this column will take all the available width.
1. Drag and drop a **Card** component inside the column. Go to the **Style** tab of the property grid and set its bottom **Margin** to `16px`.
![Crm Dashboard Column Card](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-column-card.png)

We have created the basic card layout. Now let's add some content that will display the data.

1. Drag and drop a **Row** inside the card.
1. Drag and drop a **Column** inside that row. Set its **XS** size to 4. This means that it will always occupy 4 units (1/3) of the available width (which in this case is the width of the card).
1. Duplicate the column. Set its **XS** size to 8. This column will occupy the remaining space. ![Crm Dashboard Card Row](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-card-row.png)
1. Drag and drop an **Icon** component in the first column. Set its **Icon** property to `attach_money`.
Set the **Width** and **Height** to `64px`. Set **FontSize** to `48px`. ![Crm Dashboard Card Icon](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-card-icon.png)
1. Drag and drop a **Heading** component in the second column. Set its **Text** property to `Revenue`,
**Size** to `H4`, **TextAlign** to `Right` and **Margin** to `0px`. ![Crm Dashboard Card Revenue](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-card-revenue.png)
1. Duplicate the heading. Set **Text** to `LAST MONTH` and **FontSize** to `12px`. ![Crm Dashboard Card Last Month](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-card-last-month.png)
1. Duplicate the last heading. Set **Text** to `Value`, top **Margin** to `13px` to offset it from the other headings a bit, and **FontSize** to `24px`. ![Crm Dashboard Card Value](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-card-value.png)

We have created the card design and it is time to display the `Revenue` in the last heading component that we added.

1. Add a new override for the Page **OnInitialized()** method. ![Crm Dashboard Initialized](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-initialized.png)
1. Add new **Invoke**.
1. Set **Invoke** method to `MonthlyStats` and set the result to `monthlyStats` public page property. ![Crm Dashboard Invoke Result](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-invoke-result.png) ![Crm Dashboard Invoke Result Property](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-invoke-result-property.png)
1. Select the last heading component in the card. Set its **Text** property to `@@monthlyStats?.Revenue.ToString("C")`. This displays the `Revenue` member of the `monthlyStats` page property formatted as currency.

![Crm Dashboard Card Data Bind](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-card-data-bind.png) ![Crm Dashboard Card Data Bind1](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-card-data-bind1.png)

If you now run the application you should see the following (assuming you have used the sample SQL data linked before).

![Crm Dashboard Revenue](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-revenue.png)

To display the rest of the monthly stats we should duplicate the column, change the color, heading texts and the `monthlyStats` member they display.

Here is how:

#### Opportunities

1. Duplicate the column.
1. Select the **Icon**. Set its **Icon** property to `shopping_cart`.
1. Select the first heading and set its **Text** to `Opportunities`.
1. Select the bottom heading. Set **Text** to `@@(monthlyStats?.Opportunities.ToString("C"))`.

#### Average deal size

1. Duplicate the column.
1. Select the **Icon**. Set its **Icon** property to `account_balance_wallet`.
1. Select the first heading and set its **Text** to `Average Deal Size`.
1. Select the bottom heading. Set **Text** to `@@(monthlyStats?.AverageDealSize.ToString("C"))`.

#### Win rate

1. Duplicate the column.
1. Select the **Icon**. Set its **Icon** property to `thumb_up`.
1. Select the first heading and set its **Text** to `Win Rate`.
1. Select the bottom heading. Set **Text** to `@@(monthlyStats?.Ratio.ToString("P"))`.

The final result should look like this at runtime.

![Crm Dashboard Card](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-card.png)

## Show charts

### Get data for the charts

#### Server-side Blazor
1. Open `Pages\Index.razor.cs` and add the following code:
   ```cs
   public class RevenueByCompany
   {
         public string Company { get; set; }
         public decimal Revenue { get; set; }
   }

   public class RevenueByEmployee
   {
         public string Employee { get; set; }
         public decimal Revenue { get; set; }
   }

   public class RevenueByMonth
   {
         public DateTime Month { get; set; }
         public decimal Revenue { get; set; }
   }

   public IEnumerable<RevenueByCompany> RevenueByCompany()
   {
      return Context.Opportunities
                           .Include(opportunity => opportunity.Contact)
                           .ToList()
                           .GroupBy(opportunity => opportunity.Contact.Company)
                           .Select(group => new RevenueByCompany() {
                                 Company = group.Key,
                                 Revenue = group.Sum(opportunity => opportunity.Amount)
                           });
   }

   public IEnumerable<RevenueByEmployee> RevenueByEmployee()
   {
      return Context.Opportunities
                           .Include(opportunity => opportunity.User)
                           .ToList()
                           .GroupBy(opportunity => $"{opportunity.User.FirstName} {opportunity.User.LastName}"
                           .Select(group => new RevenueByEmployee() {
                                 Employee = group.Key,
                                 Revenue = group.Sum(opportunity => opportunity.Amount)
                           });
   }

   public IEnumerable<RevenueByMonth> RevenueByMonth()
   {
      return Context.Opportunities
                           .Include(opportunity => opportunity.OpportunityStatus)
                           .Where(opportunity => opportunity.OpportunityStatus.Name == ""Won"")
                           .ToList()
                           .GroupBy(opportunity => new DateTime(opportunity.CloseDate.Year, opportunity.CloseDate.Month, 1))
                           .Select(group => new RevenueByMonth() {
                              Revenue = group.Sum(opportunity => opportunity.Amount),
                              Month = group.Key
                           })
                           .OrderBy(deals => deals.Month);
   }")

   ```

#### Client-side WebAssembly Blazor

1. Open `Server\Controllers\ServerMethodsController.cs`.
1. Add the following methods.
   ```cs
   public IActionResult RevenueByCompany()
   {
      var result = context.Opportunities
                           .Include(opportunity => opportunity.Contact)
                           .ToList()
                           .GroupBy(opportunity => opportunity.Contact.Company)
                           .Select(group => new {
                                 Company = group.Key,
                                 Revenue = group.Sum(opportunity => opportunity.Amount)
                           });

      return Ok(System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Serialize(result, new System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions
      {
            PropertyNamingPolicy = null
      }));
   }

   public IActionResult RevenueByEmployee()
   {
      var result = context.Opportunities
                           .Include(opportunity => opportunity.User)
                           .ToList()
                           .GroupBy(opportunity => $"{opportunity.User.FirstName} {opportunity.User.LastName}"
                           .Select(group => new {
                                 Employee = group.Key,
                                 Revenue = group.Sum(opportunity => opportunity.Amount)
                           });

      return Ok(System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Serialize(result, new System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions
      {
            PropertyNamingPolicy = null
      }));
   }

   public IActionResult RevenueByMonth()
   {
      var result = context.Opportunities
                           .Include(opportunity => opportunity.OpportunityStatus)
                           .Where(opportunity => opportunity.OpportunityStatus.Name == ""Won"")
                           .ToList()
                           .GroupBy(opportunity => new DateTime(opportunity.CloseDate.Year, opportunity.CloseDate.Month, 1))
                           .Select(group => new {
                              Revenue = group.Sum(opportunity => opportunity.Amount),
                              Month = group.Key
                           })
                           .OrderBy(deals => deals.Month);

      return Ok(System.Text.Json.JsonSerializer.Serialize(result, new System.Text.Json.JsonSerializerOptions
      {
            PropertyNamingPolicy = null
      }));
   }")

   ```
1. Open `Client\Pages\Index.razor.cs` and add the following code:
   ```cs
   public async Task<IEnumerable<RevenueByCompany>> RevenueByCompany()
   {
      var response = await Http.SendAsync(new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, new Uri($"{NavigationManager.BaseUri}api/servermethods/RevenueByCompany"));

      return await response.ReadAsync<IEnumerable<RevenueByCompany>>();
   }

   public async Task<IEnumerable<RevenueByEmployee>> RevenueByEmployee()
   {
      var response = await Http.SendAsync(new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, new Uri($""{NavigationManager.BaseUri}api/servermethods/RevenueByEmployee"")));

      return await response.ReadAsync<IEnumerable<RevenueByEmployee>>();
   }

   public async Task<IEnumerable<RevenueByMonth>> RevenueByMonth()
   {
      var response = await Http.SendAsync(new HttpRequestMessage(HttpMethod.Get, new Uri($""{NavigationManager.BaseUri}api/servermethods/RevenueByMonth"")));

      return await response.ReadAsync<IEnumerable<RevenueByMonth>>();
   }")

   ```

### Add the charts

As in the previous step we will start with the layout - row with three columns.

1. Drag and drop a **Row**.
1. Drag and drop a **Column** inside the row. Set the **XL** size to `4` units (1/3<sup>th</sup> of the available space) and the **LG** size to `6` (1/2<sup>th</sup> of the available space).
1. Drag and drop a **Card** inside the column. Go to the **Style** tab of the property grid and set its bottom **Margin** to `16px`.
![Crm Dashboard Chart Row](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-chart-row.png)

#### Customer life time value chart

1. Drag and drop a **Heading** component inside the card. Set its **Text** to `Customer life time value`.
1. Invoke the `RevenueByCompany` custom method in the Page **OnInitialized()** method. Create a page property called `revenueByCompany` from the result. ![Crm Dashboard Chart Company Invoke](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-chart-company-invoke.png)
1. Drag and drop a **Chart** and add RadzenColumnSeries to series. Set **Data** to `@@revenueByCompany`,
**ValueProperty** to `Revenue` and **CategoryProperty** to `Company`. Set the **Width** to `100%`.
![Crm Dashboard Chart Company](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-chart-company.png)

#### Revenue by month chart

1. Duplicate the column from the previous step.
1. Set the **Text** of the header to `Revenue`.
1. Invoke the `RevenueByMonth` custom method in the Page **OnInitialized()** method. Create a page property called `revenueByMonth` from the result.
1. Change RadzenColumnSeries to RadzenAreaSeries, set **Data** to `@@revenueByMonth`, and **CategoryProperty** to `Month`.

#### Revenue by employee chart

1. Duplicate the column from the previous step.
1. Set the **Text** of the header to `Revenue by employee`.
1. Invoke the `RevenueByEmployee` custom method in the Page **OnInitialized()** method. Create a page property called `revenueByEmployee` from the result.
1. Change RadzenColumnSeries to RadzenBarSeries, set **Data** to `@@revenueByEmployee`, and **CategoryProperty** to `Employee`.

Here is how the end result should look like.
![Crm Dashboard Chart](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-chart.png)

## Summary of recent opportunities and tasks

As usual we start with the layout.

1. Drag and drop a **Row**.
1. Drop a **Column** inside. Set its **XL** size to `6`.
1. Drop a **Card** inside the column.
1. Add a **Heading** inside the card.

### Recent opportunities

1. Add new injected Page property for `RadzenCRMService` and change `OnInitialized()` to be asynchronous. ![Crm Dashboard Opportunities Inject](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-opportunities-inject.png)
1. Drag and drop a **DataGrid** component below the heading.
1. Use **DataGrid** configuration wizard to bind the component to result of `GetOpportunities` data source method. Do not select any columns.
1. Select `Home.razor.cs`, choose **methods & design**, select method `OnInitializedAsync`, choose **Query Builder** from the properties panel and add `Contact,OpportunityStatus` as `expand` parameter.
1. Add a column and add to its **Template** two **Label** components with **Text** set to `@@context.Contact.FirstName` and `@@context.Contact.LastName`.
Set the **Title** to `Contact` and **SortProperty** to `Contact.FirstName`.
1. Add another column and set its **Property** to `Amount`. Set **Template** to `@@context.Amount.ToString("C")`.
1. Add a third column and set **Property** to `OpportunityStatus.Name` and **Title** to `Status`.
1. Add the last column. Set **Property** to `CloseDate`.

![Crm Dashboard Opportunities Data Grid](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard-opportunities-data-grid.png)

### Tasks

1. Duplicate the column.
1. Set the heading **Text** to `Active Tasks`.
1. Drag and drop new **DataGrid** component in the new column below the opportunities **DataGrid**.
1. Use **DataGrid** configuration wizard to bind the component to result of `GetTasks` data source method. Do not select any columns.

#### Server-side Blazor
We also need to include the `User` property in the result of the `GetTasks` operation.

1. Open the `Services\RadzenCRMService.Custom.cs` file.
1. Add the following method to the `RadzenCRMService` class:
   ```cs
   partial void OnTasksRead(ref IQueryable<CRMBlazorServerRBS.Models.RadzenCRM.Task> items)
   {
      items = items.Include(item => item.Opportunity.User).Include(item => item.Opportunity.Contact);
   }

   ```
![Crm Service Tasks Read](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-service-tasks-read.png)

#### Client-side WebAssembly Blazor

Set also `expand` parameter to `Opportunity($expand=User,Contact)`.

1. Add a new **DataGrid** column with **Title** `Employee` and **SortProperty** to `Opportunity.User.FirstName`. Edit its **Template**.
1. Drag and drop an **Image** component. Set its **Path** to `@@context.Opportunity.User.Picture`. Set **Width** and **Height** to `30px` and **BorderRadius** to `15px`.
1. Drag and drop a **Label** component. Set its **Text** to `@@context.Opportunity.User.FirstName`.
1. Drag and drop another **Label** component. Set its **Text** to `@@context.Opportunity.User.LastName`.
1. End template editing and add another column with **Property** set to `Title`.
1. Add another column. Set **SortProperty** to `Opportunity.Name`. Edit its **Template**.
1. Drag and drop a **Label** component. Set its **Text** to `@@context.Opportunity.Name`.
Go to **Style** and set **Display** to `block`. This will make the next label appear on a new line.
1. Drag and drop another **Label** component. Set its **Text** to `@@context.Opportunity.Contact.FirstName`.
1. Duplicate that label. Set the **Text** of the new one to `@@context.Opportunity.Contact.LastName` and end template editing.
1. Add one last column with **Property** set to `DueDate`.

The Dashboard is now complete! Here is how it will look at runtime.

# CRM Tutorial: Database Setup

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/database.md

> Create the MS SQL database for the Blazor CRM sample application.

# Database Setup | Create a Blazor CRM application with Radzen Blazor Studio
Radzen Blazor Studio applications typically start from the data. In this case we will use a MS SQL database that we will create from scratch.

## Create the database

First you have to create the tables that will store the CRM data: Contacts, Opportunities and tasks.

Fire up SQL Management Studio (or your other favorite DB management tool) create a database called `RadzenCRM` and add the following tables and foreign key relationships.

![Crm Database Tables](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-database-tables.png)

You can either create those visually or run [this SQL script](https://github.com/radzenhq/radzen-examples/blob/master/CRMBlazorServerRBS/crm-database-schema.sql).

## Create a Radzen Blazor Studio application

Now that we have a database for the CRM application it is time to start working in Radzen Blazor Studio.

1. Start Radzen Blazor Studio and click New Application.
![Crm Create](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-create.png)
1. Set the **Application Type** to **Blazor Server** and click Next.
![Crm Create1](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-create1.png)
1. Set the application **Name**, pick a directory where the application files will reside and click Finish.
![Crm Create2](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-create2.png)

1. Click the **Data** button that appears in the top left corner of Radzen Blazor Studio. Then add a new MS SQL Server data source. ![Crm Database Add Data Source](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-database-add-data-source.png) ![Crm Database Add Data Source1](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-database-add-data-source1.png)
Enter the connection info - server name, user and password (if using SQL server authentication) and select `RadzenCRM` database. ![Crm Database Add Data Source2](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-database-add-data-source2.png)
1. Click the **Infer schema** button. Radzen Blazor Studio will connect to the `RadzenCRM` database and infer its schema - tables, views and stored procedures (if there are any). ![Crm Database Schema](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-database-schema.png)
1. Check **Generate pages for CRUD operations**, **Export to Excel and CSV**, **Search as you type**, **Paging, sorting and filtering of lookup data** and `Filled` as **FormField variant**. Then click **Finish**. This will make Radzen Blazor Studio scaffold all checked tables as CRUD pages. **This feature is only available with an active subscription.**. ![Crm Database Scaffold](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-database-scaffold.png) ![Crm Database Scaffold1](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-database-scaffold1.png)

You now have a complete CRUD application which is ready for test. Click the **Run** button to see what you have created
in your browser.

![Crm Database Run](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-database-run.png)

The application doesn't show much at the moment because the database is still empty. Let's add some data.

1. Click **Opportunity Statuses** from the navigation menu. This loads the Opportunity Statuses page that displays all records from the OpportunityStatuses table (which is still empty by the way).
1. Click the **Add** button above the DataGrid to add some records to the OpportunityStatuses table. In the **Add Opportunity Status** dialog enter **Name** then click **Save**.
1. Add the following statuses: `Inactive`, `Won`, `Lost`, `Active`. Those represent the state a CRM opportunity could be in.
![Crm Database Opportunity Statuses](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-database-opportunity-statuses.png)
![Crm Database Opportunity Statuses1](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-database-opportunity-statuses1.png)

Then go to the **Task Statuses** page and add the following statuses: `Not Started`, `In Progress`, `Complete`. Those represent the state a CRM task could be in.
![Crm Database Task Statuses](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-database-task-statuses.png)

Finally go to the **Task Types** page and add the following task types: `Online Meeting`, `Email`, `Call`.
![Crm Database Task Types](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-database-task-types.png)

## Enable security

The typical web application has users that can log in and do certain things based on their role. Our `RadzenCRM` application is no exception!

Let's enable security and see how this affects the `RadzenCRM` database.

1. Go back to Radzen Blazor Studio and click the **Stop** button. This stops the running application.
1. Click the **Security** button in the top left corner of Radzen Blazor Studio. It displays the application security configuration page. ![Crm Database Security](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-database-security.png)
1. Choose **ASP.NET Core Identity** security type. ![Crm Database Security1](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-database-security1.png)
Then select `RadzenCRM` from the **Data Source** dropdown. This tells Radzen Blazor Studio what database to use to persist the users and roles.
Check **Auto generate pages for user and role management**. ![Crm Database Security2](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-database-security2.png)
1. Select `Filled` as **Login and security pages FormField variant**, click save and run the application again.

The application will start with the Login page. You can login with the test credentials `admin/admin` (available only during development).

![Crm Database Security3](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-database-security3.png)

When this happens the application will add a few more tables to the `RadzenCRM` database (all starting with `Asp`).

## Create a foreign key

The final step is to create a foreign key relationship between the `Opportunities` table and the `AspNetUsers` table. We need this to associate users with opportunities in our CRM application.

This step is done in SQL Management Studio and your favorite code editor (Visual Studio Code, Visual Studio Professional or anything else really).

1. Open SQL Management Studio or your favorite database management tool capable of running a SQL script.
1. Add a foreign key between the **Opportunities** and **AspNetUsers** table (Opportunities.UserID -> AspNetUsers.Id). You can run this SQL script:

   ```sql
   USE [RadzenCRM]
   GO

   ALTER TABLE [dbo].[Opportunities] WITH CHECK
   ADD CONSTRAINT [FK_Opportunities_AspNetUsers] FOREIGN KEY([UserId])
   REFERENCES [dbo].[AspNetUsers] ([Id])
   GO

   ALTER TABLE [dbo].[Opportunities] CHECK CONSTRAINT [FK_Opportunities_AspNetUsers]
   GO
   ```

#### Server-side Blazor
1. Add a new file `Models\RadzenCRM\Opportunity.Custom.cs` with the following content.

   ```cs
   using System;
   using System.Collections.Generic;
   using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations;
   using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations.Schema;

   namespace CRMBlazorServerRBS.Models.RadzenCRM
   {
       public partial class Opportunity
       {
           [ForeignKey("UserId")]
           public ApplicationUser User { get; set; }
       }
   }
   ```

![Crm Database Security4](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-database-security4.png)

#### Client-side WebAssembly Blazor
1. Add a new file `Server\Models\RadzenCRM\Opportunity.Custom.cs` with the following content.

   ```cs
   using System;
   using System.Collections.Generic;
   using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations;
   using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations.Schema;

   namespace CRMBlazorWasmRBS.Server.Models.RadzenCRM
   {
        public partial class Opportunity
        {
            [ForeignKey("UserId")]
            public ApplicationUser User { get; set; }
        }
   }
   ```

![Crm Database Security5](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-database-security5.png)

This extends the Opportunity model (a class which represents a record from the **Opportunities** table) with a new property `User` - the CRM application user it is related to.

Here is how the `RadzenCRM` database should look like after the last modification. ![Crm Database Full Schema](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-database-full-schema.png)

You are now ready to proceed to [Customize security](blazor-studio/documentation/crm/security).

---

# CRM Tutorial: Finishing Touches

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/finishing-touches.md

> Customize the navigation, show the current user picture, allow the current user to update his personal details.

# Finishing touches | Create a Blazor CRM application with Radzen Blazor Studio
In this final part of the CRM tutorial we will add a few final features that will make the CRM application more polished.

- Customize the navigation.
- Show the current user picture.
- Allow the current user to update his personal details - first name, last name and picture.
- Create custom design for the login page.

## Customize the navigation

We will rearrange the navigation, create a hierarchy, and add icons.

The application navigation typically lives in the **Main** layout. Layouts are special pages that define common
UI components that are shared between multiple pages.

1. Open the **Main** layout in Radzen Blazor Studio and select RadzenPanelMenu.
1. Set **Home** page RadzenPanelMenuItem **Text** to `Dashboard` and **Icon** to `home`.
1. Set **Contacts** **Icon** to `perm_contact_calendar`.
1. Make the **Tasks** page third and set the **Icon** to `work`.
1. Make **Opportunities** fourth and set the **Icon** to `shopping_cart`.
1. Add a new item with **Text** `Settings` and **Icon**: `settings`. Set the **Visible** property to `@@Security.IsInRole("Sales Manager")`.
This makes this item visible only to members of the `Sales Manager` role.
1. Add a child item with **Text** `Opportunity Statuses`, `Task Types` and `Task Statuses` as child items.
![Crm Finishing Touches Menu](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-finishing-touches-menu.png)

Now when a member of the `Sales Manager` role logs in she would see this navigation.
![Crm Finishing Touches Sales Manager](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-finishing-touches-sales-manager.png)
Members of the `Sales Representative` role will see this (note that the **Settings** menu item is not present).
![Crm Finishing Touches Sales Rep](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-finishing-touches-sales-rep.png)

## Show the current user picture

By default the **Main** layout has a **ProfileMenu** component which allows users to logout or update their profile.
Let's customize the **ProfileMenu** to show the current user name and profile picture.

1. Select the **ProfileMenu** component.
1. Click the **Edit template** button.
1. Delete the **Gravatar** component.
1. Drag and drop a **Label** component.
1. Set the **Text** of the **Label** to `@@Security.User.FirstName`.
1. Duplicate the **Label**. Set its **Text** to `@@Security.User.LastName`.
1. Drag and drop an **Image**. Set **Path** to `@@Security.User.Picture`. Set **Width** and **Height** to `32px` and **BorderRadius** to `16px`.
1. End template editing.

If you run the application from Radzen Blazor Studio you will see the current user picture and name in the top right corner.
![Crm Finishing Touches Profile Menu](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-finishing-touches-profile-menu.png)

## Update user details

When you enable security for a Radzen Blazor Studio application one of the scaffolded pages is **Profile** (also accessible from the **ProfileMenu** component in the top right corner).
By default it allows the current user to change their password. In the CRM application we have extended the **AspNetUsers** table with three new columns - `FirstName`, `LastName`, `Picture` and we want the
user to be able to change them.

### Create the UI

Now let's create the UI.

1. Open the **Profile** page.
1. Drag and drop a **Tabs** component.
1. Add two items: `Personal` and `Password`.
1. Select the `Password` tab and move the **TemplateForm** there.
1. Delete the now empty **Row**. ![Crm Finishing Touches Personal Password](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-finishing-touches-personal-password.png)
1. Select the `Personal` tab and drag and drop a new **TemplateForm** inside. Set its **Data** property to `@@user`.
1. Set the **Text** of the label to `First Name`. Set the **Value** of the **TextBox** to `@@user.FirstName`. Set the **Text** of the validator to `First Name is required`. ![Crm Finishing Touches Personal Form First Name](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-finishing-touches-personal-form-first-name.png)
1. Duplicate the first row of the form. Set the **Text** of the label to `Last Name`. Set **Component** to `LastName`. Set the **Value** of the **TextBox** to `@@user.LastName`. Set the **Text** of the validator to `Last Name is required`. Set **Component** to `TextBox2`. ![Crm Finishing Touches Personal Form Last Name](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-finishing-touches-personal-form-last-name.png)
1. Duplicate the second row of the form. Delete the **TextBox** and drop a **FileInput**.
Set the **Text** of the label to `Picture`. Set **Component** to `FileInput1`. Set the **Value** of the **FileInput** to `@@user.Picture` and its **Display** style property to `block`.
Set the **Text** of the validator to `Picture is required`. Set **Component** to `FileInput1`.
![Crm Finishing Touches Personal Form Picture](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-finishing-touches-personal-form-picture.png)

The final step is to update the personal data when the user submits the form.

1. Add a new handler for the form **Submit** event. ![Crm Finishing Touches Personal Form Submit](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-finishing-touches-personal-form-submit.png)
1. Invoke the `Security.UpdateUser` custom method. Set the `Id` parameter
  - Set the **Id** parameter to `@@Security.User.Id`
  - Set the **User** parameter to `@@user` ![Crm Finishing Touches Personal Form Submit Invoke](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-finishing-touches-personal-form-submit-invoke.png)
1. Display a notification to let the user know that their details have been updated.
![Crm Finishing Touches Personal Form Submit Then](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-finishing-touches-personal-form-submit-then.png)

Run the application to check the profile page!
![Crm Finishing Touches Profile](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-finishing-touches-profile.png)

## Custom login page

Finally let's create a custom login page by editing both the **Login** layout and page.

### Login layout

We will add a background image that will cover the whole page. Also we will add the CRM application logo.

#### Add the assets

Radzen Blazor Studio allows you to use images seamlessly. For this demo we will use a [background](/images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-login-background.png).
Download this file and add it as assets in the application (wwwroot\images).

#### Set the background image

1. Open the **Login** layout.
1. Select **RadzenLayout** component and change the background image to **crm-login-background.png**.
![Crm Finishing Touches Login Background](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-finishing-touches-login-background.png)
![Crm Finishing Touches Login Background1](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-finishing-touches-login-background1.png)

### Login page

Let's now customize the **Login** page.

#### Customize the login form

1. Open the **Login** page and set **ShowLoginButton** to `false` for **Login** component.
1. Drag a **SplitButton** component after the **Login** component, set **Text** to `Login`, **ButtonStyle** to `Primary`, **Float** to `right` and add two items with **Text** `Sales Manager` and `Sales Representative`. ![Crm Finishing Touches Login Button](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-finishing-touches-login-button.png)
1. Add **SplitButton** component **Click** event. ![Crm Finishing Touches Login Button Click](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-finishing-touches-login-button-click.png)
1. Add the following code to the **SplitButton** component **Click** event:
   ```cs
   string theForm = "document.forms[0]";

   protected async System.Threading.Tasks.Task SplitButton0Click(Radzen.Blazor.RadzenSplitButtonItem args)
   {
        if(args?.Text == "Sales Manager")
        {
            await SetLoginCredentials("salesmanager@@demo.radzen.com", "SalesManager1@@");
        }
        else if(args?.Text == "Sales Representative")
        {
            await SetLoginCredentials("salesrep@@demo.radzen.com", "SalesRep1@@");
        }

        await JSRuntime.InvokeVoidAsync("eval", $@@"{theForm}.submit()");
   }

   protected async System.Threading.Tasks.Task SetLoginCredentials(string username, string password)
   {
        await JSRuntime.InvokeVoidAsync("eval", $@@"{theForm}.Username.value = '{username}'");
        await JSRuntime.InvokeVoidAsync("eval", $@@"{theForm}.Password.value = '{password}'");
   }
   ```
That is all!

![Crm Finishing Touches Login](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-finishing-touches-login.png)

## Complete source

The complete source of this application (with a few additional changes that are mostly cosmetic) is available for [server-side Blazor](https://github.com/radzenhq/radzen-blazor-studio/tree/main/CRMBlazorServerRBS) and for [client-side WebAssembly Blazor](https://github.com/radzenhq/radzen-blazor-studio/tree/main/CRMBlazorWasmRBS) in the Radzen github repository.

# CRM Tutorial: Create a Blazor CRM application with Radzen Blazor Studio

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/introduction.md

> Specification, features and steps of creating a Blazor CRM application with Radzen Blazor Studio.

# Create a Blazor CRM application with Radzen Blazor Studio
In this tutorial you will learn how to create a complete Blazor application with Radzen Blazor Studio.

## Specification

The application is a CRM (Customer Relationship Management) with the following features:

- Support users of two roles - Sales Representative and Sales Manager. ![Crm Finishing Touches Login](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-finishing-touches-login.png)
- Contact management - add, search and update contacts.![Crm Customize Crud Contacts](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-customize-crud-contacts.png)
- Opportunity management - create opportunities for existing contacts and change their status.![Crm Customize Crud Opportunity User1](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-customize-crud-opportunity-user1.png)
- Task management - create and edit tasks (phone call, meeting etc.) associated with opportunities.![Crm Customize Crud Task Type Icons](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-customize-crud-task-type-icons.png)
- Display data-driven company performance metrics in a dashboard. ![Crm Dashboard](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-dashboard.png)

## Requirements

To create the application you need:

1. A working Radzen Blazor Studio installation.
1. A running Microsoft SQL Server instance (the free Express version will suffice).
1. SQL Server Management Studio (or some other tool that supports database table design).
1. Understanding of C# and Entity Framework core (to create the custom DB queries needed by the dashboard).

## Implementation

The application relies on the following Radzen Blazor Studio features:

- [CRUD page scaffolding from a database](blazor-studio/documentation/databases) to automatically generate most of the application.
- [Security](blazor-studio/documentation/security/identity) to support user management, login and roles.
- [WYSIWYG Design-time](blazor-studio/documentation/design-time/introduction) to customize the application visually.
- [Custom methods](blazor-studio/documentation/design-time/methods-and-statements) to get real-time performance metrics via database queries.

## Steps

The application is created in the following steps:

1. [Database](blazor-studio/documentation/crm/database)
Shows how to create the database, enable security and set up relationships.
1. [Customize security](blazor-studio/documentation/crm/security)
Allow the users to upload their picture and set their first and last name, assign page permissions.
1. [Customize CRUD pages](blazor-studio/documentation/crm/customize-crud)
Apply various visual customizations, implement contact search.
1. [Create dashboard](blazor-studio/documentation/crm/dashboard)
Create a dashboard page that uses charts, data grids and cards to display some vital performance metrics. Query the database with custom code to get
the required data.
1. [Finishing touches](blazor-studio/documentation/crm/finishing-touches)
Customize the login screen, display the picture of the logged in user, customize the navigation menu.

If you are impatient you can check the final result in the Radzen Github repository for [server-side Blazor](https://github.com/radzenhq/radzen-blazor-studio/tree/main/CRMBlazorServerRBS) and for [client-side WebAssembly Blazor](https://github.com/radzenhq/radzen-blazor-studio/tree/main/CRMBlazorWasmRBS).

# CRM Tutorial: Customize security

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/security.md

> Extend the Blazor CRM application user with additional properties - first and last name, ability to upload a picture.

# Customize security | Create a Blazor CRM application with Radzen Blazor Studio
In this step from the CRM Application tutorial we will customize the security settings:

- Add FirstName, LastName and Picture columns to the **AspNetUsers** table.
- Customize the user management pages - **Add Application User**, **Application Users** and optionally **Edit Application User**.
- Create some roles and add a couple of users.
- Set page permissions.

## Extend the AspNetUsers table

Radzen Blazor Studio applications come with a built-in security feature which relies on [ASP.NET Core Identity](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/security/authentication/identity).
ASP.NET Core Identity is backed up by a set of tables that are created via Entity Framework Core migrations automatically the first time you log in your Radzen Blazor Studio application.

Application users are stored in the **AspNetUsers** table which by default looks like this:

<img src="images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-security-aspnet-users.png" width="200" loading="lazy">

Yes, by default it has only the most basic info. Let's change that by adding FirstName, LastName and Picture columns.
This time though we are not going to edit the database in SQL Server Management Studio or run SQL. Remember that
ASP.NET Identity relies on Entity Framework Migrations which use code to create the underlying tables and columns.

1. Add a new file `Models\ApplicationUser.Custom.cs` with the following content.
   #### Server-side Blazor
   ```cs
   using System;
   using System.Collections.Generic;
   using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations;
   using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations.Schema;

   namespace CRMBlazorServerRBS.Models
   {
        public partial class ApplicationUser
        {
            public string FirstName { get; set; }
            public string LastName { get; set; }
            public string Picture { get; set; }
        }
   }
   ```

   #### Client-side WebAssembly Blazor
   Add a new file `Server\Models\ApplicationUser.Custom.cs` with the following content.
   ```cs
   using System;
   using System.Collections.Generic;
   using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations;
   using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations.Schema;

   namespace CRMBlazorWasmRBS.Server.Models
   {
       public partial class ApplicationUser
       {
           public string FirstName { get; set; }
           public string LastName { get; set; }
           public string Picture { get; set; }
       }
   }
   ```
   The `ApplicationUser` class represents a record from the **AspNetUsers** table and by adding those three properties
   we extend it.
1. Add a new file `Data\RadzenCRMContext.Custom.cs` with the following content.
   #### Server-side Blazor
   ```cs
   using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
   using CRMBlazorServerRBS.Models.RadzenCRM;

   namespace CRMBlazorServerRBS.Data
   {
       public partial class RadzenCRMContext
       {
           partial void OnModelBuilding(ModelBuilder builder)
           {
               builder.Entity<ApplicationUser>().ToTable("AspNetUsers";
           }
       }
   }")

   ```

   #### Client-side WebAssembly Blazor
   Add a new file `Server\Data\RadzenCRMContext.Custom.cs` with the following content.
   ```cs
   using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
   using CRMBlazorWasmRBS.Server.Models;

   namespace CRMBlazorWasmRBS.Server.Data
   {
       public partial class RadzenCRMContext
       {
           partial void OnModelBuilding(ModelBuilder builder)
           {
               builder.Entity<ApplicationUser>().ToTable("AspNetUsers";
           }
       }
   }")

   ```
1. Add a new file `Controllers\ApplicationUsersController.Custom.cs` with the following content.
   #### Server-side Blazor
   ```cs
   using System;
   using System.Linq;
   using CRMBlazorServerRBS.Models;

   namespace CRMBlazorServerRBS.Controllers
   {
        public partial class ApplicationUsersController
        {
            partial void OnUserUpdated(ApplicationUser user)
            {
                var item = context.Users.Where(u => u.Id == user.Id).FirstOrDefault();
                if(user != null)
                {
                    item.FirstName = user.FirstName;
                    item.LastName = user.LastName;
                    item.Picture = user.Picture;
                }
            }
        }
   }

   ```

   #### Client-side WebAssembly Blazor
   Add a new file `Server\Controllers\ApplicationUsersController.Custom.cs` with the following content.
   ```cs
   using System;
   using System.Linq;
   using CRMBlazorWasmRBS.Server.Models;

   namespace CRMBlazorWasmRBS.Server.Controllers
   {
        public partial class ApplicationUsersController
        {
            partial void OnUserUpdated(ApplicationUser user)
            {
                var item = context.Users.Where(u => u.Id == user.Id).FirstOrDefault();
                if(user != null)
                {
                    item.FirstName = user.FirstName;
                    item.LastName = user.LastName;
                    item.Picture = user.Picture;
                }
            }
        }
   }

   ```
1. Open a command prompt window and go to the directory (or Server directory in case of WebAssembly) of the CRM application.
1. Run the following command (it will take some time to complete):
   ```
   dotnet ef migrations add ExtendApplicationUser -c ApplicationIdentityDbContext
   ```
   This command uses the Entity Framework Core tooling to add the `FirstName`, `LastName` and `Picture` columns to the **AspNetUsers** table.
1. Open the generated migration class in `Data/Migrations/XXX_ExtendApplicationUser.cs` to check if newly added properties are there.
   > If you haven't installed the EF Core tools before that command will fail. Run `dotnet tool install --global dotnet-ef` to install them.

Now that we have added three new columns it is time to update the Add and Edit Application User pages.

## Update the user management pages

Radzen Blazor Studio has scaffolded pages for managing application users. We will now update those pages to allow setting the new database columns.

We will start from the **Add Application User** page.

1. Open the **Add Application User** page in Radzen Blazor Studio.
1. Duplicate the "Email" **FormField** from the page. ![Crm Security Application Users First Name](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-security-application-users-first-name.png)
1. Select the **TextBox** and set its **Value** property to `@@user.FirstName`. This will data-bind the text box to the `FirstName` property of the `ApplicationUser` class (which we added in the previous step).
1. Select the **FormField** and set its **Text** property to `First Name`.
1. Finally select the **RequiredValidatorComponent** below the text box. Set its **Text** to `First Name is required`. Set its **Component** property to `FirstName`.
![Crm Security Application Users First Name1](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-security-application-users-first-name1.png)

1. Perform steps 1 - 5 for the `LastName` property.
1. Duplicate a form row once again. Delete the **TextBox** component. Drag-and-drop a **FileInput** component.
Set its **Value** property to `@@user.Picture`. It will allow the user to upload a picture which will be saved in the `AspNetUsers` table (in the `Picture` column).
1. Change the **Label** text to `Picture`.
1. Set the **Text** of the **RequiredValidator** to `Picture is required`. Set its **Component** property to `Picture`.
1. Set **TemplateForm** `Visible="@@(user != null)"` to avoid errors when the user is still not loaded.

Optionally you can perform those above steps to add FirstName, LastName and Picture to the **Edit Application User** page.

Let's now update the **Application Users** page to show FirstName, LastName and Picture in the DataGrid.

1. Open the **Application Users** page in Radzen Blazor Studio.
1. Select the **DataGrid** component.
1. Add a new data grid column by clicking the **+** button next to the **Columns** label in the property grid. The new column goes last. Scroll to the bottom of the property grid.
1. Pick `FirstName` from the **Property** dropdown. This specifies what property (database column) this column will display.
1. Now perform steps 1-4 for the `LastName` column.

We now need to add a data grid column to display the `Picture` column of the **AspNetUsers** table.

1. Add a column for the `Picture` property by following the steps above. Then click the **Edit** button next to **Template**. We need to add an **Image** component in this column to display the user picture stored in the database.
1. Drag and drop an **Image** component from the Radzen Blazor Studio toolbox. Set its **Path** property to `@@user.Picture`. ![Crm Security Application Users Picture](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-security-application-users-picture.png)
1. Go to the **Style** tab of the property grid. It allows you to specify various visual component settings. Set **Width** to `30px` and **Height** to `30px`.
1. Click **End template editing**. ![Crm Security Application Users Picture1](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-security-application-users-picture1.png)

## Create roles and users

Now that we have customized the security pages it is time to add roles and users.

### Add the roles

1. Run the application in Radzen Blazor Studio and log in with `admin/admin`.
1. In your browser go to the application menu in the top right corner.
1. Click **Roles**. This loads the role management pages.
1. Add two roles: `Sales Manager` and `Sales Representative`.

![Crm Security Create Roles](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-security-create-roles.png)

### Add the users

1. In your browser go to the application menu in the top right corner.
1. Click **Users**. This loads the user management pages.
1. Add a new user with the following attributes:
  - **Email**: `salesmanager@@demo.radzen.com`
  - **First Name**: `Jane`
  - **Last Name**: `Smith`
  - **Roles**: check `Sales Manager`
  - Upload some photo for the **Picture** (we will use [this](/images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/jane.png))
  - **Password** and **Confirm password**: `SalesManager1@@`
  ![Crm Security Create User Jane](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-security-create-user-jane.png)
1. Add a second user with the following attributes:
  - **Email**: `salesrep@@demo.radzen.com`
  - **First Name**: `John`
  - **Last Name**: `Doe`
  - **Roles**: check `Sales Representative`
  - Upload some photo for the **Picture** (we will use [this](/images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/john.png))
  - **Password** and **Confirm password**: `SalesRep1@@`
  ![Crm Security Create User John](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-security-create-user-john.png)

And we are done with the users!
![Crm Security Users](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-security-users.png)

## Set page permissions

We would now allow only the members of the `Sales Manager` role to create new users and roles as well as opportunity statuses, task types and task statuses.

1. Go back to Radzen Blazor Studio and stop the running application.
1. Open the **Add Application User** page, clear the existing **Access** from the property grid and select only **Sales Manager** role. This will make the **Add Application User** page available only to members of the **Sales Manager** role. ![Crm Security Set Access](images/blazor-studio/documentation/crm/crm-security-set-access.png)
1. Repeat steps 2 and 3 for **Application Users**, **Application Roles**, **Edit Application User**, **Add Application Role**, etc.

We are now ready to [Customize the CRUD pages](blazor-studio/documentation/crm/customize-crud).
