# Troubleshooting

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-studio/documentation/troubleshooting.md

> Troubleshooting common issues with Radzen Blazor Studio.

# Troubleshooting
## Build error

Radzen Blazor Studio builds your application in order to show it in design time. Sometimes this build fails and you will see the "Oh, no! The build failed." message
which also asks you to check the Output window. The build could fail for two reasons:

1. Your application doesn't build in general in its current state. If your application fails to build in Visual Studio or from command line then it
won't build in Radzen Blazor Studio as well. Fix the reported errors and try again.
1. Your application builds and runs as expected but Radzen Blazor Studio fails with the design-time build. This usually happens when Radzen Blazor Studio
didn't recognize some vital part of your application startup and didn't include it in the design-time build - some service registration for example. In other
cases it is some startup code that throws an exception during design-time build. You can use Radzen Blazor Studio to [analyze](#analyze) your project for problems
and [send](#report-issue) us the output.

### Hide code from design-time builds

Use the `RADZEN` preprocessor constant if there is code you don't want Radzen Blazor Studio to include in design-time builds.

#### In C# files
```cs
#if !RADZEN
// This code will not be included in Radzen Blazor Studio design-time builds
builder.Services.AddScoped<ITradeService, TradeService>();
#endif

```

#### In razor files
```
@{ #if !RADZEN }
<RadzenButton Text="Hidden in design builds" />
@{ #endif }

```

### Preview and release candidate versions of .NET
Sometimes the design time build would fail with errors such as `CS0246: The type or namespace name 'App' could not be found`. This isually means that you have installed a preview or release candidate version
of the .NET framework which Radzen Blazor Studio does not support. Visual Stidio 2022 Preview installs such .NET framework versions.

You can find the latest installed version by running `dotnet --info` in command prompt.

To solve this problem you have two options:

- Uninstall the preview version and install the [latest official version of .NET 10](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/10.0). If it has been installed by Visual Studio 2022 Preview you would need to uninstall the VS 2022 Preview itself and
get the [RTM version](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/vs).
- Create a [global.json](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/tools/global-json) file in the directory of your application with the following contents:

```json
{
  "sdk": {
    "version": "10.0.100"
  }
}
```

## Render error

Sometimes certain pages may fail to display in Radzen Blazor Studio. You will see the "Oh, no! Page threw exception during rendering." message.

Radzen Blazor Studio does not execute the Blazor lifecycle methods of your pages in order to prevent unwanted side effects such as database access,
HTTP requests or file system access. Instead it adds code that initializes the page members (properties and fields) with sample data. This process
could fail in some cases. You can use Radzen Blazor Studio to [analyze](#analyze) your project for problems
and [send](#report-issue) us the output.

## Package restore errors

If you get `error NU1301: Failed to retrieve information about XXX from remote source` make sure the default NuGet package source is
`nuget.org`. Any third party package sources should come after it. You can verify that [from Visual Studio](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/nuget/consume-packages/install-use-packages-visual-studio#package-sources).

## Analyze

Radzen Blazor Studio can analyze your project for potential design-time build or render issues. If you experience problems here is how to run the analysis.

> Note: The analyze option requires Radzen Blazor Studio 1.0.6+.

You can terminate the analysis at any time by pressing <kbd>CTRL+C</kbd> (Windows) or <kbd>CMD+C</kbd> (macOS).

### Analyze on Windows

Open a command prompt. Then run the following command

```
dotnet "c:\Program Files\Radzen Blazor Studio\resources\Radzen.Server\Radzen.Server.dll" --analyze <path to the .sln or .csproj of your application> -o <log file>

```

For example

```
dotnet "c:\Program Files\Radzen Blazor Studio\resources\Radzen.Server\Radzen.Server.dll" --analyze c:\apps\BlazorApp\BlazorApp.sln -o log.txt
```

![Analyze Windows](images/blazor-studio/documentation/analyze-windows.png)

This command will analyze the `c:\apps\BlazorApp\BlazorApp.sln` solution and output the information to the `log.txt` file. You can omit the `-o log.txt` parameter if you
want to see the output in the console.

### Analyze on macOS

Open a terminal. Then run the following command

```
dotnet /Applications/Radzen\ Blazor\ Studio.app/Contents/Resources/Radzen.Server/Radzen.Server.dll --analyze <path to the .sln or .csproj of your application> -o <log file>

```

For example

```
dotnet /Applications/Radzen\ Blazor\ Studio.app/Contents/Resources/Radzen.Server/Radzen.Server.dll --analyze ~/apps/BlazorApp/BlazorApp.sln -o log.txt
```
This command will analyze the `~/apps/BlazorApp/BlazorApp.sln` solution and output the information to the `log.txt` file. You can omit the `-o log.txt` parameter if you
want to see the output in the console.

## Report an issue

If you hit a problem with Radzen Blazor Studio you can report it by:

- Starting a [forum thread](https://forum.radzen.com/c/radzen-blazor-studio)
- Sending us an email to info@@radzen.com (only for users that have an active subscription)

If you have a log file from [analyzing](#analyze) your project attach it to your report.

## Log file
Radzen Blazor Studio logs various info (including unexpected exceptions and other problems). The location depends on the host OS:

### Windows
`%APPDATA%\Radzen Blazor Studio\log.txt`
### macOS
`~/Library/Application Support/Radzen Blazor Studio/log.txt`
### Linux
`~/.config/Radzen Blazor Studio/log.txt` or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/Radzen Blazor Studio/log.txt`

## CSS does not load in design time
Radzen Blazor Studio will search for `_Host.cshtml` or `index.html` files in your application and parse them for CSS and JS.
It also supports component specific CSS files (`*.razor.css`).

If you are including a CSS file by other means they may not display in design-time.

## Code in lifecycle methods does not execute in design-time

Radzen Blazor Studio does not execute the Blazor lifecycle methods of your pages in order to prevent unwanted side effects such as database access,
HTTP requests or file system access. Instead it adds code that initializes the page members (properties and fields) with sample data.

You can enable the Blazor lifecycle from Radzen Blazor Studio settings (the <img style="vertical-align: middle; width: 32px" src="images/blazor-studio/documentation/settings-button.png" loading="lazy"> button in the bottom left corner). Do so at your own risk.

## Changes do not appear when the application is run
Radzen Blazor Studio does not automatically save file changes. Press `ctrl+S` to save the current file or `ctrl+alt+S` to save all open files.

# Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio Docs

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-visual-studio/documentation.md

> Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio overview. Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio extension increases development speed, and reduces repetitive coding allowing you to focus on building exceptional applications.

# Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio Documentation

The **Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio** extension helps you build Blazor applications faster and with less repetitive code.
It lets you design pages visually using a familiar WYSIWYG interface - right inside Visual Studio.

## Get Started in Minutes

## Get Started in Minutes

1. Install **Visual Studio 2022** or **Visual Studio 2026**.  
   .NET **10** is required. If you use Visual Studio 2022, install the .NET 10 SDK from https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/10.0.
1. Install the latest version of **Visual Studio 2022**, which includes support for **.NET 9**. The minimum required version is **17.12.35504.99**. All Visual Studio editions are supported - Community, Professional, and Enterprise.
2. [Install the Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio extension](/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/install) from the **Extension Manager**.
3. Create a new **Radzen Blazor** application, or open an existing **Razor** application.

That’s it - you’re ready to start designing Blazor apps visually within Visual Studio.

## Get Help

If you need assistance or have a question, visit the [Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio forum](https://forum.radzen.com/c/radzen-blazor-visual-studio).

You’ll find community discussions, troubleshooting tips, and help from the Radzen team.

---

# Applications

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/applications.md

> Create new Radzen Blazor applications in Visual Studio. Generate scaffolding, select rendering modes, apply templates, and connect data sources with the application wizard.

# Applications

## Create a New Application

<YouTube Video="VUwy-BX3eCM" />

Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio lets you create **Blazor Web** applications that target **.NET 8** or **.NET 9**.
If you want to build apps for .NET 8, make sure the **.NET 8 SDK** is also installed.

All generated applications use the **Radzen.Blazor** component library.

### Steps

1. In Visual Studio, go to **File > New Project**.
   This opens the **Create a new project** dialog.
2. Search for and select the **Radzen Blazor Application** template.
3. Enter a **project name** and choose a **location**.
   Click **Create** to start the Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio application wizard.
4. Choose a **rendering mode**.
   All interactive modes are supported - **Server**, **WebAssembly**, and **Auto**.
   Interactivity is enabled globally.
5. Select a **theme** for your application.
6. Click **Finish** to create the project.

Your new application is ready to open and run inside Visual Studio.

# What's new

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/changelog.md

> Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio release notes. See the latest updates, features, and improvements for the Visual Studio extension and download previous versions.

# What's new
## v1.41.1

### Improvements
- Updated premium themes.

### Fixes
- Design-time build fails with a duplicate variable error when two same-named locals live in sibling scopes such as try blocks or nested blocks.

## v1.41.0

### Improvements
- Added design-time support for the new Radzen.Blazor 11 components.
- Added support for the Material 3 Expressive and Material 3 Expressive Dark themes.
- Updated premium themes.

## v1.40.4

### Fixes
- Pages and components do not render in Design Mode when the project contains a partial type declared without an access modifier.

## v1.40.3

### Fixes
- Pages and components in a Razor Class Library do not render at design time, especially when they inject services the host application registers.
- A project fails to build at design time with an inconsistent accessibility error (CS0060) when a base class has no explicit access modifier.
- Analyzing a Razor component that lives in a class library project crashes.
- The DataGrid configuration wizard fails for OData methods.

## v1.40.2

### Fixes
- Scripts referenced in App.razor with the @@Assets[] helper are not loaded in the designer, so components that call their global JavaScript functions from lifecycle methods throw an error at design time.

## v1.40.1

### Fixes
- Opening a page whose base class is declared in another project of the solution fails with "Inconsistent syntax tree features" when the projects are compiled with different compiler features (e.g. .NET 10 Blazor WebAssembly applications).

## v1.40.0

### Improvements
- Components that depend on services registered through an `IHostApplicationBuilder` extension method (e.g. `builder.AddMyServices()`) now render in the designer, including when the components come from a NuGet package.

## v1.39.0

### Improvements
- Added a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server so AI coding agents can scaffold pages and applications, edit components, and manage themes and data sources.
- Updated premium themes.

### Fixes
- Design-time build fails with CS0149 when the application configures Serilog through ReadFrom.Services or ReadFrom.Configuration.
- Drill-down reports do not work in generated applications.

## v1.38.2

### Improvements
- Updated premium themes.

### Fixes
- Malformed Razor is generated for FK lookups when schema-prefixed entity names do not match the EF navigation names.
- Stored procedure input parameters are missing from WASM export URLs.
- Empty `[Column]` attribute is generated on scaffolded entity properties.

### Fixes
- The property grid sometimes steals the focus from the code editor.
## v1.0.10
### Improvements
- Infer component type argument when setting a property from the property grid.
### Fixes
- Type arguments of components are not set after drag and drop from the toolbox.

## v1.0.9
### Improvements
- Show the property grid after dragging and dropping an item from the toolbox.
### Fixes
- Cannot drag and drop components from the toolbox inside other components.
- The toolbox stays empty in some cases and asks the user to open a .razor file even though one is already open.
- Concurrency exception is sometimes thrown while trying to populate the toolbox.

## v1.0.8
### Fixes
- Design-time build sometimes fails with a web asset related exception.
- `NullReference` exception is sometimes thrown while populating the toolbox.

## v1.0.7
### Improvements
- Add additional logging when design-time startup fails.

## v1.0.6
### Improvements
- Allow the developer to change the current application theme.
- Improve the toolbox behavior - populate on demand, display message when there is no razor file opened.

## v1.0.5
### Improvements
- Use a higher contrast color for the design time selection.
### Fixes
- Context menu icons are not visible in dark Visual Studio themes.
- Cannot select some disabled components.

## v1.0.4
### Fixes
- Unhandled exceptions sometimes lead to a crash.

## v1.0.3
### Improvements
- Allow the developer to change the default edit mode from the options (split, design or source).
### Fixes
- Crash while trying to display the toolbox in some applications.

## v1.0.2

### Improvements
- Add helpful links to the **Extensions** and **Help** menu items.
- The **Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio** context menu item will check if the `Radzen.Blazor` package is installed.
### Fixes
- Generates wrong code when the data source wizard is started from a client project.

## v1.0.1
First official release of Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio.

### Available features
- WYSIWYG design time support with split view between design and source.
- Radzen Blazor application project template.
- Blazor component toolbox.
- Blazor component property grid.
- Scaffolding templates for pages, layouts, databases, security and localization.

# Work with Components

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/components.md

> Working with components in Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio

# Components
This article shows how to work with Blazor components in Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio.

## Add a component
To add a toolbox item to your `.razor` file perform the following steps:

1. Open a `.razor` file by double clicking it in Solution Explorer.
1. Go to **View &#x2192; Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio &#x2192; Toolbox** in the Visual Studio top menu.
1. Find the desired component. You can switch between Advanced mode (listing all components available for the current application) and Simple mode (showing only the Radzen.Blazor components grouped by category).
1. Drag and drop the component in the opened `.razor` file.

<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/design-time-intro-property-grid-toolbox.gif" alt="How to use the toolbox" loading="lazy">

## Select
You can select a component in one of the following ways:

- By clicking it in the design canvas.
<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/select-component.gif" alt="Select component" loading="lazy">
- From the **Outline**
<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/outline.gif" alt="Select a component from the outline" loading="lazy">
- You can also select the parent or first child of the selected component.
<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/select-toolbar.gif" alt="Select a parent or child component" loading="lazy">

You can select multiple components by holding <kbd>CTRL</kbd> while clicking components in the design canvas or in the outline.

You can also select a range of components by selecting one component and then selecting another while pressing <kbd>SHIFT</kbd>.

## Move
To move components:

1. Select one or more components.
1. Drag the move handle to the desired location.
1. Release the mouse button to complete.

<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/move-component.gif" alt="Move a component" loading="lazy">

## Cut, copy and paste
You can cut, copy and paste components by selecting them and pressing <kbd>CTRL+X</kbd>, <kbd>CTRL+C</kbd>, <kbd>CTRL+V</kbd>
You can also use the component context menu or the "..." button in the component toolbar.

<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/copy-paste-component.gif" alt="Copy and paste a component" loading="lazy">
## Delete
You can delete component by selecting it first and then clicking the **Delete** button from the toolbar "..." menu. You can also use the context menu or backspace.
<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/delete-component.gif" alt="Delete component" loading="lazy">

## Set properties
After selecting a Blazor component you will see all of its parameters (properties that are decorated with the `[Parameter]` attribute) in the property grid.

Use the property grid to set the desired property value. Do not add quotes (`"`) for string values - Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio will add them for you.
<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/set-property.gif" alt="Set property via the property grid" loading="lazy">

You can also click the **gear** icon which will open the **Expression** editor. You can pick an existing page property or field.
<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/expression-editor.gif" alt="Use the expression editor to set a property" loading="lazy">

Radzen Blazor For Visual Studio uses `@@bind-` syntax by default for properties that support two-way data-binding (e.g. `Value` property and `ValueChanged` event).
You can use the **&lt;-->** button to change that e.g. from `@@bind-Value="value"` to `Value="value"`.
<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/bind-value.gif" alt="Toggle two-way data-binding" loading="lazy">

## Attributes
Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio allows you to set custom attributes of HTML elements or Blazor components that support that (have a property decorated with `[Parameter(CaptureUnmatchedValues = true)]`).

To add a custom attribute to a Blazor component click the **+** button next to the **Custom attributes** label. Pick a name for the attribute and type its value.
<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/add-custom-attribute.gif" alt="Add custom attribute" loading="lazy">

## CSS style
The **Styles** tab of the property grid allows you to customize the appearance of the selected Blazor component or HTML element. Radzen Blazor For Visual Studio generates a `style` attribute when
you change any of the style attributes.

<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/styles.gif" alt="Set the CSS style" loading="lazy">

## Events
You can handle Blazor component events from the **Events** tab of the property grid. Click the **+** next to the event name. Radzen Blazor For Visual Studio will open a dialog
asking you to enter a name for the event handler method (a default name would be suggested). After that it will open the newly created method in design mode and allow you
to add statements to it.

<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/add-event-handler.gif" alt="Add event handler" loading="lazy">

## Templates
Radzen Blazor For Visual Studio has a special design time mode for template properties (properties of type `RenderFragment` or `RenderFragment<T>`). Click the **pencil** icon and Radzen
Blazor Studio will switch to template edit mode. Dragging and dropping components will add them inside the template property tag. If you open the **Expression** editor
you can access template context properties via the `context` parameter. Press the **Done** button when you have finished editing the template.

<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/set-template.gif" alt="Set component template" loading="lazy">

## Text
Radzen Blazor For Visual Studio includes a special **Text** component which allows you to set the text content of a HTML element, Blazor component or use text without an HTML element whatsoever.
To set the content of a Text component simply select it in the designer and update its Value property from the property grid.
<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/use-text.gif" alt="Use the Text toolbox item" loading="lazy">

> Note: Adding a Text item before or after an existing Text item will merge them together.

## Expression
The **Expression** component is another Radzen Blazor For Visual Studio toolbox item which allows you to display C# values e.g. `@@counter`.

<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/use-expression.gif" alt="Use the Expression toolbox item" loading="lazy">

---

# User Interface Overview

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/introduction.md

> Working with the design time features of Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio

# Design time
This article shows how to use the Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio design time features.

## WYSIWYG Editor
The WYSIWYG (What You See Is What You Get) editor is one of the commonly used features of Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio. It activates as soon as you open a `.razor` file.

<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/design-time-intro-wysiwyg.gif" alt="Image showing the WYSIWYG editor" / loading="lazy">

> TIP: You can chang the default edit mode (design, split or source) from the Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio settings available in **Tools &#x2192; Options &#x2192; Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio**.

You get instant feedback while coding. There is no need to run your application after every change.

<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/design-time-intro-changes-preview.gif" alt="Instant preview after making changes" / loading="lazy">

## Property Grid
The Radzen Blazor Property Grid allows you to visually configure Blazor components. Experiment with different settings to complete your task quickly.

<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/design-time-intro-property-grid.png" alt="The Radzen Blazor Property Grid" style="width: 50%" loading="lazy">

To activate the property grid:

1. Open a `.razor` file by double clicking it in Solution Explorer.
1. Go to **View &#x2192; Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio &#x2192; Properties** in the Visual Studio top menu.
1. Select a component from the WYSIWYG editor by clicking it.
1. Change the value of any property.

> TIP: When typing in a textbox of the property grid press <kbd>ENTER</kbd> to apply your changes and get a preview.

<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/design-time-intro-property-grid-activate.gif" alt="How to activate the property grid" loading="lazy">

## Toolbox
The Radzen Blazor Toolbox allows you to drag and drop Blazor components in a `.razor` file.

<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/design-time-intro-toolbox.png" alt="The Radzen Blazor Toolbox" style="width: 30%" loading="lazy">

To use the toolbox:

1. Open a `.razor` file by double clicking it in Solution Explorer.
1. Go to **View &#x2192; Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio &#x2192; Toolbox** in the Visual Studio top menu.
1. Find the desired component. You can switch between Advanced mode (listing all components available for the current application) and Simple mode (showing only the Radzen.Blazor components grouped by category).
1. Drag and drop the component in the opened `.razor` file.

<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/design-time-intro-property-grid-toolbox.gif" alt="How to use the toolbox" loading="lazy">

## Theme
If your application uses the Radzen.Blazor component library you can use the theme tool to change the current theme or customize it to your needs.

<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/design-time-intro-theme.png" alt="The Radzen Blazor Theme" style="width: 30%" loading="lazy">

> Note: The premium themes and theme customization are not available during trial.

To activate the Radzen Blazor Theme:

1. Open a `.razor` file by double clicking it in Solution Explorer.
1. Go to **View &#x2192; Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio &#x2192; Theme** in the Visual Studio top menu.
1. Pick a different theme or customize the current one.

<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/design-time-intro-theme.gif" alt="How to active the theme tool" loading="lazy">

## Outline
The Radzen Blazor Outline shows all Blazor components in the currently opened `.razor` file and allows you to quickly find the one you need to customize.

<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/design-time-intro-outline.png" alt="The Radzen Blazor Outline" style="width: 30%" loading="lazy">

To activate the outline:

1. Open a `.razor` file by double clicking it in Solution Explorer.
1. Go to **View &#x2192; Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio &#x2192; Outline** in the Visual Studio top menu.
1. Select a component from the tree. You can use the context menu to perform various operation over the selection.

<img src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/design-time/design-time-intro-outline.gif" alt="How to active the outline tool" loading="lazy">

# FAQ

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/faq.md

> Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio FAQ. Answers about pricing, licensing, setup, features, differences from Studio, and community support for the VS extension.

# FAQ

Here are answers to common questions about **Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio**.

## Is Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio free?

Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio is a paid product, but you can try all features **free for 15 days** during the trial period.

If you’re looking for a free option, check out [Radzen Blazor Studio](/blazor-studio).

## How much does Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio cost?

Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio is included in the following subscriptions:

- **Radzen Blazor Pro** - $799 per year for one developer seat
- **Radzen Blazor Team** - $1999 per year for three developer seats

You can use the same **license key** to activate both Radzen Blazor Studio and Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio.

For more details, see the [Pricing FAQ](/pricing#faq).

## I am an existing customer. Do I get Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio?

Yes. If you have an active subscription you already have access to Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio. Use the license code from your existing subscription to activate it.

## What’s the difference between Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio and Radzen Blazor Studio?

Here’s a quick comparison:

- **Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio** is a Visual Studio plugin.
  **Radzen Blazor Studio** is a standalone IDE.
- The Visual Studio extension works on **Windows only**.
  Radzen Blazor Studio also runs on **macOS and Linux**.
- The Visual Studio version doesn’t yet include all the features of the standalone app.
  You can check the [roadmap](/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/roadmap) for upcoming updates.

## What features do both products share?

Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio uses the same core engine as Radzen Blazor Studio.
That means both have identical **design-time features**, **code generation templates**, and evolve together as part of the same product family.

## Need more help?

If you have questions or run into issues, visit the [Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio forum](https://forum.radzen.com/c/radzen-blazor-visual-studio).

You can ask questions, read discussions, or get help directly from the Radzen team.

---

# Installation

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/install.md

> This article shows how to install Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio

# Installation

## Install

<YouTube Video="mkb6v2LVcek" />

> **Important**
> Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio requires the [.NET 10 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/10.0) and **Visual Studio 2022** or **Visual Studio 2026**.
> It does **not** support Visual Studio Code.

Follow these steps to install:

1. Open Visual Studio and go to **Extensions > Manage Extensions**.
2. In the **Browse** tab, search for **Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio**.
3. Click **Download**, then restart Visual Studio to complete the installation.
4. Open **Tools > Options**, then find the **Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio** section in the tree.
5. From there, you can either [start a trial](#trial) or enter your license code.

## Trial

You can start a free **15-day trial** from the **Options** page.

<img style="display: block" src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/register.png" alt="Trial registration dialog" loading="lazy">

1. Enter a valid email address.
   - Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio will send your activation code to that email.
   - Make sure your organization allows emails from **mailchimp.com** (our email provider).
2. Paste the activation code into the registration form to finish.

You’ll then have 15 days to explore all features.
When the trial ends, Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio will be disabled until you activate it with a valid license key.

> **Note**
> Each machine can only start one trial. You won’t receive a new activation code if you try again.
> If you need more time to evaluate, email **info@radzen.com**.

## Updates

You can update Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio directly from the **Extension Manager** in Visual Studio.

<img style="display: block" src="images/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/update.png" alt="Update Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio" loading="lazy">

## Uninstall

To uninstall or disable the extension, open the **Extension Manager** in Visual Studio and choose **Uninstall** or **Disable**.

> **Note**
> Restart Visual Studio after updating, uninstalling, or disabling the extension for changes to take effect.

# Manage Pages

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/pages.md

> Learn how to manage pages in your Blazor project

# Work with pages
## Create a page
1. Open a Blazor application or create a new one.
1. Right-click a folder in **Solution Explorer**.
1. Click the **Add > Radzen Blazor Studio...** context menu item. This will open the Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio template dialog.
1. Select **Page** from the available options and click **Next**.
1. Choose one of the available page template options and click **Next** to configure it.
1. Enter the required configuration options and click **Next**.

## Edit a page
To edit a page in the Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio designer just open the corresponding `.razor` file.

## Component Toolbox
To display the Radzen Blazor Toolbox click the **View > Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio > Toolbox** menu item.

# Troubleshooting

Source: https://www.radzen.com/blazor-visual-studio/documentation/troubleshooting.md

> Troubleshooting common issues with Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio.

# Troubleshooting
## Build error

Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio builds your application in order to show it in design time. Sometimes this special build fails and you will see a message in the designer
which asks you to check the Output window. The build could fail for two reasons:

1. Your application doesn't build in general in its current state. If your application fails to build in Visual Studio or from command line then it
won't build in Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio as well. Fix the reported errors and try again.
1. Your application builds and runs as expected but Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio fails with the design-time build. This usually happens when Radzen Blazor for Visu
didn't recognize some vital part of your application startup and didn't include it in the design-time build - some service registration for example. In other
cases it is some startup code that throws an exception during design-time build.

### Hide code from design-time builds

Use the `RADZEN` preprocessor constant if there is code you don't want Radzen Blazor Studio to include in design-time builds.

#### In C# files
```cs
#if !RADZEN
// This code will not be included in Radzen Blazor Studio design-time builds
builder.Services.AddScoped<ITradeService, TradeService>();
#endif

```

#### In razor files
```
@{ #if !RADZEN }
<RadzenButton Text="Hidden in design builds" />
@{ #endif }

```

### Failed to start Radzen.Server

If Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio fails to start the `Radzen.Server` process you will see an error message in the designer. This could happen if you don't have .NET 10 SDK installed on your machine.
Visual Studio 2026 comes with .NET 10 SDK but Visual Studio 2022 requires you to install it separately. To do so download and install it from the official [.NET download page](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/10.0).

### Preview and release candidate versions of .NET
Sometimes the design time build would fail with errors such as `CS0246: The type or namespace name 'App' could not be found`. This isually means that you have installed a preview or release candidate version
of the .NET framework which Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio does not support. Visual Studio Preview installs such .NET framework versions.

You can find the latest installed version by running `dotnet --info` in command prompt.

To solve this problem you have two options:

- Uninstall the preview version and install the [latest official version of .NET 10](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/download/dotnet/10.0). If it has been installed by a Visual Studio Preview you would need to uninstall the Preview itself and
get the [RTM version](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/vs).
- Create a [global.json](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/tools/global-json) file in the directory of your application with the following contents:

```json
{
  "sdk": {
    "version": "10.0.100"
  }
}
```

## Render error

Sometimes certain pages may fail to display.

Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio does not execute the Blazor lifecycle methods of your pages in order to prevent unwanted side effects such as database access,
HTTP requests or file system access. Instead it adds code that initializes the page members (properties and fields) with sample data. This process
could fail in some cases.

## Report an issue

If you hit a problem with Radzen Blazor Studio you can report it by:

- Starting a [forum thread](https://forum.radzen.com/c/radzen-blazor-visual-studio)
- Sending us an email to info@@radzen.com (only for users with an active subscription)

## CSS does not load in design time
Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio will scan the `_Host.cshtml`, `App.razor` or `index.html` files in your application for CSS and JS. It also supports component specific CSS files (`*.razor.css`).

If you are including a CSS file by other means they may not display in design-time.

## Code in lifecycle methods does not execute in design-time
Radzen Blazor for Visual Studio does not execute the Blazor lifecycle methods of your pages in order to prevent unwanted side effects such as database access,
HTTP requests or file system access. Instead it adds code that initializes the page members (properties and fields) with sample data.

---
